articleTitle: A 3-Order Multi-Level Complex Delta-Sigma Modulator For Switched-Mode Power Amplifier
abstract: Bitstream transmitter requires the RF input signal to become the pulse train which is typically utilized delta-sigma-like modulation. This paper proposes a modified 3-order complex delta-sigma modulation (CDSM) structure which contains a 3-level quantizer. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to optimize coefficients of the structure. Using the proposed CDSM technique reduces the quantization noise significantly at the output of the modulator. Various forms of signals are utilized to validate the proposed structure. For a Long-Term Evolution (LTE) signal with 20 MHz bandwidth and 10 dB peak-to-average power ratio, it achieves the adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) of 46.73dB. The comparison study between envelope DSM and the proposed CDSM shows 24.35dB improvement in ACLR of the LTE signal. The results for LTE signals are able to pass the spectral requirements defined by the standard without applying predistortion techniques. By comparing error vector magnitude (EVM) of output signals with different filter bandwidth, the proposed CDSM loosens the requirements for post-stage filters.

articleTitle: Injection-locked Frequency Divider Using an 8-shaped Transformer
abstract: Conventional harmonic mixer injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) uses spiral-shaped inductors as the ω resonator device. This designed case indicates a wide locking frequency range divider with a ratio of 3 N-core FET ILFD designed circuit with a new 8-shaped transformer. The proposed ILFD is based on a capacitive cross-coupled injection-locked oscillator (ILO) and was implemented in a commercial 0.18μm 1P6M CMOS process. At the drain-source bias of voltage is 1.2 V and the incident power of 0 dBm, the divide-by-three locking range is 3.6 GHz (48%), from the incident frequency of 5.7 GHz to 9.3 GHz. The core power consumption is 8.28 mW and the die chip area is 0.845×0.965 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The ILFD generates less magnetic fields for the coupling noise source and receives less coupling noise because the inductive components are made of two lobes generating opposite magnetic fields. The ILFD is an area-efficient circuit because it uses three inductors with a low coupling coefficient.

Author Keywords: injection-locked frequency divider with a division ratio of 3

articleTitle: Low Axial Ratio and High-precision Beamforming Circularly Polarized Phased Array
abstract: A circularly polarized phased array with a novel sequential rotation feed technique is proposed in this work, featuring superior properties of low axial ratio and high-precision beamforming simultaneously. To improve the axial ratio of the circularly polarized phased array, a multi-stage sequential rotation feed network is adopted. To further augment the performance of axial ratio and beamforming, a 90-180/180-90 combined sequential rotation feed network is proposed, with stable phase response versus frequency and high isolation at output ports. Moreover, transitions with coupling structure used in the phased array circumvent the complexity and cost of fabrication. For performance evaluation, the circularly polarized phased array is simulated. The feed network provides sequential rotation phase differences that are stable over the operating band. The phased array achieves a scanning range of ±40° with a low axial ratio. Considering both non-ideal factors of the feed network and radiation patterns of antenna elements, a PSO algorithm is used to synthesize a wide beam, demonstrating enhanced beamforming performance.

articleTitle: High Power Density Micro-System of MWPT Based on GaN HEMT
abstract: This paper presents a novel micro-system scheme for microwave power transmission that can achieve high power density at the receiver end. An inverse-F class harmonic-tuned power amplifier designed using GaN HEMT devices, as well as a rectifier incorporating an on-board coupler and phase shifter, have been realized. A significant issue is that the size of the device's peripheral on-board circuitry reduces the system's power density. By introducing a pair of aligned dual-polarized antennas, the on-board coupler and phase shifter can be designed at the transmitter end, which greatly reduces the size of the receiver end and enhances the system's power density.

articleTitle: Critical Distance for Orbital Angular Momentum Receiving Antenna Selection
abstract: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) wave reflected by the non-twisted parabolic antenna (PA) on the base station can be received by a uniform circular array (UCA) or a symmetrical PA. Both solutions have their pros and cons. When using symmetrical PA, the main beam of OAM cannot be covered, despite the improved antenna gain. And this trade-off is affected by the critical distance which finally determines whether PA or UCA can perform better in signal to interference and noise ratio and capacity. The attenuation, channel capacity and antenna size of receiving method using PA or UCA is analyzed and compared, by which the critical distance for OAM receiving antenna selection is obtained. Besides, the analysis about multiple-Input multiple-output system (MIMO) provides a reliable reference which corroborates the correctness of this method.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Multi-Octave Power Amplifier Using an Improved PSO Algorithm with Nonlinear Adaptive Hyper-Parameters
abstract: Due to the rapid development of modern wireless systems, higher performance requirements are imposed on PA, resulting in PA structures becoming more complex, making PA optimization extremely difficult. This paper presents an improved particle swarm optimization technique with nonlinear adaptive hyperparameters (PSO-NAH) for designing multi-octave PAs. A high-performance multi-octave PA with 10-W GaN HEMTs transistors has been designed and implemented to validate the proposed strategy. In comparison with the PSO algorithm with fixed hyperparameters (PSO-FH) and the PSO algorithm with linear adaptive hyperparameters (PSO-LAH), the proposed technique shows superior performance. As a result, the fabricated PA can achieve an output power exceeding 40.4 dBm, a drain efficiency greater than 60.1%, and a gain over 10.4 dB between 0.5 GHz and 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Circularly-Polarized Antenna Design in Mobile Phones by the Combination of Common and Differential Modes
abstract: To meet the coming era of direct satellite-to-handset communication, this paper proposes two design cases of single- fed end-fire circularly-polarized (CP) antennas in mobile phones based on the combination of common mode (CM) and differential mode (DM). By employing a slot-etched planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) or a slot-etched cavity antenna, a set of orthogonal-polarized modes, i.e., CM and DM, can be excited simultaneously by an asymmetrical feeding port. Then, by finely tuning the resonant frequency of the proposed orthogonal modes, a 90-degree phase shift between two modes can be realized, enabling a good CP performance in the end-fire direction. Simulation results show that a good left-hand CP directivity of 1.62 and 3.09 dBic can be realized for the CP PIFA and cavity antenna design cases, respectively. We predict that the proposed design can be a good candidate for the satellite communication antennas in mobile phones.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Multi-Sector UWB MIMO Antenna System
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized multi-sector ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system based on quasi-Yagi loop antennas is proposed. To realize multiple beams, the structural parameters of the loop antenna elements are carefully optimized to resonate at the 3.5λg mode (λg is the wavelength in free space at the center operating frequency). The antenna array consists of three horizontally po-larized elements and three vertically polarized elements. The horizontally polarized and vertically polarized impedance bandwidths of the MIMO antenna system are 2.15 GHz-3.81 GHz (55.70%) and 2.15 GHz-4.22 GHz (64.99%), respectively. The horizontally polarized and vertically polarized antennas have high front-to-back ratios (FBRs) of 15.06 dB and 19.87 dB, respectively. A prototype is fabricated and measured, the measured results are consistent with the simulated results, which proves the effectiveness of the design method.

articleTitle: Wideband Multibit Phase Shifter Based on SCRLH-TL
abstract: A phase shifter based on a simplified composite right/left-handed transmission-line (SCRLH-TL) is proposed. Compared with the conventional CRLH-TL, the SCRLH-TL is more convenient as it does not require the equilibrium condition. The phase shifter consists of a 50Ω main transmission line (MTL) loaded with P-I-N diode and lumped LC components. Principle of the unit design is presented, followed by the analysis and simulation of a 22.5° phase shifter. The achieved phase shift is accurate at the central frequency of 1.35 GHz with a ±1° phase error (PE) in a 37% fractional bandwidth. Furthermore, a 6-bit phase shifter is fabricated and measured, which can realize 360° phase shift. The rms PE is less than 8° across 1.2–1.5 GHz in measured results. The return loss is better than 10 dB, and insertion loss is less than 2 dB in all states. Good agreements are observed between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of High-Q Flexible RF Spiral Inductors on SiC/Parylene-C Substrate
abstract: In this paper, the fabrication process, radio frequency (RF) characteristics and lumped equivalent circuit model of the flexible spiral inductors on silicon carbon (SiC) / Parylene-C (PC) substrate are demonstrated. A flexible spiral inductor with a self-resonant frequency (SRF) of 7.9 GHz and Q value of 19.7 is achieved. Prominent improvement of Q factor is observed due to low-loss of parylene and thinned SiC. In order to avoid the difficulty of lithography caused by the deformable substrate, the inductors with Parylene-N (PN) as insulating layer are firstly fabricated on a rigid SiC substrate, and then SiC is thinned to 5μm from backside followed by depositing a 25-μm-thick PC. SiC layer with high thermal conductivity can improve the current tolerance level of inductors for design of high-power circuits. The equivalent circuit is also developed to characterize the high-frequency performance of fabricated inductors. These high-Q flexible RF spiral inductors and equivalent circuit would be helpful for design of high-efficiency and high-power flexible RF circuits and systems in the future.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Near-Field Imaging System with Frequency Diversity through Non-Periodic Leaky-Wave Antenna
abstract: In this paper, we present an innovative single-shot near-field imaging system utilizing non-periodic leaky wave antennas (LWA). This system stands out by offering a higher number of independent measurements compared to systems employing periodic LWAs. We incorporate compressed sensing coupled with wavelet transform techniques to to tackle the reconstruction problem. Through simulations, we demonstrate the system’s capability to precisely estimate the dimensions of scatterers by leveraging a mere 21 measurements over a 500 MHz frequency range within the10-10.5 GHz spectrum. These findings substantiate the effectiveness of our proposed model and methodology.

articleTitle: A 22~30GHz Active Phase Shifter for Radio Beamforming Systems In 65nm SOI CMOS
abstract: In this paper, an active phase shifter for radio beamforming systems in 65nm SOI CMOS is designed. The circuit uses quadrature all-pass filter (QAF) and gilbert stucture, and exploits 2-bit current compensating approache in digital control part to achieve an RMS gain error of 0.12~1 dB over 22~30 GHz. High-accuracy phase control with range of 360°is realized by a 7-bit DAC, the mesured RMS phase error is less than 3 ° over the operating band. The maximum output 1dB compression point is 6 dBm at 28.5 GHz for 0°phase state. The total power consumption of the phase shifter is 32 mW with a size of 0.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Antenna for Metal-Bezel Smartwatches with an Ultra-Compact Artificial Magnetic Conductor
abstract: A dual-band antenna with circular polarization (CP) in the GPS band and an ultra-compact artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) for metal-bezel smartwatches is proposed. The AMC structure is designed to provide phase reflection for GPS band, with the AMC's reflection phase tuned by four capacitors, resulting in an ultra-compact AMC, which is even smaller than the smartwatch antenna above it. The proposed AMC improves the dual-band antenna's front-to-back ratio (FBR), gain, and minimizes wrist effect, rendering the proposed AMC a viable option for implementation in commercial smartwatches.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Differential Coupler Based on the SISL Platform
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband differential coupler based on the substrate-integrated suspended Line (SISL) with multiple inner boards. It utilizes edge-coupled technology and multi-section asymmetry to achieve ultra-wideband and weak coupling. From 1 GHz to 16 GHz, i.e. a 176% fractional bandwidth, it demonstrates strong performance in both differential-mode and cross-mode. Furthermore, the proposed SISL differential coupler offers the benefits of self-packaging and low loss.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband DC to 67GHz Distributed Low-Noise Amplifier MMIC in 70-nm InP Technology
abstract: This paper presents the design of an ultrawideband distributed low-noise amplifier (LNA) MMIC utilizing 70nm InP technology, capable of operation from DC to 67GHz. To concurrently feature the bandwidth, gain, and dynamic range of the amplifier, a distributed topology with nine amplification stages, all employing a consistent cascode structure, is implemented in the amplifier MMIC design. By integrating an appropriate matching network between the common-gate transistor and the common-source transistor, along with a resistor-capacitor-to-ground structure parallel to the gate of the common-gate transistor, enhancements are made to the high-frequency response, gain compensation at high frequencies, and high-frequency stability of the amplifier. On-wafer measurements demonstrate a small-signal gain of 14dB across the DC to 67GHz frequency range, with an operating current of 53mA with a +3V drain voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>) and -0.4V gate voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>) supply. The input-output standing wave ratio (VSWR) is better than 1.7, and the 1dB compression output power is 4dBm. Furthermore, the noise figure in the DC to 53GHz range is measured typically at 4dB. The overall chip dimensions are 2.5mm × 1.7mm.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Front End Module in 0.15-μm GaN Technology for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
abstract: This paper introduces a high-frequency RF front-end circuit for fifth-generation (5G) millimeter-wave applications spanning 26-30 GHz. Employing 0.15-μm GaN technology, the design incorporates a two-stage low noise amplifier (LNA), a two-stage high-power amplifier (PA), and a single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch. The front end achieves optimal power efficiency and minimal noise loss by leveraging low insertion loss switching technology. The front-end module includes a peak transmitter output power of 31.2 dBm, 28% peak PAE, a gain exceeding 11 dB in the 26 GHz-30 GHz range, in-band gain of 11 dB, gain flatness of ±0.3 dB for the receiver, and a minimum noise figure of 4.1 dB at 27.65 GHz. The compact chip, measuring 2.8 × 1.7mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, underscores the circuit’s efficiency, power, and performance in millimeter-wave 5G applications.

articleTitle: 24GHz FMCW Radar Based Lightweight Real-time Hand Gesture Recognition System
abstract: In this paper, we propose a lightweight real-time gesture recognition system based on hand trajectory caught by 24GHz FMCW radar. To catch a reliable hand trajectory, we employ a computationally efficient local interpolation method to achieve super-precision positioning of the hand. Combined with lightweight neural networks for gesture capture and classification, high accuracy is achieved with minimal computational and resource consumption. After data augmentation for training, validation accuracy for 10 gestures can reach 97.5%, with the entire parameter size of only 0.02MB. The entire process from receiving raw radar data to outputting gesture recognition results takes only 6ms on a low-cost Microcontroller Unit.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss Millimeter-Wave SISL Wilkinson Power Divider
abstract: A low-loss millimeter-wave Wilkinson power divider based on the substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) platform is proposed. By utilizing unequal-height cavities and the suspended coplanar waveguide (SCPW) structure, a reasonable layout and small size are obtained. Besides, the double metal layers with side-wall copper connection and substrate patterned SISL are employed to achieve low insertion loss. A new method to package and test the inside SISL circuit using mechanical housing and glass-beads is presented. The SISL power divider is fabricated, and the measured results agree well with the simulated results. From 15 GHz to 50 GHz, i.e. a bandwidth of 107.7%, the measured return loss is better than 13.1 dB and the isolation is greater than 14 dB. The measured phase imbalance is less than 1° from 15 GHz to 32 GHz, and the measured insertion loss is smaller than 0.3 dB from 17.1 GHz to 25.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Parameter and State Estimation with Extended Kalman Filter for Dynamic Parameters
abstract: Simultaneous Parameter and State Estimation with Extended Kalman Filter (SPSE-EKF) is proposed, which integrates both state and parameter information using an extended state vector. Leveraging the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) framework, SPSE-EKF achieves joint estimation of parameters and states, enhancing accuracy and robustness. This integration allows for a more comprehensive representation of the dynamic system, making it suitable for real-world scenarios with uncertainties. We conduct a simulation experiment to simulate radar target tracking as the application scenario. The results demonstrate SPSE-EKF’s ability to accurately estimate system parameters while providing stable state estimates.

articleTitle: Design of a Balanced Bandpass Filter with Ultra-Wide DM Upper Stop-band and Compact Size Based on Semi-Circular Patch Resonator
abstract: A new balanced filter with ultra-wide differential-mode (DM) upper stopband and high common-mode (CM) suppression is designed on the basis of two back-to-back microstrip semi-circular patch resonators. To suppress high-order modes of the patch resonators, four metalized via holes are adopted to vertically feed two patches in differential pairs. By virtue of a slotline etched in the common ground plane, desired coupling strength for TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode can be achieved to attain a target bandwidth. According to the guidance of filter synthesis theory, a balanced filter prototype centered at 2.46 GHz with 3-dB a fractional bandwidth of 10% is designed and simulated. Results indicate that the proposed balanced filter exhibits nice DM filtering responses with a 20-dB harmonic suppression up to 7.2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> as well as a compact size about 0.32λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>×0.56λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Radar Indoor Human Target Loss Judgment
abstract: Radar struggles to detect stationary targets due to clutter interference. In indoor applications, the transition of a person from an active to a stationary state can result in target loss. This is difficult to distinguish from target loss caused by a person leaving the room. This paper proposes a machine learning-based method that leverages transient Doppler information before target loss for fast and accurate judgment. Two types of neural networks are experimented, and triggering mechanism are used to reduce the consumption of computational resources. Results on the collected dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Wideband Beamforming Method Based on Neural Network in Multi-Interference Scenarios
abstract: Multiple interference suppression is an important research topic in the field of wideband beamforming. Traditional approaches address this problem utilizing optimization algorithms, which usually require an adequate number of signal snapshots to ensure optimal performance. In this paper, we propose a multi-interference suppression beamforming method based on the neural network, namely, multi-interference suppression neural network (MISN), which transforms the wideband beamforming problem under multi-interference into the mapping relationship between input and output. The MISN achieves performance close to traditional algorithms although signal snapshots are inadequate. Simulation results of output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios (SINRs) and beam patterns demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Single-Gm Dual-Core Transformer-Based Cryogenic VCO for Quantum Computing Application
abstract: In this paper, a single-G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> dual-core (SGDC) transform-based cryogenic voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) at mil-limeter-wave (mm-wave) frequency is proposed for quantum computing applications. By utilizing only half of the traditional cross-coupled VCO’s transistors, both power and phase noise (PN) reductions are concurrently achieved. In addition, a symmetric transformer with a high coupling coefficient is implemented to achieve dual-core coupling and reduce PN while maintaining a constant figure of merit (FoM) and compact area. The FoM improvement of 5 dB is attained. The proposed SGDC-VCO is fabricated in 55-nm CMOS process, which can be tuned from 26.5 to 33 GHz. At 1-MHz/10-MHz offset, the SGDC-VCO achieves a PN of -101.7/-127.2 dBc/Hz at 29.4 GHz while consuming a power of 2.8 mW from a 0.6-V supply voltage under very low temperature of 6 K.

articleTitle: A 480-µW Ultra-Low-Power OOK Transmitter with 24-Phase Passive Polyphase Filter Achieving 12× Frequency Multiplication at 25Mbps for Biomedical Application
abstract: A high frequency multiplication 407-425 MHz ultra-low-power (ULP) OOK wireless transmitter (TX) is presented, which uses 24-phase Passive Polyphase Filter (PPF) and Fast-Switched Edge Combiner Power Amplifier (FS-ECPA). This is the first TX with 24-phase PPF using pole splitting technique to generate robust multiphase signals for 12× frequency multiplication. It also can reduce the overall power consumption of the TX, as the circuit before FS-ECPA operates at the extreme low frequencies. To increase the modulated data rate, a FS-ECPA is proposed to fast switching the on/off states. The TX is designed in 55nm CMOS process with 480µW power consumption under 1V supply voltage, and the active area is 0.23 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The post-layout simulated output power is -9.7dBm with 25Mbps OOK data rate. The TX also achieves a global efficiency of 22.6% and a figure-of-merit (FoM) of 0.18 nJ/(bit*mW) respectively.

articleTitle: A Design of Planar Reflective Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion Pattern Manipulation Surfaces with Enhanced Axial Ratio Bandwidth
abstract: In this article, a planar linear-to-circular polarization conversion pattern manipulation surfaces (LCPC-PMS) is designed. Firstly, the application and the structure is studied. Secondly, the patch element with variable microstrip length is analyzed, and the working condition is obtained based on equivalent circuit model. Then, the performance of the element is evaluated by calculation. To broaden the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth, fil- tenna design method is introduced to bring in extra minima. The 3dB AR bandwidth is thus broadened to larger than 3% in measurement. Finally, to verify our design concept, based on phased array theory, three prototypes are designed, fabricated, and measured. The three prototypes successfully steer the incident LP wave to the desired direction with circular polarization. The proposed linear-to-circular polarization conversion pattern manipulation surfaces is a promising candidate for 6G networks.

articleTitle: A W-Band On-Chip Slot Antenna With Multilayer PCB (Printed Circuit Board) for Gain Enhancement in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: In this paper, a W-band on-chip antenna with backside radiation is proposed. The multilayer PCB (printed circuit board) is utilized as the supporter and simultaneously the director for the on-chip slot antenna in SiGe BiCMOS, thus boosting the backside gain. Then, a transition from the on-chip antenna to the WR-10 waveguide is introduced for measurement, which consists of the bonding wires, a GCPW (grounded coplanar waveguide) and an SIW (substrate integrated waveguide) and a cavity-backed patch antenna. The proposed antenna shows the 3.5-5.8 dBi gain from 92 to 98.5 GHz, with higher than 50 % efficiency.

articleTitle: A 6.5–8.1GHz Temperature-Compensated LC-VCO
abstract: A temperature-compensation scheme is presented for LC-VCO. With a proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) voltage and a complementary-to-absolute-temperature (CTAT) voltage incorporated for frequency regulation, and the frequency drift due to temperature variations is compensated. For demonstration, a VCO prototype is fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS. Experimental results show that up to 66% frequency drift can be eliminated, while the tuning range measures from 6.54GHz to 8.12GHz, with phase noise (PN) of –141.8 dBc/Hz and figure of merit (FoM) of 186.8 dBc/Hz at 10MHz frequency offset.

articleTitle: A Ku-band TR Front-end Multifunctional GaN MMIC
abstract: A 15-17GHz fully-integrated transmit/receive (TR) multifunctional monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) is designed, realized and measured in this paper. Based on a 0.1um gallium nitride (GaN) process on Si substrate, this MMIC integrates a power amplifier, a low noise amplifier and a double pole double throw (DPDT), which is used as the transmit (TX)-receive (Rx) switch. In Tx mode, a flat linear gain level higher than 27 dB with a 37.5 dBm output power is achieved across a wide frequency range. In Rx mode, two output ports demonstrate uniform performance with a linear gain of 26 dB and a noise figure of 3.2 dB. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this work reports the first 15 to 17 GHz T/R MMIC FEM who achieves about 5 W output power and lower than 3.2 dB noise factor.

articleTitle: A Single-Pole-Double-Throw Switch For Millimeter-Wave Mobile Communication Using Gallium Nitride Technology
abstract: In this paper, a capacitor-loaded and port-loaded semiconductor radio frequency single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch is designed and fabricated by using the 100-nm silicon-based gallium nitride (GaN on Si) process. The proposed switch differs from the traditional scheme of using λ/4 transmission lines to eliminate the mutual interference between the two switch arms. Instead, the proposed switch utilizes the loading effect of the open switch arm and the increased short-circuit capacitor to form a resonant circuit, which generates an extra transmission pole. A FET on-chip resonator is introduced into the switch design on each branch. The switch designed in this paper has one more transmission pole than the traditional scheme in the millimeter wave band. It performs excellently, with a measured peak insertion loss (IL) of only 0.72 dB, an isolation (ISO) of more than 20 dB, a relative bandwidth of 67.4%, and a chip area of only 0.80 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed switch in this work has significant advantages in insertion loss, bandwidth extension, and miniaturization.

articleTitle: Bifunctional Gutman-Eaton Lens Antenna with Near-Surface Flat-Feed and Wide-Angle Beam-Scanning
abstract: This work introduces a bifunctional Gutman-Eaton lens antenna incorporating the characteristics of the Gutman lens and Eaton lens. By extracting the dielectric constant distribution formulas of Gutman and Eaton lenses, a novel spherical gradient refractive index lens antenna is devised, featuring the near-surface focus of the Gutman lens and the wide-angle beam-scanning of the Eaton lens. Simulation results reveal that the proposed composite lens antenna, excited through a WR-51 rectangular waveguide, achieves a gain enhancement of 5.99 dB at 18 GHz. The antenna demonstrates a wide-angle beam scanning of up to ±98° with a gain variation of ≤0.5 dB. Compared to the traditional Gutman lens antenna, the beam-scanning range is greatly improved.

articleTitle: A Loaded Tapered Slot Antenna Featuring Stable Wide-Beamwith in Wide Band
abstract: A novel method for minimizing the structure and enhancing the beamwidth of linearly tapered slot antenna (LTSA) is presented. In the proposed design, the basic microstrip-fed LTSA is loaded with a joint action structure (JAS) including dual L-shaped gaps and ABS-metal bonding cavity. Compared to the basic unloaded version, the proposed antenna exhibits improved impedance characteristic in the lower band. Additionally, broad beams in principal planes, high front-to-back (F/B) ratio, and improved gain are also obtained. Simulation results reveal that the proposed antenna with 23.5×23.5mm, provides an impedance bandwidth from 4.15~11.25GHz, while a pattern bandwidth of 62%, more than 116° E- and H-plane 3-dB beamwidths and over 18.0dB F/B ratio are also achieved.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized MIMO Antenna with Polarization Converter for Reduction of RCS and Mutual Coupling
abstract: This article proposes a miniaturized multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for reducing mutual coupling and radar cross section (RCS). The miniaturized antenna is composed of two radiation elements and two polarization converter (PC) cells. The PC cells are arranged between two radiation elements to realize RCS reduction and mutual coupling reduction simultaneously. The area size of the antenna is 0.69λ×0.37λ (λ is corresponding to the minimum cut-off frequency in open space). The proposed antenna operates at 7.4-8.9 GHz. Compared to reference MIMO antenna without PC cells, it can achieve maximum RCS reduction value of 6.4 dB and a maximum isolation amplitude of 27.8 dB. And the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) value is given to indicate its excellent performance. The MIMO antenna with the characteristics of miniaturization, low mutual coupling and RCS reduction shows great potential in military applications.

articleTitle: Design of a miniaturized dual-band implantable patch antenna for cows
abstract: A miniaturized dual-band implantable patch antenna for cows is designed. Its size is 9.4mm×9.3mm×0.635mm. The dual-band miniaturization is realized by opening a curved manifold slot on the radiation patch. And the impedance matching is improved by adding two orthogonal rectangular slots in the middle of the GND. Three layers of tissue model of cows have been established. The designed antenna has been implanted into cow tissue models with different health conditions. In order to further validate the design, a prototype is fabricated and measured. The antenna operating frequency bands are from 0.85 to 0.94 GHz and from 2.37 to 2.57 GHz, covering the ISM 0.9 and 2.45 GHz bands very well. The radiation pattern of the antenna is similar to that of the dipole antenna, and its H-plane has quasi-omnidirectional radiation characteristics. The maximum power allowed by the specific absorption rate safety standard is 3.9 mW at 0.9 GHz, and 7.1 mW at 2.48 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: An On-chip 28/39 GHz Millimeter-wave Diplexer For 5G Dual-band Front End Modules
abstract: In this paper, a compact millimeter-wave on-chip diplexer with low loss is designed based on lumped-distributed elements. The quasi-lumped resonator consists of interdigital capacitors and inductive transmission lines with compact dimensions. The introduction of distributed electromagnetic hybrid coupling between the quasi-lumped resonators can generate two transmission zeros (TZs) on both sides of the filter passband respectively. In addition to the good isolation of the diplexer designed by connecting two different band filters with T-junctions, the isolation of the diplexer can be further enhanced by the upper stopband transmission zero of the low-frequency filter and the lower stopband transmission zero of the high-frequency filter. Finally, the simulation results of the proposed on-chip diplexer with center frequencies of 28 and 39 GHz, respectively, show that they have good performances such as low insertion loss and high selectivity.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Compact Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna
abstract: A novel millimeter-wave compact pattern reconfigurable antenna is proposed in this paper. An endfire magnetoelectric (ME) dipole and two slot-patches are employed as sub radiators of the antenna. By adjusting the impedance characteristics of the sub radiation structures using PIN diodes, three reconfigurable radiation modes including endfire, forward broadside (broadside 1), and backward broadside (broadside 2) are obtained, which achieves large spatial coverage. In addition, by utilizing the virtual short circuit and polarization orthogonal characteristics of the antenna, the DC bias circuit does not require the design of additional choke structures, making the antenna has a compact and simple structure.

articleTitle: Threshold Optimized CSWPL Behavioral Model for RF Power Transistors Based on Cuckoo Search Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, the cuckoo search algorithm (CS) is used to optimize the threshold of the canonical section-wise piecewise linear (CSWPL) behavioral model of power transistors. An evaluation of the effectiveness of the proposed modeling method was carried out using Wolfspeed's 10-W GaN power transistors. In comparison to the existing particle swarm optimization (PSO) method, this method provides better prediction performance and is more efficient in finding the optimal threshold as well.

articleTitle: Beam-Adaptive DPD Based on Neural Network for Fully-Connected Hybrid Beamforming MIMO System
abstract: This paper proposes a beam-adaptive neural-network (NN) based digital predistortion (DPD) technique for full-connected hybrid beamforming (FC-HBF) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmitters. When the beam steering directions vary, the proposed DPD can automatically adjust the NN’s inputs using the embedded fine-tuning network, which enables adaptive and accurate compensation for the beam signals. Experimental measurement is carried out on a 2×32 quasi-test platform to validate the effectiveness of the proposed DPD technique, the verification results show that the proposed model achieves over 10-dB NMSE and 7-dB ACPR improvements.

articleTitle: A Method of Antenna Tuner’s Coff Compensation for 5G Smartphone Antenna Tuning
abstract: In this paper, a new method of antenna tuner’s Coff compensation in high frequency inductive antenna tuning for 5G smartphone is proposed. This method comprehensively utilizes the series resonance impedance of Coff and tuning inductor on OFF throw and the tuning impedance on ON throw to achieve the designed total impedance. The method is verified on an antenna designed in working at n78 and n79. The measurements of the tuned antenna with tuner have a good agreement with the reference antenna without tuner in both of the reflection coefficients and the radiation efficiencies.

articleTitle: Novel Rectangular Waveguide Band-Stop Filters with PMC MSSs in the Broad Wall
abstract: A novel waveguide band-stop filter is developed and presented. This design incorporates the integration of one or two metasurface sections onto the broad wall, effectively yielding a robust stopband characteristic within a broad passband. The underlying mechanism responsible for generating the stopband is elucidated. Simulation results demonstrate a good stopband within the wide TE10 passband of the standard rectangular waveguide WR-75. This proposed filter exhibits advantages of a straightforward structure, simplified design process, ease of fabrication, convenient mounting, and superior bandstop performance.

articleTitle: Validation and Analysis of the ITU-R P.684 Method in Medium to Long Distances Situations
abstract: To validate the usability and reliability of the ITU-R P.684 method in middle to long-distances, this paper conducts a comprehensive analysis in both the time and space domains. The analysis compares the prediction results of the ITU-R P.684 method with actual measurements within 4000 km and the prediction results of empirical models. It is found that compared with the empirical model, the overall prediction accuracy of the ITU-R P.684 method has improved by about 3.66%. The results of this validation analysis underscore the practical utility of the ITU-R P.684 method in medium to long-distances.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Broadband Metasurface Antenna Using a Novel Nonuniform Prismatic Patches
abstract: A low-profile, broadband, miniaturized metasurface antenna (MSA) based on characteristic mode analysis is proposed. The proposed MSA consists of an array of nonuniform prismatic patches, a slotted ground plane and a T-shaped feeding network. Two modes with different resonance frequency and the broadside radiation patterns are introduced by the MS and the slotted ground plane, which can be excited simultaneously by the T-shaped feeding network. Thus, miniaturization and broadband can be obtained accordingly. For demonstration, a miniaturized wideband MAS protype is fabricated and measured, achieving a large impedance bandwidth of 32.6% and a peak gain of 8.45 dBi with a compact overall size of 0.36λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf> × 0.36λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf> × 0.037λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf> is the lower operating wavelength in free space) and an overall efficiency higher than 88% is achieved. The proposed design possesses the merits of large bandwidth, low-profile, compact size and along with low cost and easy fabrication, which is appealing to a variety of space-limited, wideband wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Reconfigurable Reflectarray and Transmitarray at X-Band for Beam Steering Application
abstract: A special unit cell that can switch between reflection and transmission modes is proposed in this work. By adjusting the states of the PIN diodes loaded on the unit cell, the 1-bit phase resolution in two modes can be generated. The array that constitutes the elements can be reconfigured as a reflectarray or a transmitarray, which can steer beams at different angles on both sides of the array, offering a wider beam coverage than a single reflectarray or transmitarray.

articleTitle: An Asymmetric Pulsed Load Modulation (PLM) Power Amplifier for Power Back-off Efficiency Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents an asymmetric wideband pulsed load modulation (PLM) power amplifier (PA) with post-matching structure. By providing asymmetry PLM PA with different optimal load impedance, the main PA can reach saturation in advance. The auxiliary PA outputs more power, when two PAs are saturated. This enlarges the power back-off range. An asymmetric wideband PLM PA based on GaN HEMT transistor has been designed and fabricated. Measured result of the proposed PLM PA shows 9 dB output power back-off range at 3.15 GHz with efficiency in excess of 43%. At the same time, the proposed PLM PA can achieve high efficiency amplification from 2.8GHz to 3.3GHz.

articleTitle: A 4-to-8GHz Multi-Phase Injection-Locked Quadrature Clock Generator in 65nm CMOS
abstract: We present a low-power, low-jitter, high-accuracy quadrature clock generator (QCG) based on a multi-phase injection-locked ring oscillator (ILRO) with a passive polyphase filter (PPF) and a quadrature locked loop (QLL). The passive PPF generates a coarse quadrature clock as multi-phase injection signals to the ILRO, the QLL minimizes the quadrature phase error by tuning the self-oscillation frequency of the ring oscillator to align the injection signals. Prototyped in 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed QCG achieves a frequency locking range from 4 to 8GHz, a quadrature phase error less than 0.8°, and an integrated jitter less than 181fs, while consuming 5.7mW at 8GHz, yielding a figure-of-merit (FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">jitter</inf>) of -247.3dB.

articleTitle: Cryogenic MEMS SAW Frequency Reference for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance cryogenic 433 MHz micro-electrical mechanical system (MEMS) surface acoustic wave (SAW) oscillator, which can be employed as a frequency reference for quantum computing interface circuits. Using a commercial MEMS SAW resonator and low-noise amplifier, a driving circuit with a π-type phase shifter was implemented and measured at 4K temperature. The cryogenic MEMS oscillator works well at 4K temperature with a frequency of 433.47 MHz and an amplitude of 18.63 dBm. The measured cryogenic phase noise of the MEMS oscillator is -153 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz offset. The power consumption is 45 mA under a supply of 5 V.

articleTitle: A 0.5~22.4 GHz Ultra-Wideband LNA Using Pole Staggering Bandwidth Extension Technology in 0.18 μm BiCMOS
abstract: A fully integrated two-stages cascode ultra-wideband (UWB) low noise amplifier (LNA) for 0.5-22.4 GHz application in 0.18-μm silicon germanium (SiGe) technology is presented in this paper. The pole staggering technology is adopted to expand the operation bandwidth with multiple technologies of collectively mitigating the gain roll-off of LNA. The proposed LNA achieves a simulated gain of 26.5 dB with less than 0.5 dB in-band fluctuation from S-band to Ku-band. The noise figure (NF) varies from 1.5 dB to 2.7 dB within the 3-dB bandwidth. Moreover, the chip occupies a silicon area of 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including all pads.

articleTitle: The Cross Media Transmission Analysis and Experiment of the Spinning Magnet as a Mechanical Antenna
abstract: The equivalence of the field between the spinning magnet and the orthogonal current loops is established using the magnetic dipole moment. Compared with the traditional orthogonal current loops, the radiation efficiency of the spinning magnet is increased by five orders of magnitudes below 100 Hz. The spinning magnet with the residual magnetization of 1.4 T is used as a mechanical transmitting antenna. The magnetic flux density at the near-field zone is computed considering the half space model of sea-to-air. The field component along the interface across sea and air contributes to the slower decay of the underwater magnetic flux density along the distance. Compared with the rapid decay in the infinite space filled with sea water, this field component across the interface between the sea and the air is beneficial to underwater communication. The magnetic flux density of the prototype will reach 128 fT at 1000 m according to the measured result of 128 pT at 100 m.

articleTitle: A New Five-layer Differential Magnetic-Field Probe With High Sensitivity
abstract: This work introduces a novel differential magnetic-field probe that incorporates parasitic elements. The probe features a pair of shorted differential loops as the parasitic components, which significantly boost detection sensitivity due to the expanded detection area. The construction of the proposed probe includes a U-shaped loop with dual outputs serving as the primary element, supplemented by a pair of shorted differential loops acting as parasitic elements, a set of shorted vias, a set of connected vias, and numerous shielded vias. First, the usual single-loop probe is applied to measure the electric and magnetic field components at the same time. Subsequently, a pair of shorted loops are integrated into the differential single-loop probe to function as parasitic elements, thereby increasing the reception of magnetic flux. To demonstrate the design rationality, the correspondingly simulated results are given in this work. Ultimately, the probe with integrated parasitic elements is crafted, printed, and assessed. The simulation results indicate that the developed probe exhibits high detection sensitivity.

articleTitle: Novel Optimization Designing Method for Multilayer Broadband Absorber with Frequency-Domain Continuity
abstract: This work presents one novel method for designing ultra-wideband multi-layer microwave absorbers, which is based on an improved optimization algorithm with frequency-domain continuity. First, Beta distribution function is used to imitate the characteristics of electromagnetic parameters of actual materials varying with the frequency. Second, Beta distribution function is incorporated into the genetic algorithm, and a broadband design method based on the multi-layer absorber model is proposed. After that, the result of the optimization method is input into the simulation software for verification. The optimization result is consistent with the simulation result, which validates the effectiveness of the optimization method and provides valuable guidance for the design of multi-layer broadband absorber.

articleTitle: A D-band Frequency Quadrupler with 8.5dB Conversion Gain in 250 nm InP DHBT
abstract: This work presents a new-designed D-band multiplier with high conversion gain designed in 250 nm indium phosphide (InP) double heterojunction bipolar transistor (DHBT) technology. The quadrupler consists of two frequency doublers and a 2-stage common-emitter amplifier, with the embedded harmonic rejection module to suppress the useless signals. As shown in the post-simulation results, the proposed frequency quadrupler achieves a high conversion gain of 8.5 dB at 140 GHz. At a total DC power consumption of 51.1 mW, the output power saturates at 6.4 dBm. The operation frequency occupies a relatively wide bandwidth of 3-dB gain ranging from 124 to 156 GHz (BW3dB = 32 GHz) and a 5-dB gain bandwidth from 116 to 158 GHz (BW5dB = 42 GHz). The design also achieves good harmonic rejection ratios and a power efficiency of 8.37%.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Accurate Beamforming Based on Sparse Antenna Array
abstract: The conventional beamforming methods mainly focus on optimizing array factors to fulfill the targeted requirements. It suffers from the limitations of neglecting both the array-element radiation pattern and the mutual coupling in a practical antenna array. In this paper, an iterative synthesis method is introduced for the accurate beamforming of a practical antenna array, and two key techniques are discussed to overcome the limitations. Both the array-element radiation pattern and the mutual coupling are taken into account during the synthesis, contributing to accurate beamforming. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, two antenna arrays are experimentally exemplified: a 1×10 sparse patch array with flat-topped beam, and a 1×20 patch array with cosecant-squared beam. Good agreements are achieved between the measured and targeted radiation patterns. The proposed method is promising for beamforming of large-scale antenna arrays.

articleTitle: A QMSIW Bandpass Filter With DMS Fed
abstract: In this paper, a bandpass filter with defected microstrip structure(DMS) is designed based on quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide(QMSIW). Transmission zeros are achieved on both sides of the passband by using the cross-coupling introduced by the higher modes of TE102 and TE201 in the QMSIW, and suppression of parasitic passbands is achieved by defected microstrip structure. The filter is designed on a 0.254mm single-layer TLY-5 dielectric substrate, and the measured results show that the center frequency is 25.5GHz, the passband is 24.75-26.3GHz, the in-band insertion loss is less than 3.0dB, the in-band return loss is more than 12.5dB, and the rejection is more than 20dB at 27.7-35GHz.

articleTitle: A Wideband MIMO Antenna With Shared Radiator For 5G Smartphones
abstract: A novel metal frame MIMO (multiple-input, multiple-output) antenna with broadband performances has been designed for 5G smartphones. The antenna pair had a common radiator with an L-shaped open slot and a shorting stub in the center of the radiator. The bandwidth was improved with the open slot, and the isolation was improved by decoupling with the shorting stub. The 8 × 8 MIMO array has a bandwidth of 3.2 to 5.9 GHz, covering the 5G NR band n77/n78/n79 and the WLAN 5 GHz band, while the isolation was below than -10 dB and the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) was below than 0.05 in the band. Finally, an antenna prototype was manufactured and the measurement results were in excellent accordance with the design results.

articleTitle: AI-Based RF-Input RF-Output Digital Predistortion Architecture for the Linearization of RF Power Amplifiers
abstract: In this paper, we propose an AI-based RF-input RF-output digital predistortion (AI-RIRO DPD) system that incorporates the strengths of both digital predistortion (DPD) and analog predistortion (APD) techniques, which is well-suited for scenarios where deploying a baseband DPD technique is unfeasible due to various constraints. The proposed hardware-friendly polyphase real-valued time-delay neural network (PRVTDNN) model is capable of linearizing multiple samples per clock cycle while avoiding the need for resource replication. The system prototype is demonstrated in FPGA with 983.04 MHz baseband sampling rates. Experiment results show a 14.47 dBc ACPR reduction for 40 MHz 5G-NR signal with a 3.5 GHz GaN power amplifier using the proposed model and hardware implementation.

articleTitle: A Synthesis Method for All-Resonator Diplexer with Contiguous Channels Based on Gaussian Cauchy Differential Evolution - LM Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a synthesis method for the diplexers with contiguous channels based on a hybrid algorithm. For the diplexer with contiguous channels, additional coupling between the two channels is added into the all-resonator diplexer, thus achieving significant isolation. Furthermore, all-resonator diplexer topology cannot be synthesized with the conventional analytical method, a synthesis framework that integrates Gaussian Cauchy differential evolution (GCDE) method and Levenberg Marquardt algorithm is presented. Here, GCDE is used to implement the global search to avoid local minimums, while LM can accelerate the convergence. Compared with the traditional synthesis algorithms, the proposed synthesis approach is more general.

Author Keywords: Gaussian Cauchy differential evolution - Levenberg Marquardt algorithm (GCDE-LM)

articleTitle: Enhanced Micrometer-Scale Motion Sensing Using a Reconfigurable Virtual CW Algorithm Based on 60 GHz FMCW Radar
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar is widely used in motion sensing. However, when the motion’s amplitude is smaller than the deep sub-wavelength, it fails due to the short I/Q trajectory. In this paper, a novel reconfigurable virtual continuous-wave algorithm (RVCWA) is proposed to enhance radar's capability in perceiving micrometer-scale motion. The frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar can be represented as multiple CW radars with different frequencies, and then the multiplication of several single-tone signals is reconfigured as a higher-frequency CW signal, which is more sensitive to micromotion. Experiments were conducted to validate the superiority of the algorithm. The mechanical vibration experiment demonstrates that the algorithm can recover sinusoidal motion with 10 μm (1/500 λ@60 GHz) amplitude, yielding a root mean square error of only 3.55%, an improvement of 2.3 times compared to the traditional algorithm. A cardiac motion monitoring experiment is also used to validate the algorithm for biomedical application.

Index Terms: GHz Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Radar

articleTitle: A GaN-Based Rectifier with Ultra-High Efficiency and Power Bandwidth
abstract: In this paper, a 2.4-GHz GaN rectifier with ultra-high efficiency and ultra-wide input power range is proposed for wireless power transmission. Firstly, an equivalent current model is proposed for accurately analyzing the power losses resulting from gallium nitride Schottky barrier (SBD) diodes. Based on the model, a custom GaN Schottky barrier diode is designed and manufactured. The series resistance and junction capacitance of the diode are decreased to 2.6 Ω and 0.47 pF, respectively, while the breakdown voltage is increased to 54 V. Then a wideband microwave rectifier is fabricated with harmonic harvesting and impedance compression technology. The test results shows that a maximum rectification efficiency of 90% at 25.2 dBm input power is achieved of the proposed rectifier. While the high-efficiency power range (efficiency ≥ 50%) is extended to 23.5dB (3.5-27dBm). The proposed GaN-based rectifier offers significant benefits for enhancing the working distance and anti-interference capabilities of wireless power transmission systems.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network based Stable Digital Predistortion using ELU Activation for Switchless Class-G Power Amplifier
abstract: In this paper, a deep neural network (DNN) based digital pre-distortion (DPD) technique is proposed. It utilizes the exponential linear unit function instead of the sigmoid one to activate the hidden layer neurons, consequently mitigating the gradient vanishing problem and accelerating the DNN training. For validation, its linearization effects on a SLCG PA that is excited by a 256QAM signal with various modulation bandwidths (swept from 20MHz to 200MHz) are carefully compared with other existing DPD algorithms. This comparison reveals that, when applied under the signal with a modulation bandwidth of 200MHz, the proposed DPD method can further reduce the adjacent channel power ratio and the normalized mean square error of the PA output signal by 4-8.4dB and 1.3-4.3dB, compared to other polynomial/NN-based DPD methods. This demonstrates the superiority of the proposed technique in linearizing the nonlinear SLCG PA under wideband modulated signal excitations.

articleTitle: An E-band ×6 Multiplier With 7.9 dBm Peak Output Power and > 20 dBc Harmonics Rejection in 0.1 μm GaAs pHEMT Technology
abstract: This paper presents a 60-90 GHz (E-band) ×6 multiplier with a minimum of 40 dBc 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics rejection, 20 dBc 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic rejection, and a peak saturated output power of 7.9 dBm. The ×6 multiplier comprises a 20-30 GHz frequency doubler, driver amplifiers, and an E-band frequency tripler. The input adopts a push-push architecture-based doubler, effectively ensuring the odd-order harmonics suppression. The output is a tripler based on antiparallel diodes pair (APDP) topology that includes a pair of power enhancement T-lines, effectively improving output impedance and power of the chain. To effectively expand the bandwidth of the frequency multiplier chain, driver amplifiers integrated with an RC negative feedback network are inserted. Furthermore, to further bolster harmonics rejection performance, a compact filter is integrated.

articleTitle: A System and Method for On-wafer RF Power Measurement Based on Calorimetric Chips
abstract: A direct on-wafer RF power measurement system and method based on the calorimetric chip is proposed in this paper to meet the need for precise on-wafer RF measurement. This approach enables direct measurement of RF power at the tip of the RF probe without the need to correct for the insertion losses associated with the transmission line and RF probe. The methodologies, measurement process, and system configuration of this approach are discussed in the paper. Experimental results demonstrate the consistency of this method with traditional insertion loss correction methods within the 1-5 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: 3D Rotation-driven Reconfigurable Holography via Bilayer Spatially Cascaded Metasurfaces
abstract: Metasurface-based three-dimensional (3D) reconfigurable vectorial holography is regarded as a remarkable platform for large-capacity information storage, imaging devices, and encryption, which not only manipulates the complex amplitude of the holograms but also at-will tailors its polarization in the 3D space. However, designing economical and convenient 3D reconfigurable vectorial holography is still a great challenge. Here, we propose a rotation-driven reconfigurable holographic scheme via spatially cascaded phase-only metasurface (PM) and birefringent metasurface (BM), which can achieve reconfigurable vectorial holography in the 3D space. The PM is located on the front side of the BM, which serves to control the state of wavefront incident on the BM by rotation. Moreover, an inverse design algorithm is proposed to optimize the phase distribution of PM, and Jones matrix distribution of BM. As a certificate of concept, the 3D reconfigurable vectorial holographic is validated by numerical simulation in the microwave region. Our proposed 3D reconfigurable vectorial holography scheme provides a new strategy for optical information encryption, high-capacity information storage, and reconfigurable meta-devices.

articleTitle: Modeling of On-chip Transformers for RFIC Design
abstract: This paper presents a review of the electrical performance and equivalent models of on-chip transformers fabricated in IC technology. The effects of parasitic parameters and imperfect coupling between transformer coils are included in the compact equivalent model. A complete signal analysis for the passive component is done based on the mixed-mode S-parameters to evaluate the electrical performance and equivalent models under different excitations. Considering the transformers’ usages in RFIC design, the influences of the center-taps and their load impedance are also analyzed with the corrected mix-mode S-parameters. Finally, Y-parameters converted from the mixed-mode matrix are employed to estimate the transformer’s self-inductances and coupling factor.

articleTitle: A Programmable Meta-System with Hybrid Architecture
abstract: In this paper, a meta-system with easy integration and energy conservation is presented, with a view to its practical application in wireless communication. The meta-system features a hybrid architecture that includes a programmable feed array and a metasurface lens. The feed array is divided into three subarrays, where active elements are doped with passive elements, and interconnected configurations are employed to decrease the number of active elements by one-third effectively. The metasurface lens serves as a passive phase shifter to improve beamforming performance, consequently reducing the number of active elements. An experiment in wireless communication is demonstrated, in which the meta-system acts simultaneously as a direct digital modulator and a transmitting antenna. With its cost-effectiveness, high integration, nearly passive feature, and programmability, the meta-system holds significant potential for future applications in wireless communications.

articleTitle: Terrain Target Height Reconstruction via Terahertz DBS Forward and Down Looking Imaging
abstract: In this letter, a terrain target height reconstruction method based on terahertz Doppler beam sharpening (DBS) imaging is proposed. Specifically, the two-dimensional image of range-pitch angle in terrain scanning area is acquired using the DBS method. The range between the target and platform can be acquired by resort to the pulse compression of echo signal. Since targets at different positions within the radar beam scanning area correspond to different Doppler frequencies, the pitch angle between the target and radar platform can be acquired by the Doppler spectrum of the echo signal. Then, the height of targets can be determined by inversion calculation based on imaging results as well as the geometric model. Numerical results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Antenna Gain Enhancement Based on a Compact Metasurface
abstract: A compact metasurface reflector is designed for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) antenna gain enhancement. The proposed 2-bit circular metasurface reflector is constructed by arranging arrow-shaped unit cells with an embedded nest ring phase profile, thus achieving synthesized phase distribution for an outstanding multi-frequency focusing effect. A UWB Quasi-Yagi patch antenna is designed to evaluate the performance of the proposed metasurface. The result shows that by employing the proposed metasurface reflector, without affecting the -10 dB impedance bandwidth (5.6-18 GHz), the antenna gain is significantly enhanced throughout the ultra-wide operating band, achieving a gain increasement over 6 dB from 6.8-20 GHz and a peak gain enhancement up to 15 dB at 9.2 GHz.

articleTitle: An Analytical Approach to Extract Circuit Model for Low Loss Filtering Multimode Patch Antennas from S11 Measurement
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical approach to diagnose coupling matrix and extract circuit model for low loss filtering multimode patch antennas from S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> measurement for the first time. In contrast to existing reported methods by introducing extra simulation ports or radiation measurement data, we find an analytical method to recover the two-port S-parameters from one-port antenna’s S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>. On the one hand, the proposed method can diagnose coupling matrix and extract circuit model quantitatively and directly. On the other hand, it is applicable for multimode antennas. To verify the proposed method, a practical dual-mode filtering patch antenna is given as an example. The experimental results evidently validate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Non-contact Periodic Limb Movements Monitoring in Sleep Using LFMCW Radar
abstract: Periodic limb movements of sleep (PLMS) are abnormal body movements during sleep and are closely related to various sleep disorders, especially restless legs syndrome. The existing reliable monitoring methods are polysomnography and wearable accelerometers, which are challenging to meet in terms of comfort and convenience in home environments. This paper uses a linear frequency modulation continuous wave (LFMCW) radar to implement the non-contact detection for PLMS. It extracts leg movement signals from the echo signals collected by the radar and effectively identifies PLMS through feature extraction and machine learning. The proposed method achieves an accuracy of 86.41% in detecting PLMS. Therefore, the PLMS detection method based on radar monitoring is an efficient and convenient method that can potentially be applied to home monitoring.

articleTitle: Broadband Elliptical Wide Beam Microstrip Antenna with Low Profile and Large Ground Plane
abstract: A broadband elliptical wide beam microstrip antenna is investigated in this article. The proposed antenna comprises dual radiation patch, corresponding parasitic patch, T-shaped power divider feed network, microstrip waveguide converter, dielectric wall and metallic wall. Dual radiation patch mainly implements the initial elliptical wide beam property and parasitic patch for broadband. The radiation patch is fed by the power divider and connected to the microstrip waveguide converter for integration with the cavity filter further. Both the dielectric wall and metallic wall are used to improve the low elevation gain of the antenna in the H-plane. The validity of the antenna’s performances is verified with a fabricated prototype. Measured results show that the designed antenna can produce 10dB return loss bandwidth with the stable gain from 11.25 to 13GHz.

articleTitle: Antenna decoupling by wavetrap in 5G mobile phone antenna
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a decoupling method in 5G mobile phone antennas by adding wavetrap, which improved about 10 dB for the isolation of two antennas at close distances. This method provides a new idea of antenna decoupling in the increasingly crowded mobile phone space.

articleTitle: An ISGW-based Millimeter-wave Leaky Wave Antenna With Miniaturization and Large Scanning Angle
abstract: A miniaturized leaky wave antenna (LWA) based on substrate integrated gap waveguide (ISGW) was proposed, the ISGW leaky wave antenna consists of three layers. By drawing on the MIM structure of the composite left-handed transmission line, the left-handed inductor LL and the left-handed capacitor CL are introduced into the radiation gap design of the antenna, and the constructed structure has the performance of lefthanded materials, so that the beam can be scanned backward. In order to confirm this, a test sample with three radiating elements was designed. The simulative results verify that the leaky wave antenna has the ability to scan continuously from 28° to -22°. Moreover, there is no attenuation of gain during terminal emission, which overcomes the Open Band (OSB) effect, and the proposed miniaturized structure has a broad application prospect in highly integrated microwave systems. Index Terms—leaky antenna, backward scanning, Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide (ISGW).

articleTitle: Dual-Mode Orthogonal Doherty Power Amplifier With Efficiency Enhancement and Load Mismatch Adaptability
abstract: This paper presents the theory, design and implementation of the orthogonal Doherty power amplifier (ODPA) with dual-mode configuration. It is illustrated that the DPA efficiency performance under active load modulation condition can be further enhanced by introducing the proposed orthogonal architecture with control signal power (CSP) injection. Meanwhile, strong adaptability against load mismatch effect can be achieved by the proposed ODPA with the collaborative use of dual-mode reciprocal bias configuration. A 2.1 GHz dual-mode ODPA is then design and implemented to validate the proposed architecture. With matched load, the fabricated dual-mode ODPA attained higher than 60% drain efficiency throughout the power range from 6 dB output back-off (OBO) to saturation. Moreover, output power variation between 42.8 dBm to 44.6 dBm and OBO efficiency between 47.2% and 58.1% were achieved for mismatched loads at a 2:1 voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) through the mode reconfiguration.

articleTitle: Microwave Scalable Rectenna Array Using Log-Periodic Dipole Antenna Structure
abstract: This paper presents a method for designing a scalable rectenna array using a log-periodic dipole antenna (LPDA) structure. Each dipole antenna element in the LPDA is replaced with a dipole rectenna, which operates at a specific frequency to output DC power. By arranging these dipole rectennas into an array, not only can the bandwidth of the rectenna be extended, but its gain can also be increased, enhancing the antenna’s directivity. Finally, a three-element rectenna array was designed to validate the proposed concept. Simulation results demonstrate that the designed antenna array achieves 28.34% power conversion efficiency at 2.4 GHz when the input power is -20 dBm and a gain of 11.7 dBi.

articleTitle: High-Precision Positioning Intelligent Safety Helmet System for both Inside and Outside Coal Mines
abstract: This project designs an intelligent safety helmet system that integrates functions such as positioning, image transmission, emergency SOS, and emergency lighting. This article first designs a novel butterfly-shaped slot dual frequency filtering antenna, with a frequency range of 4.794GHz to 4.901GHz and 5.510GHz to 5.535GHz, with bandwidths of 107MHz and 25MHz, respectively. This enables image transmission and localization to be transmitted separately, filtering out unnecessary frequency bands and avoiding interference between signals within the pass-band. In terms of positioning, it is proposed for the first time to combine SLAM and YOLO-v4 deep learning algorithms to improve the accuracy of mine positioning, which will solve the problem of significant decline in mine positioning accuracy without GPS signals for the first time. The final intelligent safety helmet has made significant progress in positioning accuracy and electromagnetic compatibility inside and outside the coal mine. This article will provide a detailed introduction to how to improve the accuracy of positioning and image transmission, as well as the electromagnetic compatibility of multiple modules.

articleTitle: A Variable Gain Phase Shifter Based on Insertion-Loss-Tunable Baluns
abstract: In this paper, a Q-band variable gain phase shifter (VGPS) based on insertion-loss-tunable (ILT) baluns is presented, which is designed in a 65nm bulk CMOS process. The proposed VGPS consists of an active phase shifter (PS) based on vector-summing technique and a passive three-stage attenuator. The ILT balun containing a conventional octagonal balun and an additional thin-metal inductor is proposed, which is used to finely tune the insertion loss of the VGPS. The VGPS consumes a DC power of 23mW. In terms of 6-bit phase tuning within 360° at 42GHz, the RMS gain and phase errors of the VGPS are 0.89dB and 0.48°, respectively. And in terms of 6-bit gain tuning with a 31dB maximum attenuation range at 42GHz, the RMS gain and phase errors are 0.47dB and 2.23°, respectively. The VGPS occupies a core chip size of 0.28mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A W-Band LNA with 24.9-dB Gain and 4.8-dB Noise Figure in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: In this paper, a W-Band cascode low noise amplifier (LNA) is fabricated in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. The inductive emitter degeneration technique and serial inductor noise reduction technique are applied for optimizing noise and gain performance. The chip occupies a core area of 0.08 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This integrated LNA achieves a measured maximum gain of 24.9 dB at 94 GHz and a simulated minimum noise figure of 4.8 dB at 83 GHz with a 3 dB bandwidth spanning from 83 GHz to 103 GHz, making it a promising candidate for high-performance radiometer frontends in phased arrays for high speed wireless communication and automotive radars systems.

articleTitle: Tuning the Electromagnetic Degree of Freedom with Engineered Mutual Coupling
abstract: Limited data processing capabilities hinder the full use of electromagnetic degrees of freedom (EDoF), making the redundant EDoF cause network burden. Here, we classify that tuning the EDoF is feasible with the engineered mutual coupling. For the efficient characterization of the mutual coupling, we develop the mutual coupling compensation method based on the theory of characteristic mode. On this basis, we reveal the impact of mutual coupling on the EDoF based on the electromagnetic information theory (EMIT) framework. To further demonstrate the methodology for tuning the EDoF, we give a conceptual result of the tuning EDoF with engineered mutual coupling. Our theory paves the way for the intelligent design and adaptive regulation of the EDoF under the EMIT framework.

articleTitle: Broadband Continuous Complex Propagation Constant Extraction for Differential Transmission Lines
abstract: The complex propagation constants are critical parameters to characterize the differential transmission lines. However, the numerical illness and the assignment of eigenvalues significantly impact the extraction accuracy of the complex propagation constants. This paper presents an automatic method for extracting the broadband complex propagation constants of differential transmission lines. The proposed method can accurately determine the distribution of the eigenvalues and distinguish the differential mode and common mode. Additionally, the method can eliminate the discontinuity points of the attenuation constants by measuring several transmission lines with different lengths. The effectiveness and reliability are validated by the full-wave simulation method in the frequency range of 0.01-130 GHz.

articleTitle: Reverberation Chamber Stirring Method based on Phased Array Antenna and Frequency Stirring Techniques
abstract: In order to overcome the difficulties in construction and operation of mechanical stirring in the reverberation chambers (RC), this paper proposes a mixed stirring method based on phase scanning and frequency stirring (FS) of phased array antennas. The performance of the new stirring method is verified with a 1×8 array in a RC of 8 m × 4.8 m × 3.4 m, and the field uniformity (FU) satisfies the IEC 61000-4-21 standard. In addition, the traditional method and the autoregressive (AR) model are compared for solving independent samples. The results of the experiment indicate that the stirring method proposed in this article is applicable to RC of any size without mechanical stirrers, helping to reduce electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing costs.

articleTitle: Q-band GaAs Quasi-Reflectionless Bandpass Filter with Compact Structure and Wide Absorption Bandwidth
abstract: This paper presents a Q-band quasi-reflectionless bandpass filter (BPF) that is targeted for application in the superheterodyne receivers. The BPF is designed with the inductive loaded coupled-lines and step impedance resonators for a compact structure, such that it can be easily implemented by the GaAs pHEMT technology. In addition, by combining with two wideband Lange coupler, the BPF realizes ultra-wide absorption band within 20-62GHz. The designed BPF is verified in a super-heterodyne receiver, and results show that the BPF is effective to suppress the imbalance in the quadrature demodulation even there is a poor isolation of the mixer.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Wideband Differentially-Fed Dual-Polarized Patch Antenna for 5G/6G mmWave Mobile Terminal Application
abstract: A miniaturized wideband differentially-fed (DF) dual-polarized (DP) patch antenna is proposed for the fifth/sixth generation (5G/6G) millimeter-wave (mmWave) mobile terminal application. The coaxial DF structures are employed to excite the parasitic strips, enabling indirect coupling of energy to the radiation patches owning the shorting pins. As a result, a wide overlapped impedance bandwidth of around 60% (23.6-43.5 GHz), high polarization isolation exceeding 60 dB, and a compact size of 4.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>4.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>1mm are successfully achieved. Meanwhile, the antenna element exhibits a consistent gain response, characterized by a peak gain of 7.1 dBi. It also demonstrates stable radiation patterns, accompanied by remarkably low cross-polarization levels below -50 dB. More importantly, the antenna design only utilizes a single-layer dielectric substrate, contributing to low manufacturing complexity and cost. Therefore, the proposed antenna would be a competitive candidate for numerous smartphone designs.

articleTitle: A 24-GHz Voltage-Combined Stacked Power Amplifier With Current-Sharing Technique in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a voltage-combined stacked field-effect-transistor (FET) power amplifier (PA). The drain-source shunt feedback guarantees proper phase alignment of the voltage swings across the stacked transistors and ensures stability. The proposed current-sharing technique enables single supply operation, which is favored in phased array applications to reduce the design effort of the array board. The PA is designed and fabricated in 65-nm bulk CMOS, and occupies a core area of 0.33 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. At 24 GHz, the PA achieves an output-referred 1-dB gain compression point (OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>) of 19.0 dBm with 17.8% power added efficiency (PAE), and a saturated power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) of 20.0 dBm with 20.1% peak PAE.

articleTitle: A Planar Phased Array Antenna With Wide Angle Scanning Performance
abstract: A planar phased array antenna, operating at X-band, with wide beam-scanning angle is designed and validated in this paper. A wide beamwidth magnetic dipole antenna element is designed at first with half power beamwidth (HPBW) of 130° and 115° in the E- and H-plane respectively, and then an 8×8 planar array is designed using the designed element. Simulation results show that the designed array has a scanning range of ±65° and ±50° with 3 dB gain fluctuation in E- and H-plane respectively. The designed array prototype has been fabricated and experimentally verified. The proposed array has merits of wide-angle scanning, low-profile, low-cost, simple structure and easy integration.

articleTitle: Design of a 2-18 GHz Differential Phase Invariant Low Noise Variable Gain Amplifier in 0.18-μm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated differential ultra-wideband low noise variable gain amplifier (LNVGA) for 2-18 GHz applications in HHNEC 0.18-μm SiGe BiCMOS technology. To achieve the broadband response and in-band gain flatness, a resistive feedback loop and a mutual gain compensation technique are adopted in both amplification stages. In addition, a phase invariant method using opposite phase variations cancellation is proposed, analyzed, and implemented in the current-steering VGA blocks to miniaturize the phase shifts in all gain states.
