The proposed LNVGA exhibits 18-dB gain tuning range and <1dB gain flatness with 2-18 GHz operation bandwidth. The noise figure is 3.2 dB-4.7 dB in all gain states, and the phase variation across different gain states is <3° with a 0.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> compact core area.

articleTitle: A Fully Flexible Compact Dual-frequency Wireless Energy Harvesting System
abstract: For the urgent need for the development of flexible wearable energy harvesting systems or devices, a fully flexible compact dual-frequency wireless energy harvesting system is proposed in this paper. The system comprises a fabric-based omnidirectional flexible antenna measuring 44.4×42.4mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a flexible rectifier circuit measuring 28×33mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. With the measured results, the rectifier circuit achieves excellent efficiencies of 72.3% and 59.8% at 2.4GHz and 5.8GHz under optimal conditions, respectively. It also exhibits good harmonic suppression and wide dynamic load characteristics. The broadband matching characteristics and reflection coefficient of the flexible antenna are also demonstrated. In the end, the entire flexible system is proved to be operated effectively. It obtains DC voltages of 1.27V and 1.07V at 2.4GHz and 5.8GHz from a horn antenna with a power of 20dBm. Furthermore, the rectification efficiency remains relatively constant when the system is bent.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Distributed Amplifier Using Gain Cell with Current-reused and Gain-Enhancement Techniques
abstract: In this paper, as an alternative solution to resolve the high dc power dissipation and low-gain deficiencies of conventional distributed amplifier (DA), for the first time, a gain cell with current-reused, inductive-peaking, and inter-stage series resonance technique is employed as the gain unit of DA. The gain of DA using the employed gain cell can be significantly improved without addition of dc power dissipation and chip area. On-wafer measurement results of a single-stage DA using 4-unit proposed gain cells, fabricated by using 0.25-μm GaAs pHEMT process, indicate that the implemented DA achieves a high average gain up to 19 dB, 14-dBm OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>, and 2.5-dB typical noise figure in the frequency range from 2.8 to 24 GHz. The fabricated amplifier occupies a chip area of 2.52 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: An External Cap-Less Dual-Loop LDO with Low Noise and High Power Supply Rejection
abstract: This paper proposes an external cap-less dual-loop low-dropout regulator (LDO) with simultaneous low noise and high power supply rejection (PSR). The proposed LDO has a low noise global loop and an inner fast loop. To achieve low output noise, a narrow bandwidth in the global loop and a triode in the inner fast loop are adopted. High global loop gain and wideband inner fast loop helps achieve high PSR. Transient-enhanced circuits are employed to improve transient response. The measurement results indicate that the PSR is -33.8dB at 1MHz, the output noise is 2.4nV/√HZ at 1MHz and the undershoot/overshoot is 184mV/50mV.

articleTitle: Class iGF−1 Mode Power Amplifier with Enhanced Linearity
abstract: In this paper, the iGF<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode is proposed to enhance the linearity of the traditional Class F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode while maintaining the high efficiency. The iGF<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode achieves greater flexibility in controlling the amplitude-to-amplitude modulation (AM/AM) profile of the traditional Class F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode by regulating the input nonlinearity and conduction angle simultaneously. This adjustment allows the first inflection point of the AM/AM profile shifted to the higher output power level. The PA is fabricated by CGH40010F and the frequency range is from 2 to 2.6 GHz. The linearity is tested with a 100 MHz 5G NR signal (the peak average power ratio (PAPR) is 8.5 dB) at 2.3 GHz. The worst adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) is -32.3 dBc without digital predistortion (DPD), and −52.1 dBc with DPD. The results show that the iGF<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode has successfully further optimized the linearity of the traditional Class F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode.

articleTitle: One-bit Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging by Adaptive Sparse Logistic Regression
abstract: Owing to the extremely low burdens of transmission and storage by replacing the high-precision and high-speed analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) with simple comparators, many algorithms for one-bit synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging have been proposed in the last decade. Generally, these algorithms can correctly reconstruct the positions of targets and obtain satisfactory imaging quality. However, it is difficult to get the same performance when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is sufficiently low. In this paper, we propose an algorithm combining the sparse logistic regression (SLR) with an adaptive quantization level to improve robustness, named ASLR algorithm. Both simulation and measured data processing demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm under low SNR conditions.

articleTitle: A 122-143GHz(~1/2 fT) Low Noise Amplifier with 7 dB Noise Figure in 130nm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: This paper presents a low noise amplifier (LNA) with 3-dB bandwidth of 122GHz-143GHz in 130 nm SiGe BiC-MOS technology with f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 260 GHz. The design takes into account both gain and noise by using three stage Cascode structure employing feedback capacitance and noise reduction technique. The result shows that the circuit can achieve 7-dB minimum noise figure(NF) at 129 GHz, exceeding 20-dB gain across the whole operation band and an input 1-dB compression point(IP1dB) of −18 dBm, with DC power of 42mW. The chip area of the fabricated LNA is 0.8 × 0.52 mm2, including I/O and DC pads.

articleTitle: A 4.6mW 28-GHz Bidirectional Active Mixer Utilizing Reconfigurable-Gm-R Technique
abstract: This paper presents a bidirectional Reconfigurable-Gm-R active mixer at 28GHz in a 55nm CMOS technology. The proposed mixer can achieve both up and down frequency conversion under 1 dBm local oscillator (LO) by adjusting DC bias and a control signal. A Reconfigurable-Gm-R technique is utilized to realize bidirectional amplifying and minimize current branches in the proposed mixer for saving power. The simulated conversion gain (CG) is-0.42/-0.38 dB at 28-GHz, and the 3-dB bandwidth is 4.9/8.9 GHz in receive (Rx)/transmit (Tx) mode. The total simulated DC power consumption is only 4.2/4.6 mW under 1/1.2V supply voltage in Rx/Tx mode, respectively. Compared with the reported bidirectional active mixers, the proposed mixer exhibits the highest CG and consumes the lowest DC power.

articleTitle: An 18.3-to-44.3-GHz CMOS Low-Noise Amplifier With Triple-Coupled Transformer-Based Interstage Matching Technique
abstract: A broadband millimeter-wave (MMW) low-noise amplifier (LNA) is presented. A novel interstage bandwidth extension technique based on a triple-coupled transformer is presented to effectively improve the gain bandwidth. The proposed MMW LNA can realize a post-simulated peak gain of 17.3 dB at 40.8 GHz with a 3-dB bandwidth from 18.3 to 44.3 GHz and a 10-dB return loss bandwidth from 17.1 to 53.6 GHz. The minimum noise figure (NF) is 2.9 dB at 18.8 GHz and the IIP3 is -2.6 dBm at 30 GHz. The proposed MMW LNA occupies an area of 0.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and consumes 12.3 mW of power.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation for Coprime Array via Capon-MUSIC Algorithm
abstract: In the field of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, coprime array is a new type of array rising in recent years. It significantly improves the degree of freedom (DOF), cope with scenarios when the number of sources is larger than that of array elements compared with traditional uniform linear array (ULA). In this paper we study the DOA estimation method based on multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with coprime array, build the coprime array signal model, obtain the steering vector of the virtual array and calculate the coprime array signal covariance matrix which can be disposed by Capon and multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. We develop the Capon-MUSIC algorithm to deal with situations when the target number is unknown. Compared with the ULA with equal array elements, simulation experiments verify the superiority of DOA estimation performance of coprime array.

articleTitle: Design of a 64-Element Dual-Polarized Planar Receive Phased Array with Four Concurrent Reconfigurable Beams for Ka-Band SATCOM
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a 64-element low-profile dual-polarized receive phased array antenna system with four independent reconfigurable beams for Ka-band low-earth-orbit satellite communication (SATCOM). Single-aperture-integrated multi-beam array systems induce great electrical, thermal, physical, and process challenges due to the extremely limited layout space requirements. To tackle the above problems, an 18-layer high-density hybrid laminated printed circuit board stack-up is utilized. A slot-fed dual-polarized patch antenna array with feed rotation is designed and simulated to guarantee polarization diversity within a simple geometry. Dedicated onboard multi-layer-embedded 4 × 16:1 Wilkinson combining networks are proposed and optimized to facilitate compact multi-beam forming. Simulated results show that the proposed array can synthesize four separate beams scanning up to ±50° in the azimuth plane with low loss and high isolation across 27.5−32 GHz. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a planar phased array supporting four simultaneously reconfigurable beams for Ka-band SATCOM.

articleTitle: A X-band Dual-Power Mode Power Amplifier with Duality Impedance Matching Network
abstract: A monolithic power amplifier in 0.25 µm GaN process is proposed for joint radar and communication. The presented PA is comprised of dual branches to facilitate the specified output power level. In order to meet the load impedance of dual branches, an on-chip duality impedance matching network (DIMN) consisting of switches is realized as a part of input and output matching network. As a proof, under the excitation of a pulse signal with a 100 µs pulse width and a repetition frequency of 1 KHz, it demonstrates a saturated output power of 48.2 dBm-49.5 dBm with a power-added efficiency (PAE) of 40.5%42.8%, and a power gain of 22.2 dB-23.5 dB for high power mode. When the PA operates in low power mode, the measured results obtained using continuous wave signals reveal a saturated output power of 35.7 dBm-37.3 dBm, a PAE of 18.0%-21.8%, and a linear gain of 14.1-17.8 dB. When the proposed PA output a power level of 34.5 dBm, the PAE in LP mode is increased to 17.3% from 2.5% in HP mode. Moreover, the third-order intermodulation is below 30 dBc with a two-tone output power of 30.5 dBm.

articleTitle: SIW-Based Reflectionless Filter/Antenna Using Complementary-Diplexer Architectures
abstract: In this paper, a class of SIW-based reflectionless filter/antenna based on the complementary-diplexer approach is proposed. Firstly, by extracting and controlling the couplings between the adjacent SIW-based cavities, an input-reflectionless bandpass filter consisting of two channels, i.e., a bandpass one for transmission and its complementary resistively-loaded bandstop counterpart for out-of-band RF-power absorption, is realized in the SIW structure. Subsequently, the last cavity resonator of the bandpass channel of the input-reflectionless filter is replaced by a SIW-based slot antenna to form a reflectionless antenna, which shows almost the same input-power-reflection parameter as the initial input-reflectionless filter. For practical-validation purposes, a prototype of the SIW-based reflectionless antenna is fabricated and tested. It is found that the developed antenna prototype exhibits a reflectionless spectral band going from 7.6 to 11.8 GHz and high out-of-band radiation suppression levels above 15 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a Microfluidic Millimeter Wave Chip for Magnetic Beads based Biosensing
abstract: A novel method utilizing a millimeter wave and microfluidic sensor for testing magnetic beads solutions is introduced and experimentally validated for the first time. The sensor based on resonant principles is composed of an easily integrable coplanar waveguide (CPW) and a sprial-shaped defect ground structure (DGS). The transmission parameters of the sensor are simulated and analyzed when the material under test (MUT) are air, ethanol solution and magnetic bead solution. The impact of the complex permittivity and complex permeability of the MUT on the sensor’s performance is also simulated. Simulation results indicate that the proposed sensor is more sensitive to changes in complex permeability. Micro-nanofabrication and on-chip measurement of the designed sensor demonstrate its capability to distinguish the presence of magnetic beads in MUT. Magnetic beads, as one of the commonly used biomarkers, have extensive applications in cell analysis and sorting. Our preliminary study provides a new perspective for the application of millimeter wave and microfluidic technology in biological fields.

articleTitle: Dual-band Flexible Antenna with AMC backing for Wearable Applications
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band flexible antenna with artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) backing for wearable applications. The proposed antenna is designed on a textile material with an overall size of 14 mm × 35 mm × 2 mm. It operates at 2.45 GHz (Industrial Scientific Medical band) and 5.8 GHz (WLAN band) for communications. An AMC reflector with a four-leaf clover-like unit cell is designed and optimized to provide two zero-crossing phases at the desired frequencies and act as a planar reflector. Simulation results show that the AMC reflector enhances the antenna realized gain from 1.80 dB to 3.09 dB at 2.45 GHz, and from 3.86 dB to 6.12 dB at 5.8 GHz. Therefore, the proposed flexible antenna with AMC backing could be a suitable candidate for wearable applications.

articleTitle: A DC-40GHz Switched-Type Attenuator with Combined Capacitive-Inductive Compensation Achieving RMS Amplitude/Phase Errors of <0.23dB/1.3°
abstract: This paper presents a 6-bit broadband switched-type attenuator (STA) with a large attenuation tuning range and low phase error. Four switched attenuation topologies are employed in the attenuation cells, including π-type, cascaded π-type, T-type, and simplified T-type. A novel combined capacitive-inductive compensation technique is proposed in the cascaded π-type structure to compensate for the phase variation of the maximum attenuation unit during state switching. The 6-bit STA is designed in a 65nm-CMOS technology. According to electromagnetic simulation (EM) results, it demonstrates a 31.5-dB amplitude tuning range with a 0.5-dB tuning step and a 2.3-5dB insertion loss (IL) across DC to 40 GHz. The RMS amplitude and phase errors are below 0.23 dB and 1.3° respectively. The chip occupies a core area of 0.14mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.59mm×0.23mm) and consumes negligible power.

articleTitle: Realization of non-uniform metasurface antennas based on the characteristic mode theory
abstract: This paper explores the design process of metasurface antennas using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). A simple 3 x 3 circular patch metasurface is used as the basic structure. By analysing its CMA and modify the structure step by step, two single-layer non-uniform metasurface antennas operating in the 5 GHz WLAN band are designed. Three horizontally polarized modes of the antenna are excited to form a linearly polarized antenna with a relative impedance bandwidth of 21.8% (4.93-6.13 GHz). The circularly polarized antenna is achieved by adjusting two orthogonal modes, resulting in a relative impedance bandwidth of 16.7% (5.05-5.97 GHz) and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth above 500 MHZ.

articleTitle: A Wideband Spoof Plasmonic Circularly Polarized Antenna
abstract: A unidirectional wideband spoof plasmonic (SP) circularly polarized (CP) antenna is proposed in this paper. Four rotating SP dipoles are excited by a sequential-phase feed network using parallel transmission lines, obtaining 90°phase shift and equal power division. Owing to the subwavelength property of spoof plasmonics, our proposed wideband SP CP antenna has a smaller size without parasitic elements. The fabricated antenna has a size of 75mm×75mm×30.83mm (0.67λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.67λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.28λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency), and an average CP gain of 8.74dBic with less than 0.65-dB variation within the 3-dB ARBW. Measured results show an impedance bandwidth (IBW) for S11<-10dB of approximately 47.2% (2.09– 3.38GHz) and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of approximately 33.9% (2.23–3.14GHz), agreeing well with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Design of W-band Antenna Array with Differential Feeding Network
abstract: A 4 × 4 antenna array for W-band applications is presented in this paper. The radiating element of the array is stacked patch fed by substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) directly, a differential feeding network is proposed to feed these radiation elements. The antenna array shows good performance at W-band with the center frequency of 89GHz. The stacked antenna array with differential feeding network is simulated and fabricated, measured results show the return loss of this array can reach-10dB from 83.7GHz~93.8GHz, and the relative bandwidth is about 11.38%, the measured peak gain is 13.63dBi at 87GHz.

articleTitle: Novel Substrateless Metal-Integrated Suspended Line (MISL) Platform and Its Application to a Low-Loss 2-18 GHz Power Divider
abstract: This paper presents a 2-to-18 GHz low-loss power divider using a novel substrateless metal-integrated suspended Line (MISL) platform. Different from the traditional substrate-integrated suspended line (SISL) platform that uses multi-layer substrates, the proposed MISL platform uses an all-metal structure with almost no dielectric material in its core circuit, thus minimizing the dielectric loss. A wideband Wilkinson power divider operating from 2 GHz to 18 GHz is implemented based on the substrateless MISL platform, and the measured insertion loss is less than 1.5 dB in the frequency band. The standing wave ratio (SWR) is maintained below 1.52 while isolation of greater than 15.5 dB.

articleTitle: An Efficient Measurement Technique of Radiation Pattern for Millimeter-Wave Antenna Array Based on Phased Array
abstract: This research proposes an expedited and highly efficient system for testing the directional patterns of antenna arrays, employing phased-array electronic scanning. Specifically designed for production testing of antenna arrays, our method enhances testing speed, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. By strategically adjusting the phase of known phased-array elements and leveraging directional pattern information from the antenna array under examination, our approach outperforms traditional testing methods. The study systematically explores the foundational algorithmic theory behind the testing system and meticulously conducts the construction and validation of the experimental setup.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable terahertz spatial-light-modulator based on a graphene-loaded metasurface
abstract: Spatial light modulators (SLMs), capable of spatially manipulating electromagnetic waves, find extensive applications across diverse fields. However, the current SLMs still face the question of whether they can achieve tunability and reconfigurability. Moreover, tunable SLMs based on phase-change materials still need improvement in terms of the response speed. Here, we proposed a reconfigurable terahertz SLM based on a graphene-loaded metasurface in transmission space. The transmission channel of the device can achieve free switching between on and off states by adjusting the DC voltage applied to graphene. We demonstrated 3 reconfigurable output power density images through pixelated encoding of the DC voltage. The proposed SLM can find widely applications including wireless communication and optical information processing.

articleTitle: A 35-dBm-Output-Power, 26-GHz-Bandwidth Power Amplifier for Space-Air-Ground Applications from C to Ka Band
abstract: In this paper, a high-output power wideband power amplifier (PA) with straightforward matching networks is proposed, demonstrating a seamless integration of active and passive components. Impedance matching is accomplished using a straightforward microstrip parallel network with stepped impedance. Simultaneously, the broadband power distribution/synthesis network enables a six-octave bandwidth spanning from 5 GHz to 31 GHz. To attain high-output power, the PA incorporates an eight-way differential power combining scheme in conjunction with a broadband power synthesis network. The three-stage eight-way power combining PA design achieves a notable 20 dB gain across the frequency range from 5 GHz to 31 GHz, maintaining a tight gain flatness of merely 1.5 dB. It delivers a high output saturation power of 35 dBm and demonstrates a robust linearity index (OIP_3) of 36.13 dBm. This design leverages the pHEMT process.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Wide Tuning Range and Low Phase Noise VCO Using Dual-Mode Switching in 90-nm SOI CMOS
abstract: This paper introduces a novel mode-switched dual-core voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) that integrates a variable inductor and dual-core VCO. The mode switching mechanism involves utilizing a high-Q capacitor as a transformer load and incorporating an external switch to modify the voltage signal across the capacitor. The VCO core maintains low phase noise levels while achieving a broad frequency tuning range, as the switching process does not introduce additional losses. The tuning range implemented by VCO is 12.82 to 16.16 GHz(23%), the peak PN measured at the 1MHz offset obtained by simulation is -117.44 dBc/Hz, and the corresponding FOM is -186.9 dBc/Hz. Each core of the VCO consumes 9.75 mA on a 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz Ultra-Compact Bi-directional PA/LNA Front-End Using Decoupling Balun in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: A 28 GHz ultra-compact bi-directional power amplifier/low noise amplifier (PA/LNA) front-end (FE) using decoupling balun is presented. The proposed decoupling baluns operate as T/R switches and input/output (I/O) matching networks, which also mitigates interference between PA and LNA to improve bi-directional performances. The cascode and common-gate (CG) topologies are adopted in PA and LNA respectively to share the output decoupling balun connected with the antenna, and then reduce the current leakage induced by incomplete transistor on/off operation and parasitic effects. Furthermore, an interstage decoupling matching network based on magnetic self-canceling technique is introduced to improve area efficiency with negligible performance penalty. The measured results demonstrate that the proposed FE achieves 18.1-dB peak gain with a 3.36-dB minimum noise figure (NF) in LNA-mode, and 20.3-dB peak gain with 15.4-dBm 1-dB compression output power (OP1dB) and 17.2% power added efficiency (PAE) in PA-mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Data-Based DC Offset Calibration Technique for Millimeter-wave Interferometric Sensing of Weak Displacement Motions
abstract: The millimeter-wave radar benefits from the short wavelength exhibiting superior performance in sensing weak displacement motions. However, the phase demodulation accuracy can suffer from DC offset. The traditional calibration method struggles with weak displacement motions, which are significantly smaller than the wavelength, as inaccurate estimations result from fitting ultrashort I/Q signals onto the unit circle trajectory. Moreover, this method entails computational complexity. This paper proposes a data-based DC offset calibration technique. It directly utilizes pre-sampled DC values for signal calibration, which is suitable for subtle displacement sensing and simplifys computational demands. The impact of the static clutter reflections on target detection in the experimental environment is analyzed. Experimental results using a 24 GHz interferometric radar show that the proposed technique enables the precise deep sub-wavelength displacement motion detection of 1/104 wavelength with a relatively low root mean square error (RMSE) of 23.06 μm and a weak motion of 1/15.625 wavelength is reconstructed with the relative RMSE (RRMSE) < 4.1%.

articleTitle: Material Surface Classification Based on 24GHz FMCW MIMO Radar
abstract: Surface classification using millimeter wave radar commonly focuses on road condition monitoring, in this area the roughnesses of different surfaces change noticeably. Another challenge is that it’s usually difficult for radar system to recognize various materials when radar is fixed on a moving platform. In this paper, we will introduce a system capable of recognizing 3 materials: carpet, tiles and wooden floors based on 24GHz FMCW MIMO radar. Particularly, this system mainly considers scenarios where radar is fixed on a moving platform. Full-connect neural network and support vector machine (SVM) are employed for classification, achieving a current accuracy of up to 99.04%.

articleTitle: Design of a Tapered Frequency Selective Surface for the Suppression of Edge Wave Scattering
abstract: In this paper, a tapered frequency selective surface (TFSS) has been designed for suppressing electromagnetic scattering from both leading and trailing edge of a square metallic plate. The TFSS is realized by tapered patterned metallic patches with tapered lumped resistor loading. The width of the patterned metal patch gradually decreases away from the edge, while the resistance of resistor gradually increases away from the edge. The backscattering properties from the leading and trailing edge with the proposed TFSS loading are analyzed and compared with that of bare metallic plate. The simulation and measurement results show good consistence, indicating that the TFSS loading can achieve wide angular and wide band edge wave scattering suppressing. Specifically, the average mono-static radar cross section reduction is approximate 20 dB in S-band at 60° oblique incidence.

articleTitle: Axial Deviation Periodic Structure Boundary FDTD Algorithm
abstract: In order to solve the problem of irregular arrangement of periodic structure and deviation in one direction, this paper proposes an algorithm of axial deviation periodic boundary structure. The algorithm is easy to implement and requires less time and memory than ordinary periodic boundary structure. The common periodic boundary structure is just one specific type of axial biased structure. Therefore, the axial biased periodic boundary structure algorithm has a broader range of applications and is more versatile. This lays the groundwork for simulating more complex arrangements of periodic boundary structures.

articleTitle: A 30 MHz to 2.5 GHz GaAs MMIC Power Amplifier
abstract: A 30 MHz to 2.5 GHz ultra-broadband MMIC PA is developed using a 0.15 μm GaAs pHEMT process. Employing an 8-parallel 4-stacked-FET configuration and an RCL feedback circuit without any off-chip matching components, approximately 3 watts of output power with a corresponding power-added efficiency of 28.5-36% is achieved for this PA. Moreover, it also has the gain around 18.5 dB ± 2.5 dB, with a P1dB greater than 33 dBm for the whole frequency band, when it is operating at the bias voltage of +20 V and a current of 240 mA. The chip size is 1.7×1.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Irregular Broadband Doherty Power Amplifier Based on 3-Port Output Combining Network
abstract: To meet the design requirements of the broadband high-efficiency Doherty power amplifier (DPA), a broadband DPA with an irregular matching structure was designed. By using the 3-port combining network design method to conduct an overall analysis and design of the output matching network, the complex steps of designing the main and auxiliary output matching networks of the traditional DPA are simplified. Additionally, a method combining irregular structures and optimization algorithms is used to optimize the output combining network and input matching network, respectively, providing more flexible and efficient impedance matching in the design. Measurement results indicate that within the 1.2-2.8 GHz operating frequency band, the designed DPA achieves a saturated output power greater than 43 dBm, with a saturation efficiency of approximately 50.1-73.4%, and an efficiency exceeding 50% at 6 dB back-off power.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Loss Millimeter-wave Vertical Transition for Interconnects Within Multiple-Inner Layer SISL Platform
abstract: In this paper, a novel low-loss millimeter-wave vertical transition for interconnects within the multiple-inner layer substrate-integrated suspended line (SISL) platform is proposed. The coupled line structure is used to achieve vertical interconnections. Moreover, the coupled lines adopt a double metal inter-connect to achieve low dielectric loss. The proposed vertical transition is designed based on the multi-layer PCB process, and it has the advantages of low loss and self-packaging. From 25 GHz to 42 GHz, i.e. a bandwidth of 50.7%, the simulated return loss is better than 20 dB and the insertion loss is smaller than 0.14 dB.

articleTitle: An Indoor Positioning Method Using Dual FMCW Radar Systems
abstract: This paper presents a new technique for indoor near-field positioning using non-inherent linear frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) dual radar systems. The method involves deploying two incoherent millimeter-wave radars placed vertically to detect the target range, which is particularly suitable for indoor applications. We also describe a fusion method for the vertical radar based on an ideal spatial and signal model, which results in an equivalent distance after fusion. Furthermore, we discuss range and angle resolutions, supported by theoretical simulation results. We have validated the effectiveness of our method through relevant experimental findings.

articleTitle: Digital Predistortion Based on Clustering for Fully-Connected Hybrid Beamforming MIMO Transmitters With Dynamic Beam Steering
abstract: In this paper, a novel method based on the K-means clustering algorithm is proposed to reduce the coefficients sets of digital predistortion (DPD) for fully-connected (FC) hybrid beamforming (HBF) transmitters. With the K-means algorithm, a set of coefficients can compensate for multiple beam directions, which reduces the storage pressure of transmitters while keeping the performance basically unchanged. To validate the proposed method, simulations are performed on a 2-stream, 64-channel millimeter-wave beamforming transmitter array. A total of 1700 beam direction combinations can be reduced to 60 clusters, and the adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) and normalized mean square error (NMSE) are both reduced by less than 2 dB.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Passive double-layer Absorber Design from the Reflective Point
abstract: This paper demonstrates an effective method for designing ultra-wideband double-layer absorbers by using total reflective points. The method realizes ultra-wideband absorption by adjusting the position of the absorption peak of the upper FSS so that it coincides with the total reflection points of the lower FSS structure. Based on this method, an ultra-wideband double-layer absorber is proposed simply and efficiently. From the simulated and measured results, it can be seen that the designed absorber can achieve -10 dB absorption performance in the frequency band of 1.05 - 17.88 GHz with the bandwidth ratio of 17 under the normal incidence.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband High Combining Efficiency Power Combining Network on SISL Platform
abstract: An ultra-wideband 8-way power combining network based on the spatial interconnected structure of substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) is designed for the first time in this paper. Multiple ultra-wideband low-loss Wilkinson power dividers based on the SISL platform are used, and the spatial inter-connection structure is designed to reduce the area of the planar circuit based on the highly integrated characteristic of SISL. The overall circuit layout is compact and easy to integrate with other modules. An ultra-wideband 8-way power combining network is implemented and measured. From 0.5 to 4 GHz, the maximum output power at 1-dB compression point is 29.9 dBm, the power combining efficiency is 71%-91% and reaches a maximum of 91% at 0.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Out-of-band Radiation Suppression in Direct Digital Modulation Communication by Metasurface
abstract: For metasurface-based direct digital communication, a method of suppressing out-of-band radiation is presented to reduce signal leakage and interference outside the target transmission band. By adding a window signal to the feeding source, the radio frequency carrier wave's amplitude can be adjusted. Signal components with lower power levels are obtained beyond the desired frequency spectrum with non-uniform amplitude. The appropriate window signal can be chosen based on the requirements. To confirm the viability of the suggested approach, transmitter structure and transmission simulation are supplied. The results show that this method can increase the radiation performance of direct digital communication and achieve symbol transmission, indicating its potential for future wireless communication.

articleTitle: The Concept of Polarization Effect on Passive Intermodulation
abstract: This paper proposes that the radiation passive intermodulation (PIM) has polarization effect in line-contact junction for the common antenna system. A nonlinear circuit model is proposed to simulate PIM sources with line contact in a radiation environment. Also, a method to obtain PIM value by EM simulation and calculation is proposed. Through the model and simulation PIM levels, this study first introduces the concept of PIM polarization effect.

articleTitle: Multi-band geometric phase metasurface with independent phase modulation
abstract: Geometric phase has stimulated great importance among the metasurface community to realize abrupt phase changes. Here, we presented a metasurface with high efficiency, consist of two different structures having independent phase shift response. The two structures consists of an inner resonator (X-shaped) and outer split ring resonator (SRR). The inner structure resonates at 29.5 GHz with 95% reflection efficiency while outer SRR exhibits a dual-band response at 11.6 GHz and 15.8 GHz, with efficiency exceeding 92%. Moreover, both the bands of outer structure simultaneously exhibit independent phase shift response with the inner structure under geometric rotation. The overall effectiveness of the design can be observed from its ability to achieve high efficiency, compactness, independent and stable response under geometric rotation.

articleTitle: Design of A Third-order Inline Waveguide Bandpass Filter With Cross Coupling and Spurious Mode Suppression
abstract: A third-order inline waveguide bandpass filter (BPF) with cross coupling and spurious mode suppression is designed in this paper. Based on the conventional cascaded-coupled filter, the cross coupling is realized by reducing the height of the second resonating cavity and introducing a stacked cavity for cross coupling, which generates a transmission zero (TZ) on the right side of passband. In order to eliminate the spurious modes caused by the cross-coupled cavity, a short-circuited post is introduced to make TE101 and TE102 mode of the cavity introduced for cross coupling self-suppressed. Therefore, the proposed inline waveguide BPF is with one TZ on the right side of passband while preserving almost the same bandwidth of stopband when compared to the conventional cascaded-coupled filter. The design process is illustrated in detail and the measured results verify the feasibility of the proposed inline waveguide BPF.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Subspace-based Optimization Method with the Cross-correlated Term
abstract: In this paper, we proposed the cross-correlated subspace-based optimization method (CC-SOM) to solve inverse scattering problems. CC-SOM combines the concept of subspace partition and the cross-correlated cost function, which can determine the deterministic part of the induced current by spectrum analysis and the rest part by an iterative method. It enables higher inversion accuracy, faster convergence, and better robustness than the classical SOM and cross-correlated contrast source inversion (CC-CSI).

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Current-reuse LNA in 100nm GaAs Process
abstract: In this paper, a design and implementation of a low-noise amplifier (LNA) Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) chip operating at Ka-band (30-40GHz) is presented. The proposed chip utilizes a current-reuse structure, which significantly simplifies the design and save the current consumption from one DC supply. A three-stage common-source amplifier is fabricated in 100nm GaAs pHEMT process. Measurement results show a noise figure of less than 2.2dB, gain of 18dB, power consumption of 70mW from 5V supply, and an output 1dB compression point (P1dB) of 4.5dBm.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized 3-D Microwave Absorbers With Synthesizable Operating Bandwidth, Absorptive Resistance, and Absorption Ratio
abstract: This paper proposes dual-polarized 3-D microwave absorbers. The working strategy of single-polarized design is firstly analyzed with the equivalent transmission line model. In this way, the absorptive performance, including operating bandwidth, absorptive resistance, and absorption ratio, can be easily synthesized. Characteristic impedances for different absorptive performance are given to provide more design selection. Besides, only one absorptive resistor is employed in the proposed absorber element, avoiding complex structure with multiple resistors. Two absorbers are successfully implemented with different operating bandwidths and absorptive resistances to verify the selectable performance. Finally, the single-polarized designs are extended to dual-polarized versions. Good agreement can be seen for two perpendicular polarizations with expected performance, which further prove the proposed design concept.

articleTitle: A 26~32 GHz Bidirectional Up/Down Image-Reject Mixer Module with 2~8 GHz IF Bandwidth for 5G Applications
abstract: This paper presents a 26~32GHz image-reject bidirectional mixer in 55nm CMOS for the fifth-generation (5G) application. The Hartley architecture is utilized for image rejection in the mixer. Meanwhile, the mixer achieves the transition between TX and RX modes by switching the relative phase of the LO signals. The detailed principal analysis is presented in the paper. A two-stage IF Polyphase Filter (PPF) is introduced to support a wide IF bandwidth. Additionally, calibration capacitors are employed in the mixer core to reduce LO leakage. According to simulation results, the mixer shows the IF bandwidth of 2~8GHz. In the up-conversion operation, the mixer achieves the conversion gain (CG) of -12.2~-14.6dB, the image rejection ratio (IRR) of 26~37dB and the isolation between LO and RF port of 56~62dB. In the down-conversion operation, the mixer realizes the CG of - 12.4~-14.6dB, the IRR of 26~33dB and the isolation between LO and RF port of 52~54dB.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide Metal Column Perturbation Dual-band Bandpass Filter
abstract: This paper proposes an Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide metal pillar micro-perturbation dual-band bandpass filter. The main idea is to introduce a micro-perturbation structure into the filter structure, which disturbs the electromagnetic field propagation of the bandpass filter, introduces new resonance points, and changes the coupling mode of the filter to achieve the function of dual-band bandpass filter. The designed filter achieves -3 dB passband in 23.24-27.12 GHz and 28.01-29.5 GHz, with fractional bandwidths of 15.9% and 5.2%, respectively. The insertion loss and return loss performance in the passband are both good. The structure has good filter roll-off characteristics, with group delay in the passband less than 0.5ns, achieving a low group delay effect.

articleTitle: Characterization of Kinetic Inductance and Sensitivity in Superconducting MKIDs with Varied Aluminum Film Thicknesses
abstract: This paper examines how the thickness of Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) films affects their sensitivity. We fabricated MKIDs with different film thicknesses on monocrystalline silicon substrates and investigated their response rate, noise, and sensitivity at 100 mK. Our results indicate that changes in film thickness do not impact the noise spectrum, but they do lead to a decrease in the responsivity of the MKID. Ultimately, this decrease in responsivity results in a reduction in the sensitivity of the MKIDs.

articleTitle: High-gain Miniaturized Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Leaky-Wave Antenna with Slow-wave Substrate Integrated Waveguide
abstract: A high-gain, miniaturized spoof surface plasmon polariton leaky-wave antenna (SSPP-LWA) with a slow-wave substrate integrated waveguide (SW-SIW) is designed. This antenna has a two-layer structure, the top layer comprises SSPP units, while the bottom layer incorporates metal blind vias and metal patches within the SIW, culminating in a SW-SIW-SSPP configuration. In the SW-SIW the guided wavelength of the electromagnetic wave is reduced to half of its original length. Consequently, in the same antenna length, the LWA based on the SW-SIW has twice the number of radiating elements, thereby enhancing both efficiency and gain. On the other hand, due to the slow-wave structure’s enhancement of the effective relative permittivity and effective relative permeability, the lateral dimensions of the antenna are reduced by 53% and its longitudinal dimensions by 73%. Furthermore, to suppress the open stopband (OSB) of the antenna, surface sinusoidal modulation has been applied to the SSPP slot units on the antenna’s top layer. The antenna exhibits a gain exceeding 15dBi in the 10.6 GHz to 14.4 GHz frequency range and supports a continuous beam scanning range of 114° (from -68° to +46°).

articleTitle: A Simple Decoupling Method for Closely-Spaced Circular Patch Antennas
abstract: In an effort to reduce the coupling between compact array antenna elements, circular stubs were incorporated at the edges of the circular antenna elements in this study. Without any additional decoupling structures being used, the mutual coupling between two closely placed antenna elements was effectively reduced. The proposed array antenna is achieved with greater than 23.8 dB isolation within the -10 dB operating bandwidth from 2.75 GHz to 2.86 GHz. The array elements are in the form of circular patches loaded with circular stubs, and the distance between the elements is very closely spaced, only 0.3 mm in this work.

articleTitle: SiC-Based D-Band Substrate Integrated Waveguide Dual-Band Bandpass Filter and Diplexer
abstract: For the first time, a D-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) dual-band bandpass filter (DBBPF) and a diplexer using mixed single- and dual-mode coupled topologies are presented based on silicon carbide (SiC) technology. Circuit miniaturizations can be achieved utilizing such type of mixed-mode coupled topologies while maintaining flexibly controlled dual-band frequencies and bandwidths. Fractional bandwidth (FBW) design graph is employed to show the flexibility of the realizable FBWs of the two bands for both devices. A third-order direct-coupled DBBPF and a diplexer with two bands centered at 120 and 140 GHz are synthesized and designed as demonstrations.

articleTitle: Improved Theoretical Model for the Reflection Coefficient Coverage of Tunable Lossy Lumped Matching Networks in Complex Impedance Case
abstract: Tunable reactance component (TRC) plays an important role in adaptive impedance matching technology. In order to design a tunable matching network (TMN) that can cover a specific region, it is necessary to establish a reflection coefficient model to indicate the coverage region. In this paper, the theoretical boundary arcs of TMN composed of lossy TRCs with respective quality factors (Q) in complex impedance case are proposed. The proposed model determines the coverage region by multiple Jordan closed curves in terms of self-intersecting coverage and multi-connected coverage regions. This model is suitable for L, T and π lossy TMNs. It is validated in experiments in terms of both simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Design of Folded SIW Cavity-Fed Miniaturized Microstrip Patch Filtering Antenna
abstract: This paper proposes a design of folded substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-fed miniaturized microstrip patch filtering antenna. The presented antenna consists primarily of a folded SIW cavity, a rectangular coupling aperture, and a stacked patch resonant radiator. Energy is fed into antenna through the folded SIW cavity on the bottom layer, coupled to the patch radiator on the upper layer, and then radiated. The multilayered design, along with the folded SIW cavity, allows for a compact antenna configuration. A prototype is designed and simulated. The results show a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 4.75% (4.11 GHz to 4.31 GHz), a peak realized gain of 7.8 dBi, and a cross-polarization level better than 35 dB.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Analog Baseband for Superconducting Qubit Readout
abstract: Superconducting qubits are promising candidates for building scalable quantum computers, but they require efficient and flexible readout systems that operate at cryogenic temperatures. This article presents a cryo-CMOS analog baseband (ABB) for superconducting qubits readout, which targets flexibly reconfigurable gain, center frequency, and bandwidth. The ABB achieves power and area reduction by integrating programmable-gain amplifiers and filters in one block and by using differential capacitors rather than single-ended ones. The differential-mode gain and common-mode stability of the low-pass filter are improved by negative-impedance inverters. Implemented in 28-nm Bulk CMOS technology, the ABB occupies an active area of 0.016 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It has a tunable gain range from 10.7 to 42.5 dB, a center frequency from 101 to 189 MHz, and a bandwidth from 1.3 to 2.8 MHz. Thus, the ABB enables high-fidelity and low-power readout of superconducting qubits for future large-scale quantum computers.

articleTitle: A new 2-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Metasurface unitcell for sub-6GHz band
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent metasurface (RIS) has been widely concerned because of its strong ability to regulate electromagnetic waves. Compared with the reflected RIS, the transmitted RIS can realize the forward space scanning and avoid the local occlusion caused by the feed antenna. In order to improve the efficiency of the transmissive RIS, in addition to improving the transmission efficiency, improving the phase quantization accuracy is also a way. Based on this, we propose a 2-bit transmission-type RIS unit. In order to test the performance of the RIS unitcell, we made a unitcell without receiving antenna, directly feeded RF signal with SMA connector, control the switching diode on and off, and measure the phase shift of the unitcell. The test results show that in the sub-6GHz band 5.7-5.9GHz, the proposed transmission-type metasurface unit can achieve phase shifts of 0°, 90 °, 180 ° and 270 °. The test results are consistent with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A 21-24 GHz Phase Controlled Frequency Source Array Based on Cascade LO Phase-Shifting Architecture for mmW Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: A phase-controlled frequency source array based on cascade local oscillator (LO) phase-shifting architecture for millimeter wave (mmW) wireless power transfer is introduced in this paper. A phase-controlled frequency source is designed by using 65 nm CMOS technology. The designed array can achieve over 360° continuous phase shifting in the range of 21-24 GHz, and the phase error and amplitude error of each phase shifter unit are less than 0.72°and 0.7 dB respectively. The core area of the phase shifter unit is 0.86×0.835 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The power consumption is 60 mW, and the output power is greater than -10 dBm.

articleTitle: An overlapping Sub-Aperture Method for Unified Near-Field and Far-Field Localization
abstract: The topic of positioning is challenging and complex. Many closed-form positioning solutions have been suggested, utilizing modified polar representation (MPR) to account for measurement error and sensor position errors. High sensor position errors can significantly reduce the accuracy of target location. In this paper, a novel overlapping sub-aperture (OSA) localization method is designed to mitigate inaccuracies in target positioning resulting from measurement errors and sensor position errors by a novel correlation method of these sub-apertures. The proposed method has shown superior localization accuracy in simulation results compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: A Fast Inverse Design Method for Reconfigurable Intelligent Metasurface Based on Generative Model
abstract: Traditional design of reconfigurable intelligent metasurface (RIS) with specific scattering properties is a time-consuming process that relies on the design experience. In this article, we propose an inverse design method for RIS based on generative model to solve the non-uniqueness problem that one electromagnetic (EM) response corresponds to multiple unit structures. This method includes three parts: a forward prediction model, a conditional variational auto-encoder (CVAE) model and a Gumbel-Sinkhorn operator model. The forward prediction model is trained to quickly obtain the corresponding EM responses of RIS patterns. The CVAE model first encodes the RIS pattern and EM responses together into latent space and flexibly generates a series of corresponding candidate RIS patterns based on the target EM response. The Gumbel-Sinkhorn operator is used to reduce the discrete mapping error of these candidate RIS patterns. Then we feed these candidate patterns generated by the CVAE model and optimized by the Gumbel-Sinkhorn operator into the trained forward prediction model to obtain their corresponding EM responses. By selecting the predicted responses that fulfill the target response, the non-uniqueness problem is solved, which verifies the practicality and accuracy of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A 32.8GHz bandwidth 50GSa/s InP Track&Hold Amplifier using Darlington Structure and Clock fT-Doubler Technique
abstract: A high-speed track and hold amplifier (THA) based on INP double-heterojunction bipolar transistor (DHBT) process technology is proposed, which is applied to high-speed sampling system. This design innovatively uses Darlington Structure and inductance peaking technology to improve the input and output circuit bandwidth. At the same time, the Darlington Structure is also used to Increase sampling speed of the track and hold (T/H) switch, and the Clock cutoff frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>)-Doubler structure is used to increase the working frequency of the clock buffer, so as to further improve the sampling rate. The design is based on a base-emitter (BE) diode switching architecture that achieves a -3dB bandwidth of 32.8GHz at a sampling rate of 50GSa/s. The simulation results show that the THD is -32.1dB and SFDR is 32.5dB at 15GHz P1dB input.

articleTitle: A 5-18 GHz 6-bit Active Phase Shifter with Transformer-based Quadrature Poly-phase Networks in 0.18 µm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: In this letter, a 6-bit ultra-wideband phase shifter for active phased arrays is presented in 0.18 µm SiGe BiCMOS process. A differential two-stage transformer-based poly-phase quadrature signal generator with over 100% bandwidth is proposed and analyzed. The vector modulator consists of a common-base buffer for polarity selection and invariant input impedance and variable gain amplifiers (VGAs) with an active inductive load for bandwidth extension. The 360° full-span vector-modulator phase shifter achieves a 5.625° resolution and 0.9 dB peak gain with 0.99-3.75° and 0.82-0.94 dB RMS phase/gain error at 5 to 18 GHz. The core area of the circuit is 0.98 mm × 1.55 mm.

articleTitle: Filtenna-Filtenna Design for Broadband and High-Selectivity Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: This paper presents a novel broadband quasi-elliptical bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) for radome applications. The proposed FSS consists of a periodic array of patch with the stub-loaded resonator in pieces of double-layer printed circuit boards, which are connected by via through the ground and then stacked together with a certain distance. The simulation results show that the −1.5 dB transmission bandwidth is 8.21 ~ 11.66 GHz, and two transmission zeros are outside of a passband. This configuration enables FSS to facilitate broadband transmission and high selectivity.

articleTitle: SISL-based Miniaturized Bandstop Filter with Broadband Continuous Frequency Tuning for X-band Applications
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized broadband frequency tunable bandstop filter is proposed for X-band applications based on substrate integrated stripline (SISL). Miniaturization is achieved by a pair of stepped impedance resonators (SIRs) with mixed electrical and magnetic coupling and large capacitance to the ground. The wide frequency tuning range is due to the varactor diodes placed near the short circuit end. By suspending the main part of the filter in the air cavity, the restriction of the very low Q-value of the varactor diode at high frequencies can be eliminated. The fabricated filter exhibits a wide frequency tuning range of 7.63-11.42 GHz and a stopband rejection level of 14-28 dB.

articleTitle: Application of Millimeter-wave Radiometer to the Measurement of Electromagnetic Parameters in Solid Materials
abstract: In order to study the electromagnetic parameters of dielectric materials in the millimeter-wave band, the complex permittivity of polypropylene material and soda-lime glass was actually measured by using a millimeter-wave radiometer to build a free-space measurement system and perform error control. The measurement results show that the relative error of the real part of the complex permittivity measured by using the millimeter-wave radiometer measurement method does not exceed 8.51%, which has a good measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: An Overview of the Impact of the Temperature on the Small- and Large-Signal Performance of 0.15-μm Microwave GaN HEMTs
abstract: The goal of the present work is to study the influence of the thermal effects on the small- and large-signal characteristics of gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) devices by using an extensive campaign of measurements. The studied devices were manufactured using a 0.15-μm process on silicon carbide (SiC) substrate. Experiments carried out on the three HEMTs with different gate widths are investigated in detail to get a thorough comprehension of how changing the backside temperature up to 100°C affects the transistor performance.

Index Terms: Gallium Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors

articleTitle: A Compact Filtering Power Divider with Wideband Harmonic-Suppressed Ability
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of a wideband power divider (PD) with large spurious suppression. By modifying the Wilkinson-PD structure with simple stubs, out-of-band controllable transmission zeros are achieved up to the fifth harmonics. Only a few transmission lines and one resistor are needed. With derived equations for calculating the design parameters, the proposed circuit can be optimized and implemented flexibly at a fast speed. To validate the proposed design, a 1.0 GHz filtering PD prototype is demonstrated on the Rogers RO4003C substrate. The fabricated PD shows a compact layout, occupying only 0.13λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.18λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. From the measurement results, 70% operating bandwidth and a 0.2 dB in-band insertion loss are achieved. Meanwhile, the superb spurious control ability is also tested, which shows ⩾40 dB ultra-wide harmonic suppression covering 2nd to 5th and ⩾23 dB stopband suppression at 1.9~5.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Interconnection Design for a 2.5D Integrated RF Front-End Based on Silicon Interposer
abstract: This article presents the interconnection design for a 2.5D integrated eight-channel RF transmitter front-end module. The front-end is the stack structure of a multi-chiplet silicon interposer and an antenna in low temperature cofired ceramic, with an area of 20×15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Applying the asymmetric round bend and single-stub matching structures, good performance can be achieved with the interconnects between CMOS and GaAs chiplets and those from the GaAs chiplet to antenna. In full-wave simulations, the return loss is better than 25 dB and the insertion loss is not higher than 2.3 dB up to 33 GHz. The link budget is further carried out for one transmitter channel.

articleTitle: Characterization of Cryogenic Photo Diodes on the Standard 28nm Bulk CMOS Process
abstract: Inside a quantum computer, using optical links for communication between low temperature and room temperature can reduce cooling requirements, prevent crosstalk, and simplify communication interfaces. In this paper, we propose a CMOS cryogenic photo diode fabricated on the standard 28nm bulk CMOS process without any modification, whose diagonal length is 38 micrometers, and the PN junction is formed by N-well and P substrate. We tested the response of the photodiode to 637nm red laser and 532nm green laser at room temperature and 7K low temperature, and the largest measured responsivity reaches 55.8mA/W at 7 kelvin.

articleTitle: A Novel Design Methodology for MSSW Transmission Lines Without Iteratively Solving Maxwell-Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Equation
abstract: Magnetostatic surface wave (MSSW) has unique features of unidirectional propagation, slow group velocity, and magnetic tunability, leading to wide applications in microwave devices and components like magnetostatic surface wave transmission lines (MSSW-TLs) for analog signal processing. Due to the strong interaction between MSSW and RF signals, solving the coupled Maxwell-Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (Maxwell-LLG) equations is necessary in modeling MSSW devices, which is however resource-intensive and time-consuming. To avoid solving the coupled equations, in this work, a novel design methodology based on the analogy between magnetic biasing and amplification is proposed for MSSW-TLs. The performance of a biased MSSW-TL can thus be easily predicted by its unbiased performance (Maxwell’s equation only) with an amplification factor, leading to a rapid optimization process that is accelerated by ~100. An yttrium iron garnet (YIG)-based MSSW-TL prototype is successfully designed using the proposed method. The experimental data proves the effectiveness of the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: A 24-30 GHz 6-Bit GaN HEMT Digital Attenuator for Millimeter-Wave Phased Array Systems
abstract: A 24-30 GHz 6-bit digital attenuator for millimeter-wave phased array systems based on a 100-nm gallium-nitride-silicon (GaN-on-Si) technology, is presented. To improve insertion loss (IL) and attenuation accuracy, switched-π/T improved structures are employed in this design. The cascade sequence of the attenuation units is selected according to the influence of standing-wave characteristics. Experimental results show that the presented GaN-on-Si digital attenuator achieves a dynamic range of 31.5dB, incremented by 0.5dB. From 24 to 30 GHz, the IL is less than 4.9dB and the attenuation accuracy is better than 0.5dB, with the RMS attenuation error of less than 0.31dB. The return loss is better than -12.8dB in all states. The chip size is 2.31×0.76.

articleTitle: Design of 2-Track DMS SAW Filter with Low Loss, High Selectivity and Compact Size for Band-29 Applications
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized surface acoustic wave (SAW) bandpass filter for Band-29 applications is designed, fabricated, and measured. The proposed filter is composed of two symmetrically cascaded double-mode SAW (DMS) structures with the same configuration. Each DMS comprises five interdigital transducers (IDT) with pitch modulation. The operating mechanism of the 2-track DMS filter is elucidated through even- and odd-mode analysis methodologies, and the lumped-element equivalent circuit of the proposed filter is derived. Flexible control over even- and odd-mode resonances, along with the positioning of the transmission zero (TZ) at the left side of the passband, is achieved by adjusting the pitch sizes of different IDT groups. Various grounding strategies are explored to enhance the out-of-band rejections. The proposed filter is simulated by both the coupling-of-modes (COM) model and the finite element method/boundary element method (FEM-BEM). For verification, the filter is fabricated, and packaged, demonstrating good agreement with the simulated performance.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency and Low-Ripple Microwave Rectifier Based on GaN Schottky Barrier Diode
abstract: A high-efficiency, low-ripple microwave rectifier based on a gallium nitride (GaN) Schottky barrier diode (SBD) is presented. A vertical GaN-SBD, specifically designed and fabricated for rectification, features anode and cathode electrode dimensions of 285 um × 397 um. Large pad size and robust stability allow it to function without package, thereby circumventing the parasitic effects induced by packaging. As a result, the accuracy of the GaN-SBD model is enhanced. With this model, we conceived a 5.8 GHz high-efficiency, medium-power rectifier. The rectifier's ripple coefficient is significantly reduced by selecting an appropriate filtering capacitor and integrating it with a rear low-pass microstrip filter for cooperative simulation—enabling the rectifier to deliver stable output power as a power source. Measurement shows that at an input power of 29 dBm, the peak rectification efficiency reaches 79.7%, with an output current of 80.4 mA, signifying the rectifier's robust current driving capability. Moreover, owing to the precise high-frequency model of the GaN-SBD, the efficiency and current curves derived from testing correlate closely with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Investigations on Polarization Insensitive/Sensitive Energy Harvesting Metasurface
abstract: The polarization-insensitive energy harvesting metasurface (EHM) can exhibit a stable harvesting efficiency under the incident electromagnetic wave with arbitrary polarization. However, the desired polarization insensitivity highly depends on the specific structures of EHMs. A three-step evolutionary design of EHMs is discussed and compared, to reveal the relationship between the polarization insensitive/sensitive performance and the desired power-combining networks of the designed EHMs. The comparison and analysis show that the polarization-insensitive EHM is typically comprised of two or four centrosymmetric vias in each unit cell with orthogonal placements, which inevitably introduces a design complexity to the power-combining network. Moreover, the guided currents on these vias are naturally out of phase, and thus phase shifters are necessary for phase compensation. The polarization-sensitive EHM has the simplest structure, and it is experimentally demonstrated with a measured energy harvesting efficiency of 82.1% at 5.8 GHz. Hence, a trade-off design should be considered during the design of EHM for specific applications.

articleTitle: Anisotropic 3-D Frequency-Selective Structure with Identical Profile Consideration for Unified Manipulation Designs of Spatial Waves
abstract: This paper proposes an anisotropic three-dimensional (3-D) frequency-selective structure (FSS) design method, utilizing a variety of stacked slotlines and microstrip lines (MSL) based slow-wave structures, which are mapped by a generalized filtering network. Additionally, leveraging the phase slope relationships of adjacent- or different-order networks, this paper introduces a unified phase design concept for spatial wave manipulation, encompassing both in-band constant phase slopes and true-time delay characteristics. Using the numerical short-open-load calibration extraction, this paper thoroughly compares propagation performance and slow-wave coefficient between slow-wave structures and uniform transmission lines. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed design concept is verified by designing a right-hand to left-hand circular polarization converter mapped by orthogonal fourth- and sixth-order wideband filtering topologies. The simulation results agree with the theoretical prediction and have good angular stability.

articleTitle: A 2.8-to-67 GHz 180-degree Phase Shifter Based on the SISL Platform
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband 180-degree phase shifter based on the substrate-integrated suspended line (SISL) platform. The proposed phase shifter consists of a wideband phase inverter and a reference line. The phase inverter is composed of a transition structure from the suspended microstrip line (SML) to a substrate-integrated suspended parallel strip line (SISPSL). A shielding enclosure composed of double-layer metamaterials is designed to eliminate the resonance caused by the transition structure. The 180° SISL phase shifter has been fabricated and measured. From 2.8 GHz to 67 GHz, i.e. a 183.95% fractional bandwidth, the measured return loss is better than 11 dB. The output phase imbalance is within ±3° from 39.8 GHz to 60 GHz. The proposed SISL phase shifter can be combined with a broadband power divider to form an ultra-wideband balun.

Author Keywords: substrate integrated suspended parallel strip Line (SISPSL)

articleTitle: A 24.25-29.50 GHz 6-Bit Active Vector-Summing Phase Shifter with Low Gain Variation for 5G Communication
abstract: This paper presents a 6-bit active vector-summing phase shifter (VSPS) fabricated in 65nm 1P9M CMOS technology. To achieve low gain variation, low root-mean-square (RMS) phase and gain error, a degenerated-Q quadrature-all-pass filter (QAF) and a novel current-canceling phase inverting variable gain amplifier (PIVGA) with magnetically coupled resonators (MCR) for pole-tuning are used. Measurement results show that the proposed VSPS covers a 360° phase shifting range with a 5.625° step. The gain variation is no more than 3.18 dB throughout all the 64 phase states at 24.25-29.50 GHz. The RMS phase error is <1.1° after calibration, and the RMS gain error is <0.46 dB. The input-referred 1-dB compression point (IP1dB) is 5.4-6.8 dBm, and the power consumption is 33.4 mW. The proposed VSPS is suitable for 5G NR FR2 n257, n258, and n261 band communication.

articleTitle: A 3.0-3.7GHz Outphasing Power Amplifier with Bandpass Combiner for 5G Applications
abstract: This paper introduces a broadband outphasing power amplifier (OPA) meticulously designed for operation within the 3.0~3.7 GHz frequency range, strategically addressing the imperative for wideband and high peak-to-average-power ratio (PAPR) signal transmission in the realm of 5G wireless communications. The proposed OPA employs the current combining mode in its architectural framework, intricately integrating a multi-stage bandpass network to formulate the combiner. In order to substantiate the viability of the proposed design, a prototypical broadband model is meticulously constructed. Experimental results unequivocally demonstrate that the maximum output power is confined within the ambit demarcated by points 44.78dBm to 45.03dBm. Furthermore, saturation and 6 dB power back-off drain efficiencies are meticulously delineated within the intervals 63.4% to 72.6% and 51.6% to 76.4% respectively at 3.0~3.7 GHz. These empirical findings unequivocally affirm the efficacy of the designed broadband OPA in adeptly meeting the stipulated requisites for 5G wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna With Wide Axial Ratio Beamwidth Based on Square-Ring Coupled Feeding
abstract: A compact dual-circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna with wide axial ratio beamwidth (ARBW) based on square-ring coupled feeding is proposed. A meandered patch and a shorting wall are introduced for size reduction and ARBW enhancement. A square ring structure etched below the patch is used to feed through capacitive coupling. A quadrature hybrid, integrated into the feed network, introduces a 90° phase difference between the outputs of the through and coupled arms, facilitating the emission of CP radiation. The ultimate size of the proposed antenna are 0.38λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.38λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.05λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The simulated outcomes demonstrate the -10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW) over 30% and the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth exceeding 20%. The maximum ARBW reaches 227° in two orthogonal principal planes at 2.44 GHz, consistent for both CP states.

articleTitle: Design of Bandpass Filters with Flexible Transmission Zeros Based on Metal Integrated Suspended Line Technology
abstract: We present bandpass filters based on multi-layer metal integrated suspended line (MISL) technology in this paper. The designed filters have flexible transmission zeros (TZs). First, we analyze how a single resonator’s construction affects its resonance frequency. Second, aim at verify the concept of the resonator, we give out the design of two second-order filters which are coupled with electric dominant and magnetic dominant, the two filters produce TZs at different locations. Finally, we conduct simulations and measurements on the designed BPF, the results validate the feasibility of the design.

articleTitle: A Wideband Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array for Sub-6G With Integrated Tapered Balun and FSS
abstract: In this paper, a wideband wide-angle scanning phased array is presented, capable of covering the entire Sub-6G frequency range. The array has linear polarization and is capable of wide-angle scanning capabilities. Notably, the array achieves a continuous impedance bandwidth of 18:1 at the broadside (VSWR < 3). As the scanning angle increases, a wide scanning range (±70°) can be achieved, with VSWR below 4 at each angle. However, in the H-plane, the VSWR worsens when scanning beyond 70°. In addition to building on the tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) concept, a novel ring-type resistive frequency selective surface (FSS) card is designed, which is frequency related and adjusted for maximum radiation efficiency across the whole working band. Furthermore, a tapered balun is employed for feeding, which realizes the desired large operating bandwidth. Finally, a 4 ×4 array prototype was simulated and fabricated, demonstrating its suitability for 5G ultra-wideband beamforming arrays.

articleTitle: A Highly Selective and Compact SAW Filter With Cascaded DMSs
abstract: High-performance filter is currently a critical component for radio frequency (RF) front-end modules, and piezoelectric on insulator – surface acoustic wave (POI-SAW) is gradually becoming the mainstream implementation form due to its good electromechanical coupling coefficient and high quality factor (Q). Based on the 50°Y-X LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si substrate, a highly selective SAW filter is designed and fabricated, which is mainly composed of two cascaded double-mode SAWs (DMSs) and a series resonator. The tilted interdigital-transducer (IDT) is used to suppress the transverse modes, and the tilt angle is 8 degrees. The center frequency of the filter is 1059 MHz. The relative bandwidth is 1.7%. The out-of-band rejection can reach 40dB, and the active chip area is 1mm×0.4mm. The filter is fabricated, packaged and finally tested by means of wire bonding. The measured results are consistent with the simulation results.

articleTitle: A dual-band power amplifier with simultaneously controllable bandwidth
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band impedance matching method is proposed and applied to the design of dual-band power amplifier. The proposed impedance matching network can control the bandwidth of two operating bands simultaneously through network parameters, achieving an asymmetric controllable bandwidth with one wide and one narrow. Additionally, harmonic control is added to the output matching network to enhance the performance of the power amplifier. For demonstration, a dual-band power amplifier was designed and manufactured using the CREE CGH40010F gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor(GaN HEMT). The measurement results show that the drain efficiency of the power amplifier at 2.0 GHz and 3.3 GHz reaches 69.7% and 73.5% respectively, the gain exceeds 10.5 dB for both frequency bands and the output power is greater than 40 dBm. This verifies the design of a low band range with 400 MHz bandwidth and a high band range with 100 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband, Miniature Microstrip Antenna with High Dielectric Constant based on Non-Foster Circuit Matching
abstract: In this paper, a non-Foster circuit with a balun transformer is designed to match a high dielectric constant microstrip antenna. This circuit uses Linvill's floating negative impedance transformer, which generates negative impedance to offset the reactive component of the antenna and enhances the antenna's real resistance for improved matching. Simulation validation of the designed antenna and circuit is performed using HFSS and ADS. The microstrip antenna loaded with dielectric constant of 44 only has a relative bandwidth of 0.5%. With the help of non-Foster circuit matching, the relative bandwidth is increased to 55%, ranging from 440 MHz to 780 MHz, and a maximum gain enhancement of 11.7 dB is achieved. The overall volume of the microstrip antenna is 0.04λ×0.05λ×0.002λ, where λ is the wavelength at the lowest frequency.

articleTitle: Harmonic Beam Manipulation Using A Guided-Wave-Excited Space-Time Digital Coding Metasurface
abstract: This paper proposes a guided-wave-excited space-time digital coding metasurface (STCDM) for harmonic beam scanning and independent multi-harmonic beam control. To realize real-time control of the STCDM, the element composed of the round complementary electric-LC-coupled resonator (cELC) structure and a PIN diode is carefully designed. The space-time modulation scheme for harmonic beam manipulation is introduced based on the 1-bit amplitude switching of each unit cell. The 8×30 metasurface array is fabricated and measured. Stimulated by a 26 GHz RF signal, the STCDM accurately steers the +1st harmonic from 0° to 45° with other harmonics lower by almost 10 dB and independently controls the +1st and +3rd harmonic pointing in different directions, indicating its potential applications in broadband and sideband-free wireless communication platforms.

articleTitle: Bandpass Filters Based on Novel "Γ"-Shape Coaxial Resonator Coupling Structures
abstract: This paper introduces a novel structure of "Γ"-shaped coaxial resonator (ΓSCR), achieved by bending the conventional coaxial structure at a 90-degree angle, aiming to achieve a more compact and easily controllable of electric and magnetic coupling. The ΓSCR structure not only enables electric coupling and magnetic coupling but also possesses flexible adjustability. The coupling degree can be controlled simply by adjusting the distance between resonators, without the need for additional external circuitry control. This study presents a novel design of a four-pole bandpass filter (BPF) utilizing the ΓSCRs. The BPF is centered at 1.02 GHz with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 6.32%. Additionally, transmission zeros (TZs) are strategically placed at 0.95 GHz and 1.08 GHz for demonstration purposes. Theoretical responses from the coupling matrix are provided for comparison, showing excellent agreement with simulated responses.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Residual Phase Noise Measurement of Microwave Amplifiers Using Interferometric Measurement System
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates a prototype of an interferometric residual phase noise measurement system operating at 10 GHz. Employing a carrier suppression and noise amplification scheme, the system achieves a high sensitivity of 25 dBV/rad, which is calibrated using an innovative two-source frequency offset method.
