The experimental results reveal this measurement system exhibits a flicker noise floor of -143dBrad<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Hz@10Hz and a white noise floor of 170 dBrad<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Hz @ 100kHz. These parameters prove to be adequate for the precise evaluation of ultra-low residual phase noise microwave amplifiers. The paper also conducts measurements of some commercial low residual phase noise amplifiers to verify the phase noise mechanisms in amplifiers, which is essential for evaluating the performance of the system phase noise in construction of ultra-low phase noise applications.

articleTitle: Terahertz Frequency Doubler Combiner Module
abstract: In this paper, a novel terahertz frequency doubler utilizing spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) transmission line for high-isolated waveguide T-junction divider is proposed. Utilizing the natural stopband characteristic of metal nickel-based SSPPs with perfect absorptivity for the terahertz wave, which can be employed as a matched load for the waveguide T-junction divider to achieve high-isolation between the output ports. Furthermore, by combining two Terahertz Monolithic Integrated Circuits (TMICs) in two T-junction dividers, we proposed a waveguide-based terahertz frequency doubler. The result shows that the doubler we proposed has a broad bandwidth from 170GHz to 220GHz, an excellent output power of 41mW and converting efficiency with a maximum 10.3%, and has a high isolation between two output ports, indicating the potential value of using SSPPs in terahertz devices.

articleTitle: A Multi-Octave Millimeter-Wave Power Combiner Using Rectangular Coaxial Transmission Line
abstract: A multi-octave power combining structure based on rectangular coaxial transmission line (RCTL) is presented in this paper. In this structure, a tapered transition T-junction is employed for power combining, while the operating bandwidth is extended to cover multiple octaves by introducting multistage impedance transformation. A suspended structure is adopted for the inner conductor, which minimizes the dielectric loss and improves the power handling. Utilizing this technology, a prototype of four-way combiner with simulated power combining capacity of 2kW was designed and fabricated. According to the measured results, the insertion and reflection loss is better than -0.5dB and -15dB, respectively, along with excellent amplitude and phase balance.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Millimeter-wave Patch-based Power Divider Using SISL-based Metasubstrate
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized millimeter power divider with a right-angle isosceles triangle patch based on the substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) platform that fills the air cavity using metasubstrate is proposed. A dumbbell-type metasubstrate is designed with an effective permittivity of 6.57 and an effective permeability of 0.83 near the operating frequency of 27 GHz. The simulated return loss is better than 15 dB from 26.4 GHz to 28.1 GHz. At the same time, the inclusion of metasubstrate reduces the volume of the power divider to 0.28λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>×0.28λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>×0.14λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. The proposed power divider has significant advantages such as miniature size and self-packaging.

articleTitle: Novel Low-Profile Folded Transmitarray Antenna Based on Metasurface for Millimeter-Wave Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a novel low-profile folded transmitarray antenna based on a metasurface. The antenna structure comprises two metasurface arrays and a microstrip antenna serving as the feed source. The bottom metasurface transforms the linearly polarized incident wave emitted from the feed source into a cross-polarized reflected wave, while the upper metasurface, featuring a polarizing grid, achieves full reflection of specific linearly polarized waves and complete transmission of another linearly polarized wave. The folding of the wave path between the transmit array and the reflect array significantly reduces the profile height from the original 2.85λ to 0.95λ, as compared to traditional structures. Simulation results confirm its excellent performance, achieving a gain of 20.1 dBi at the central frequency of 11 GHz with an aperture efficiency of 30.9%.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Transmission Line Model of Temperature-Dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance Effect Based on Coplanar Waveguide
abstract: In this paper, we extract some transmission line parameters from experimental data based on microstrip line theory that can be used to describe the YIG ferromagnetic resonance phenomenon under coplanar waveguide (CPW) excitation conditions. The change of YIG ferromagnetic resonance phenomenon can be accurately reflected from the change of αd when the temperature changes.

articleTitle: An Efficient DNN/ML Training Approach for Designing Metasurfaces
abstract: Deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) techniques have revolutionized the design and optimization of metamaterials, expediting these processes significantly. Nevertheless, their efficacy hinges on vast amounts of pre-existing datasets essential for training designated DL/ML networks, a task notorious for its time-intensive nature. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel approach grounded in an equivalent transmission line circuit model. This method aims to efficiently and precisely generate the requisite training datasets for DL/ML network training. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated through the utilization of a three-layer metallic/dielectric metasurface in conjunction with a deep neural network (DNN), yielding promising results.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Polarized End-Fire Phased Array Antenna With Zero Ground Clearance for 5G mm-Wave Mobile Terminals
abstract: A compact dual-polarized end-fire phased array antenna with zero ground clearance is presented for 5G mm-wave mobile terminals. A double-layer twisted substrate integrated waveguide with a plated through hole fence is developed for vertical polarization, and the microstrip line-fed dipole is further integrated to produce horizontal polarization. Both are capable of covering the n257 and n261 bands, while no ground clearance is required. A compact 1 × 4 phased array is constructed with the antenna length and element spacing of only 2.65 mm and 5.5 mm. The realized gain reaches 9.7 dBi for both polarizations and the 3-dB beam steering range is ±45°.

articleTitle: Analysis and Mitigation of Transmitter Nonlinearity Effects on FBMC Signals
abstract: This paper investigates the performance enhancement of wireless transmitters driven by Filter Bank Multi-Carrier (FBMC) signals using digital pre-distortion (DPD) techniques. The study explores the superiority of FBMC over Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) in terms of spectral efficiency and error performance. Extensive measurements are conducted on a base station transmitter, employing both memory-less and memory polynomial DPD models to analyze the impact of non-linearity and memory on FBMC and OFDM signals. Experimental results demonstrate that DPD significantly improves Adjacent Channel Power Ratio (ACPR) and Error Vector Magnitude (EVM), thereby enhancing Power Amplifier (PA) efficiency. The study provides valuable insights for designers in selecting appropriate waveforms and DPD algorithms to achieve desired performance metrics in wireless communications.

articleTitle: Broadband 3D-Printed Dielectric Rod Antenna with a Flat Peak Gain Over a Wide Bandwidth
abstract: This paper presents a broadband 3D-printed dielectric rod antenna, which is fed by an N-type coaxial connector that excites a ridge waveguide as the feed source. The impedance bandwidth can cover the 6-16 GHz range. By controlling the width, length, and cross-sectional shape of the dielectric rod, the transmission of electromagnetic waves on the rod can be manipulated, thereby achieving a flat gain variation over a wide frequency band. Test results show that the proposed 3D printed dielectric rod antenna has a gain of more than 10 dBi in the 6-16 GHz (90.9%) range, with a peak gain reaching 14.9dBi. And the gain variation is less than 2.5 dB in the 7.8-16 GHz (68.9%) range. The efficiency of the antenna is higher than 50% in the 6-16 GHz range. The proposed antenna offers advantages of low cost, ease of fabrication, ultra-wide bandwidth, and flat gain, and exhibits promising applications in wireless communication, and microwave measurement systems.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency 10W S/C-band GaN HEMT Power Amplifier in Quasi-MMIC Technology
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized and high-efficiency quasi-monolithic microwave integrated circuit (Q-MMIC) power amplifier operating in the frequency range of S/C-band is designed and fabricated. The power amplifier features heterogeneous integration of GaN-based power transistors, using a 0.25-um GaN-HMET process, and GaAs-based passive matching circuits, utilizing a high breakdown voltage GaAs-IPD proess. High gain is achieved through two-stage circuits application, and the mathing circuits and the power tansistors are bonded with gold wire, mounted on a 8 mm × 15 mm flanged molybdenum copper metal carrier plate. The test results show that the power amplifier can be achieved in the 2.8-4.2 GHz frequency band with power gain of 21dB, saturated power of 41 dBm and power added efficiency of about 55%. The perfect combination of high performance of a power amplifier and miniaturization integration is realized.

articleTitle: Wideband Filtering Antenna with Wide Suppression Band Based on Stacked Circular Patches
abstract: One wideband filtering antenna with wide rejection band based on circular patch is proposed in this paper. The filtering antenna consists of two circular patches, two short pins and a pair of half-mode slots. The stacked circular patch not only greatly improves the impedance bandwidth of the antenna, but also achieves a wide suppression band in the high stopband by using the high order modes of the circular patch. Without affecting the radiation mode, the antenna achieves a low stopband filtering effect by adding two pins and a pair of slots. The filtering antenna has the characteristics of wide bandwidth and wide out-of-band suppression. The measured results show that the operating frequency band of the filtering antenna is 2.05GHz-2.79GHz, and the maximum gain is 8.09dBi. The out-of-band suppression level in the lower stopband (1.2-1.8GHz) is more than 20dB, and the out-of-band suppression in the upper stopband (3.2-5.4GHz) is more than 15dB.

articleTitle: A High Gain SISL MIMO Antenna Array with Enhanced Bandwidth Using a Defected Ground Structure
abstract: A multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) substrate-integrated suspended line antenna using a defected ground structure (DGS) is presented for bandwidth enhancement. By incorporating a pair of oblique slots (slots A) on a rectangular stacked patch and employing a defected ground structure (DGS) on top of the sub#5, the proposed antenna demonstrates good impedance matching over a wide bandwidth of 38% (3.81–5.6 GHz) covering various communication bands such as 5G (4.8–5.0 GHz), 5.2 GHz WLAN (5. 15–5.35 GHz), and HiSWANa (5.15–5.25 GHz). The antenna has overall dimensions of 2.17 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.95 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.09 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength. It exhibits favorable radiation characteristics and offers high gain ranging from 7.2 to 13 dBi with a good front-to-back ratio better than 20 dB. A very low envelope correlation coefficient (< 0.07) is also obtained. The results indicate that the proposed approach performs effectively with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Compact Frequency Reconfigurable Cavity-Backed Antenna Based on Dielectric Fluids With Self-Diplexing Property
abstract: A highly-isolated compact cavity-backed frequency reconfigurable antenna employing dielectric fluids with self-diplexing property is presented. The proposed antenna is implemented using two adjacent half-mode substrate-integrated rectangular cavities, radiating slots, microstrip feed lines, and fluidic vias. A detailed explanation is provided for better understanding of the radiation mechanism, self-diplexing property, and tuning process. The frequency reconfigurable is achieved by pouring different dielectric liquids into the fluidic packets. The realization and optimization of the antenna structure are carried out using Ansys HFSS software. The proposed antenna occupies a compact footprint area of ${\text{0}}{\text{.09}}\lambda _g^2$. The proposed antenna allows a tuning of 3.5–4.09 GHz and 6.0–6.98 GHz at lower and upper frequency bands with isolations varies of 49.4–49.7 dB and 38.2–44.6 dB, respectively. Additionally, the front-to-back-ratios and cross-polarization levels of the antenna are greater than –18 dB and –20 dB at all the frequency bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Near-Field-Focused Antenna Implemented by Passive Metasurfaces
abstract: This paper introduces a mechanically reconfigurable variable-focus near-field-focused (NFF) antenna implemented by passive metasurfaces. The proposed system works at 15 GHz and consists of two passive metasurfaces (MS), an array antenna, and a feed network, adopting a folded reflectarray antenna (FRA) profile. Different from active reconfigurable structures, its reconfigurable capability stems from the concept of the Alvarez lens, enabling a variable focal length between 86 mm and 220 mm in the vertical direction by transversely adjusting the relative position. Our mechanism presents a departure from existing variable-focus NFF antennas, offering fresh perspectives for further NFF antenna systems. The proposed design methodology is validated through numerical simulation and experimentation.

articleTitle: 0.5-8.5 GHz Cryogenic Low Power Consumption Amplifiers for Superconducting SIS Mixer-based Water Vapour Radiometer Applications
abstract: An ultra-wideband cryogenic-low-noise-amplifier (CLNA) was designed, fabricated and measured at the ambient temperature of 290K and 4K respectively. The amplifier exhibits a typical gain of 33±1.5dB and an average noise of 8.8K with total power consumption of 4mW at the temperature of 4K. To verify the feasibility of the cryogenic amplifier for the 183GHz water vapour radiometer based on superconducting Superconductor-Insulator-Superconductor (SIS) mixer, we measured the performance of the water vapour radiometer front-end using the amplifier following the SIS mixer as well, resulting in the average noise temperature of the radiometer front-end is about 110K. All the results indicated that the 0.5-8.5GHz CLNA developed in this paper makes it suitable for the radiometer and other application of radio astronomy, space science, atmospheric science and so on.

articleTitle: Magnetoelectric Dipole Filtering Antenna with High Out-of-Band Suppression Level for 5G Application
abstract: A magnetoelectronic dipole filtering antenna achieving high out-of-band suppression is introduced in this letter. Distinguishing from traditional magneto-electric (ME) dipole antennas, the antenna studied in this paper fed by short-circuited SIR (Stepped Impedance Resonator) microstrip line aperture-coupled excitation. Through this approach, the antenna possesses a radiation null below the passband, and combining with the inherent radiation null of the ME dipole, yields an admirable filtering response at lower band edge. The electric dipole is excited by four driven stubs connected with the short wall. The coupling capacitance and parasitic inductance introduced by driven stubs can be equivalent to a low-pass filter network, thereby introducing a radiation null at a higher frequency. Simulation results indicate that the antenna has a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 48.2% (2.99–4.89 GHz), an out-of-band suppression level higher than 20.7 dB.With its flat in-band gain and proficient band suppression capability, the antenna can be applied to 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Compact True Time Delay Unit Based on 8-Shape Transformer
abstract: In this work, a novel design method for achieving ultra-compact on-chip true time delay (TTD) unit is presented. The proposed TTD unit is constructed by cascading two series-inductor all-pass networks (SIAPNs) and two series-capacitor all-pass networks (SCAPNs). By appropriately optimizing the delay slope of each SIAPN and SCAPN, a flat time delay within a wide operating frequency range is successfully achieved. Moreover, different from other reported works, the proposed TTD unit in this work is implemented using 8-shape transformer and 8-shape inductor. By making use of the self-canceled coupling features of 8-shape transformers, the required inductors in each APN are embedded together, leading to an ultra-small circuit size. The proposed TTD unit is designed and implemented using 65 nm CMOS process. Numerical results show that the proposed TTD unit can achieve a size reduction of 44.7 % when compared to conventional artificial transmission line (ATL), while maintaining a small delay variation and reasonable insertion loss level.

articleTitle: Wide-beam Circularly Polarization Antenna Based on Three-dimensional Slots
abstract: This paper presents a wide beam circular polarization (CP) antenna based on 3D slots. Four cuboids are used to construct horizontal and vertical radiation slots. The slots are fed by crossed branches. Adjusting the width and height of the cuboid to distribute the radiation energy in the horizontal and zenith direction could flexibly tune the circularly polarized beamwidth . In this article, the antenna operating around 2 GHz, and the 3-dB axis ratio beamwidth is -87 degree to 82 degree. This antenna is suitable for vehicle-mounted or airborne satellite communications

articleTitle: Huygens Metasurface-Based Transmit-Reflect-Array with Wideband Bi-directional Independent Beam Control for W-Band Applications
abstract: A novel design of Huygens metasurface (HMS)-based transmit-reflect-array (TRA) with bidirectional radiation is proposed. The proposed W-band TRA shows high aperture efficiency of 40.92%/45.31% and wide bandwidth of 13.6%/23.8% in reflection/transmission radiation simultaneously. Compared with conventional HMS-based TRA, higher efficiency and wider bandwidth are achieved within a low profile of 0.144 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. More importantly, efficient independent beam coverage can be realized in both radiation directions. Therefore, owing to the features of high-efficiency, wide-bandwidth and low-profile, the proposed TRA becomes a promising candidate for bidirectional wireless communication applications in high millimeter-wave band.

articleTitle: RFID-Based Unobtrusive Pedestrian Identification Using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Nowadays, there is a wide variety of pedestrian recognition approaches, such as using visual or voice features. Although these approaches have great accuracy, they are also prone to privacy issues or require extra attention. This study offers an RFID-based unobtrusive pedestrian identification, which employs a 6×6 tag array to collect the phase angle and received signal strength indicator (RSSI) differences produced by body size and movement pattern of different individuals as they walk by, providing biometric information for identification. Due to the advantages of convolutional neural network (CNN) in feature extraction, we employ it in combination with the squeeze-and-excitation block to develop a deep learning model. Our model achieves 99.4% accuracy in the classification of 660 samples from 11 classes.

articleTitle: A 54-67-GHz Low-Power Highly-Integrated Transceiver in 65-nm CMOS for FMCW Radar Applications
abstract: This paper presents a 54-67 GHz highly-integrated transceiver fabricated in 65-nm CMOS for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar applications. It consists of a frequency synthesizer, a transmit (Tx) channel, and three receive (Rx) channels. The proposed current-sharing low-noise amplifier (LNA) and injection-locking-based frequency multiplier (FM) facilitate low-power operation. Besides, a class-B-biased mixer is proposed to enhance conversion gain and linearity with low power consumption. The chip achieves a peak Tx output power of 13.1 dBm, a Rx conversion gain (CG) of 25-74 dB, a minimum Rx noise figure (NF) of 8.4 dB at 5 MHz IF frequency across 54-67 GHz. The measured phase noise (PN) is -95.5 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset at 60 GHz. The entire chip occupies 2.8 × 4.78 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area and consumes 385 mW.

Index Terms: For Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Radar

articleTitle: A DC-54 GHz 5-bit Attenuator with Sub-0.35 dB/2.9° RMS Amplitude/Phase Errors in 0.18-μm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband digital attenuator using hybrid topology and capacitive phase compensation method, which achieves high amplitude control precision and low phase shifts from DC to 54 GHz in 0.18-μm SiGe BiCMOS technology. The parasitic effect of the switch transistor and capacitive phase compensation for high-band response improvement are visualized and analyzed. A maximum attenuation of 15.5 dB is achieved with a step of 0.5 dB. Simulated results show the insertion loss (IL) of the attenuator is 4.25-9.35 dB and the RMS amplitude/phase errors are less than 0.35 dB/2.9° over the operating frequency. While the return losses of all 32 states are better than 10 dB with a compact core area of 0.046 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Hologram Based on An Origami Metasurface
abstract: In this research, a single-layer passive metasurface structure is designed for reconfigurable hologram imaging. This design relies on an origami-inspired structure that can be manipulated through stretching and compressing. This approach contrasts with other multi-layer metasurfaces that utilize the complex FPGA active circuits. Different folding angles, specifically 5° or 35°, impart distinct configurations to the origami metasurfaces, resulting in the formation of distinct images denoted as 'Z' or 'J'. Regardless the folding angles are set at 5° or 35°, the transmission phase of origami unit cells is close to the Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase. Additionally, the cross-polarized transmission linear amplitude of origami supercells also could remain consistently above 0.35 in the frequency band of 15 GHz to 17 GHz. The metasurface comprises a total of 1600 meta-atoms arranged in a 40 × 40 array. A Diffractive optical network approach is utilized to optimize the compensation phases of 1600 elements essential for generating transmissive hologram images. Upon incidence of a right-handed circular polarized plane wave onto the origami metasurface structure, images resembling the letters 'Z' or 'L' are generated on the imaging plane. Validation of these results is conducted through simulations using the commercial electromagnetic software CST Studio Suite.

articleTitle: An 18-to-39 GHz SPDT Switch with AC-floating Technology Achieving < 2.0-dB Insertion Loss
abstract: This letter presents an 18-to-39 GHz low-insertion-loss single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch. Adopted triple-well NMOS transistors, the proposed switch utilizes low-loss Π-network and AC-floating technology to improve the insertion loss. Fabricated in 0.13-μm SiGe BiCMOS, the proposed switch achieves an insertion loss of less than 2.0 dB and an isolation of better than 16.5 dB in the frequency range of 18-39 GHz. The measured input 1 dB compression point of the proposed switch is 11.7 dBm, and the chip-core area of the proposed SPDT switch is 0.138 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-band RCS Reduction in Microstrip Antenna Based on AMC Structure
abstract: Based on the working principle of artificial magnetic conductor (AMC), a coaxial feed microstrip antenna is designed to effectively reduce radar cross section (RCS) in three frequency bands. This innovative design takes advantage of the phase cancellation phenomenon between the AMC and perfect electric conductor (PEC). The AMC unit is meticulously engineered to achieve a reflection phase difference of 180° ± 37° compared to PEC unit. To achieve this phase cancellation effect, a checker-board arrangement structure is employed in the AMC design. Through simulation experiments, it has been demonstrated that this design allows for significant reduction in RCS across the L-band, C-band, and X-band frequencies. Importantly, this RCS reduction is achieved without compromising the original antenna's radiation performance.

articleTitle: A D-Band 28-nm CMOS Differential Low-Noise Amplifier with Transformer-Based Broadband Matching Network Applied for 6G Receiver
abstract: This letter presents a 118-170 GHz low-noise amplifier (LNA) fabricated in 28-nm bulk CMOS applied for high-speed 6G receiver. The broadband high gain of the 5-stage common-source(CS) LNA is achieved by transformer-based matching network with common-mode suppression. The sensible connection of compact transistor layout is utilized to reduce parasitic effect and noise figure. More than 19.3 dB gain with a peak of 25.3 dB at 130 GHz can be presented and the simulated minimum noise figure (NF) can reach 6.8 dB. The IP1dB of -23 dBm and the consumption of 47.7 mW are achieved, which occupies an area of 0.49×0.81 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with pads.

articleTitle: A Robust Decentralized Routing Protocol for Airborne Networks with Directional Antennas
abstract: Airborne networks (ANs) are always faced with the challenge of anti-jamming communications due to a lack of physical boundaries. A robust decentralized routing (RDR) protocol is proposed in this paper for ANs with directional antennas in the content of the network layer. The routing centrality is first defined and its correlation with the network topology is investigated. Accordingly, a novel weight assignment mechanism is proposed to make the central node less often appear on a routing path. In this way, the failure rate of routing can be decreased once the central node is disconnected. Based on simulation results, the routing centrality of the central node can be reduced from 39.6% to 21.8% while the average end-to-end delay (EED) is slightly increased.

articleTitle: A Unified 77/79GHz Low-Profile Digital Code Modulation (DCM) Automotive Radar Aiming at Mass Production
abstract: Starting from the proof-of-concept phase in the 1960s, millimeter-wave automotive radar officially unlocked the prelude to its successful commercialization in the early of 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century. Although various modulation regimes were proposed from research aspects based on technology upgrade within recent years, frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) has still dominated as the most reliable automotive qualified solution basis with fair price for radar suppliers. Tens of millions of automotive millimeter-wave radars are produced each year to meet increasing demand of advanced driver assistant system (ADAS) and autonomous driving (AD) functions. Mainly concerned of interference that more and more FMCW radars on road could cause, digital code modulation (DCM) radar chipset as one of phase modulation (PM) regime has been developed, verified, and commercialized since 2022. This work extensively introduces the design, implementation, and verification of the first 77/79 GHz automotive radar based on DCM chipset toward serious mass production, which could lead the commercialization of the DCM automotive radar in visible future. The implemented DCM radar combines the traditional front and corner radars together as a unified version with a compact size of 40 mm×126 mm×32 mm, achieving wide field-of-view (FoV) of 120°, maximum detection range of 218 m for a target of 10 dBsm radar cross section (RCS), and a natural angular resolution of 1.6°on azimuth plane. A preliminary on-vehicle test showed, that steady tracking of object on high way scenario under rainy weather can fulfil requirements of driving functions such as adaptive cruise control (ACC) and automatic emergency braking system (AEBS).

articleTitle: A Colinearly Polarized Full-Duplex Antenna With High Tx-Rx Isolation Using Resonance Technology
abstract: A colinearly polarized full-duplex antenna with high Tx-Rx isolation using resonance technology is presented for full-duplex application. A low profile antenna is designed where the Tx and Rx use the same radiation patch. Based on resonance technology, a microstrip antenna with double resonators and metallic vias is designed to achieve high isolation. The I-shaped slots etched from the ground plane further adjust the bandwidth and improve isolation. The overall size of the final design is 0.74λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×1.29λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.03λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free-space wavelength at 6.5 GHz operational frequency). The simulation results exhibit a 10 dB return loss bandwidth of 3.4 % (6.39–6.62 GHz). The proposed microstrip antenna demonstrates the isolation of 67.7 dB at 6.5 GHz operating frequency, along with peak realized gain of 7.4 dBi.

articleTitle: C-Band 15 W Power Amplifier MMIC with Second Harmonic Suppression for Radar Network Application
abstract: This paper presents a C-band 15 W power amplifier(PA)microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) based on 0.25 μm gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) process in order to satisfy the application requirements of radar networks for high efficiency and high second harmonic suppression (SHS) of power amplifiers. A two-stage amplifier structure is employed, and second harmonic suppression topology is incorporated in the output-matching network to enhance high harmonic suppression. The harmonic control technology is used to improve efficiency. Adopted multi-pole reactance matching network is used to expand the bandwidth of amplifier and reduce inserting loss. The measurement results show that, in 5 GHz~6 GHz, the PA delivers a small signal gain larger than 28 dB, and a saturated output power of 15 W with the max additional power efficiency (PAE) of 64%, the harmonic suppression exceeds 40 dBc. The size of the PA is 3.0 mm×2.1 mm. This PA has widespread application prospect.

articleTitle: Design of a Five-Channel Circulator-Coupled C band Multiplexer Using Dielectric Resonators and Coaxial Filters
abstract: In this paper, a five-channel C-band circulator-coupled multiplexer (CCM) using dielectric resonators (DRs) and coaxial channel filters is designed and tested. DRs are used to achieve miniaturization and high performance in narrow band filter, while coaxial filter is used in wide band situation, which is with low Q-value requirements. The spurious mode effects of the channel filters are discussed in detail for the first time, and two principles are proposed: one is that channels with "unclean" modes should be placed at the rear of the signal, and the other is that for spurs that cannot be eliminated, an "accept out-of-band" strategy should be adopted. The test results is highly consistent with the simulations, verifying the effectiveness of the design and analysis.

articleTitle: A high linearity and high efficiency C-band power amplifier utilizing third-order intermodulation component cancellation
abstract: A C-band high linearity and high efficiency MMIC power amplifier (PA) was designed and implemented using the 0.25 μm advanced GaN HEMT process. By appropriately adjusting the gate bias voltage of transistors, the mitigation of the third-order intermodulation component can be accomplished. The individual gate voltages, VG1 and VG2, are combined into a unified gate voltage input, VG, through a voltage divider network. Building on this foundation, by judiciously determining the fundamental impedance and harmonic impedance, the amplifier not only exhibits high linearity but also demonstrates notable additional power efficiency. The designed chip occupies an area of 5.94 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, with test results demonstrating that within the range of 3.0-5.0 GHz under continuous wave testing conditions, it achieves an average power gain exceeding 24 dB, a saturated output power within the range of 40.0-41.3 dBm, and a peak saturation Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of 63.5%. When tested under two-tone signal conditions at 3.7 GHz, 4.0 GHz, and 4.2 GHz with an output power of 36 dBm, the third-order intermodulation distortion (IMD3) ≤ -30 dBc, while the PAE ≥ 30%.

articleTitle: A Novel Slow-Wave Substrate Integrated Suspended Slot Line
abstract: This paper proposes a novel slow-wave substrate integrated suspended slot line (SW-SISSL), which puts slotline inside a metallic shielding enclosure to resolve the packaging problem and reduce the radiation loss. By using the microstrip-to-slotline transition, the slow-wave slotline is compared with the uniform slotline, good slow-wave characteristic is achieved over a wide frequency. The uniform and slow-wave slotline circuits are designed by using the printed circuit board (PCB) process. Three designs are fabricated and measured to verify the slow-wave characteristic and feasibility.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Rasorber With Elliptic Filtering Response
abstract: This work proposes a three-layer frequency selective rasorber (FSR) architecture that facilitates switchable wide-passband in wide low-reflection bands and state-of-the-art elliptic filtering response in the passband. First, a passive FSR model is designed to validate the bandwidth expansion capabilities of the proposed three-layer architecture. The simulations and measurements confirm the passive device exhibits wideband low reflection and passband characteristics. Second, by integrating multi-path electromagnetic coupling into a switchable frequency selective surface (FSS) design, multiple transmission zeros are excited in the out-of-band region. Therefore, the final device is composed by sequentially layering non-switchable and switchable impedance layers on this FSS. Simulation results indicate that the device possesses a narrow passband with elliptical filter response, capable of switching from a rasorbering state to an absorbing state.

articleTitle: Efficient Design and Implementation of On-Chip Low-Temperature Superconducting Filter with Wide Bandwidth and Sharp Selectivity
abstract: This paper presents an effective method for designing and implementing low-temperature superconducting (LTS) filters on-chip, offering wide bandwidth and sharp selectivity via transmission zeros (TZs). The technique involves extracting an in-line bandpass model using a general matrix synthesis method, comprising cascaded lumped sections. Note that all circuit elements (inductances and capacitances) are derived from a reactance matrix directly, thus allowing convenient adjustment for compact realization through a 4-layer niobium (Nb) process. Additionally, a practical mechanism for layout implementation is introduced, aiding in the physical dimensioning of wideband filters with multiple TZs near the passband. A fifth-order wide-band filter operating between 3.5-6.5 GHz with three assigned TZs is demonstrated to validate the approach. The implementation procedure confirms desired in-band and out-of-band performances through simulation and test responses in a 4.2 K environment.

articleTitle: A Compact Low Spurious Superheterodyne Transceiver Module Based on PCB Stacking Structure for Multi-band Communication System
abstract: This paper proposes A low-cost, high-density integrated transceiver module with two-stage superheterodyne architecture based on PCB stacking structure. Firstly, a reasonable compartmentalized design is applied to various functional circuits within the module, achieving high-density integration. Additionally, EM simulation is conducted for the distribution of the isolation solder balls between the PCBs, ensuring a high isolation between different functional circuits. Furthermore, two-stage FBAR filters with an out of band rejection of more than 40dBc are used to enhance the suppression for the intermodulation distortion of the transceiver. A transceiver module prototype has been designed, fabricated and tested. The intermodulation suppression is 64 dBc, and the size of the module is 10.5 × 18 × 3.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed transceiver module has the characteristics of miniaturization, low cost and high isolation, which can be used for multi-band high performance communication systems.

articleTitle: A 2.8-to-7.3 GHz Quad-Mode QVCO Achieving 205.9 dBc/Hz FoMTA in 55nm CMOS
abstract: This work describes a transformer-resonator based quad-mode quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (QM-QVCO), which improves the frequency tuning range (FTR) and phase noise (PN). We also utilize the diode-connected network to achieve in-phase coupling in the QM-QVCO without deteriorating tank Q. Besides, the resistance of mode-selection switches is ignored. Thus, the wide FTR and low PN are realized simultaneously. The QM-QVCO is manufactured in 55-nm CMOS, which occupies a core area of 0.318 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and exhibits an FTR of 88.8%. The measured best PN is −120.2 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset, corresponding to a peak FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TA</inf> of 205.9 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method to Simplify the Design of a Broadband High-Efficiency Load Modulated Balanced Amplifier
abstract: The motivation of this work is to simplify broadband high-efficiency load modulated balanced amplifier (LMBA) designs with the aid of a standalone control amplifier (CA) and two standalone balanced amplifiers (BAs). Based on the operation principle of a LMBA, the proposed method firstly derives the saturated current ratio and load impedances on the coupler plane, and then calculates the desired phase shift, and finally optimizes the phase shift of the CA for enhanced efficiency across a broad band. To validate the proposed optimization method, a 2.0-2.8 GHz LMBA is fabricated and tested. Measurements show that the LMBA realizes the drain efficiency (DE) of 47.7%-83.5% at saturation, 48.8%-65.3% at 6-dB power back-off, moreover, 36.5%-45.7% at 10-dB power back-off across the whole band.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characterization of Materials Based on Genetic Algorithm and Prior Knowledge
abstract: This paper proposes a method for extracting the complex permittivity of materials, utilizing genetic algorithm optimization and prior knowledge. S-parameters of the grounded coplanar waveguide with an upper cover containing the material under test are obtained through simulation in CST. Then, the genetic algorithm optimization procedure of a finite element method (FEM) software is utilized to minimize the difference between the simulated S-parameters from CST and FEM. Finally, the possible optimal values of the permittivity are searched iteratively. The approach can be used to extract material parameters across a wide frequency spectrum. To validate the proposed method, experiments were conducted using pure water as the test material.

articleTitle: A 215-GHz Radial Power Combination System With Multilayer and Contactless Structures
abstract: This paper presents a sub-millimeter wave radial power combination system with multilayer and contactless structures. The system is mainly composed of ${\text{T}}{{\text{E}}_{10}} - {\text{TE}}_{11}^{{\text{CP}}}$ (circular polarized TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) mode converters, the radial power divider and combiner, waveguide-to-microstrip transitions, and eight power amplifier MMICs. The entire system is divided into multiple layers to facilitate passive and active power combination measurements. Furthermore, to simplify the assembly difficulty, and reduce unnecessary losses of waveguide splitting and interconnection, some contactless structures such as groove gap waveguides and waveguide chokes are designed and adopted. In the measurement, the passive radial power divider/combiner achieves a return loss of higher than 14 dB with an average insertion loss of 0.5 dB within 200-260 GHz, the eight-way combined active power amplification system delivers a maximum power of 23.3 dBm (212.4 mW) at 215 GHz. In the band of 207-223 GHz, the output power is higher than 100 mW.

articleTitle: A Self-Powered Environmental Data Sensor Node Based on Efficient RF Power Transfer
abstract: This paper introduces a self-powered environmental data sensor node that relies on the collection of radio frequency (RF) energy transmitted by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). A meticulously designed rectifier circuit not only captures RF energy at 433 MHz but also provides feedback of the second harmonic signal at 866 MHz to the UAV. This feedback mechanism enables antenna alignment, thereby improving energy conversion efficiency. The proposed rectifier circuit exhibits a measured RF-DC conversion efficiency of 22.8% and generates a second harmonic power of -39 dBm at an input power of -20 dBm. It is employed to power a microcontroller which coordinates the sensor to periodically collect environmental data, including temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide concentration. Then the sensing information is transmitted to a mobile terminal using Bluetooth. An antenna calibration experiment was conducted, during which the transmitter successfully received a second harmonic signal of -59.5dBm at a distance of 12 meters from the rectifier. This experiment serves as verification that the proposed rectifier can effectively assist UAVs in achieving efficient wireless power transfer to sensing nodes located at considerable distances.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Using Wide- Beam Magneto-Electric Dipole for C-Band Satellite Communications
abstract: A compact C-band ultra-wideband wide-angle scanning array for satellite communications is investigated in this paper. The radiating element is an ultra-wideband magneto-electric dipole (ME-dipole) exhibits a wide half-power beamwidth (HPBW) in both E and H-planes. In contrast to traditional ME-dipole antenna, the proposed radiating element exhibits a more compact configuration and achieves a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 102% (2.98-9.21 GHz). Additionally, a 1 × 8 linear array is designed, fabricated, and tested, capable of scanning beams that cover territories from -60°to 60°, with a scanning gain loss less than 3dB within 3 to 6 GHz. With the advantages of compact size, ultra-wide bandwidth, and wide-angle scanning performance, it would be appealing for C-band satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: A 22.6-to-73.9 GHz Ultra-Wideband Low-Noise Amplifier With Flat In-band Power Gain in 0.13-µm BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a 22.6-to-73.9 GHz ultra-wideband low-noise amplifier in IHP SG13G2 0.13-µm BiCMOS technology. The proposed LNA comprises two amplifier stages and achieves ultra-wideband performance by utilizing various bandwidth extension techniques, including shunt feedback, peak inductors, and resonant feedback compensation. Simultaneously, it significantly enhances gain flatness and noise figure (NF). The results indicate that the proposed amplifier shows a measured gain of 15.2 dB and a simulated NF ranging from 3.96 to 4.26 dB within the 3-dB bandwidth from 22.6 to 73.9 GHz, respectively. The circuit’s footprint is just 0.18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, encompassing bond pads, and and its power consumption is a modest 17.5 mW, drawn from a 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: Compact Bilayer SIW Filter Based on Novel Annular Coupled Structure
abstract: A compact bilayer SIW filter without blind holes based on a novel annular coupled structure is proposed in this article. The bilayer filter with only through holes simplifies processing and provides a universal miniaturization method to remain performance, by a novel annular coupled structure and optimization from DGS. The proposed annular coupled structure transmits energy through the equivalent electric wall of the SIW by an annular slot etched around the central metallized hole. To confirm the effectiveness of the design, a filter operating at 9.65GHz was fabricated using PCB technology, which have a bandwidth of 13.5%, an insertion loss of 1.34dB, and a size of 1.43λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>×0.95λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>×0.05λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. The measure results are consistent with the simulation, indicating its excellent performance and potential for future miniaturized applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced sensing telemetry using reconstruction of divergent exceptional points with cross-coupling
abstract: We herein introduce a new wireless sensing telemetry with enhanced sensitivity by leveraging the reconstruction of divergent exceptional point (DEP) in a cross-coupled third-order parity-time (PT)-symmetric electronic system. We confirm that with the presence of cross-coupling between the gain and loss components, which was ignored in the previous work, the phenomenon of DEP can still exist. In addition, we theoretically provide the design strategy for building such a system and explicit guidance for reconstructing the DEP. We also demonstrate that such a reconstruction procedure of the cross-coupled DEP can indeed be utilized as the sensing mechanism having unprecedented sensitivity. This work may provide a comprehensive understanding of the DEP benefits of the practical implementation of DEP sensors.

articleTitle: A 94GHz Down-Conversion Mixer with High LO-to-RF Isolation in 130nm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: In this paper, a down-conversion mixer with operating frequency of 88-96GHz is presented. Based on 130nm SiGe BiCMOS process, the mixer has the characteristics of high isolation. The mixer includes a double-balanced Gilbert core, a local oscillator drive amplifier and an intermediate frequency drive amplifier. A single stage differential amplifier is used in the intermediate frequency output to improve the conversion gain. The mixer and drive amplifier use a current mirror for DC bias to reduce the influence of temperature and process on RF performance. The design adds a ground wall between the LO and RF signal lines, which increases the isolation well and optimizes the amplitude phase imbalance of the input and output balun. The measured input 1dB compression point (IP1dB) is -9dBm@95GHz, the peak conversion gain is 9.3dB@88GHz in the frequency range of 88-96GHz, the maximum LO-to-RF isolation is 57.4dB and the LO-to-IF isolation is 67.6dB, and the RF-to-IF isolation is 37.6dB.

articleTitle: A Method to Halve the LUT Size for MPWM-based All Digital Transmitters
abstract: The all-digital transmitter (ADT) based on mapping-base pulse width modulation (MPWM) has the advantages of agile carrier-frequency and low DSP resource consumption. However, when the bit-width of the intermediate frequency (IF) signal increases, the size of look-up table (LUT) increases sharply, which leads to excessive storage resource consumption. This paper proposes a method to reduce the LUT size of MPWM ADT. The principle of the method is explained and the ADT implemention architecture is given. The experiments on field-programmable gate array (FPGA) show that the proposed method can halve the BRAM resources of MPWM ADT, and the ADT performance is comparable to the original one.

articleTitle: A 0.5-0.8 GHz Cryogenic LNA with 0.7 dB NF in 180nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a cryogenic low noise amplifier (LNA) in TSMC 180nm CMOS for silicon spin-based quantum computing. The proposed LNA exploits source degenerate inductive common source structure, which operates well at 300K and 4K. At 300K, the LNA achieves a measured gain (S21) of 15.8 dB and noise factor (NF) of 2 dB at 600 MHz with 117 mW power consumption. At 4K, it attains S21 of 20.8 dB and NF of 0.7 dB at 600 MHz with 52 mW power consumption. The area of the core circuit is 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Active Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons with Integrated Graphene
abstract: In this paper, a graphene-based tunable filter with adjustable bandwidth and amplitude is proposed. The structure of filter consists of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP), controlling the lower and upper cut-off frequencies of the filter, respectively. By integrating monolayer graphene on the surface of SSPP and sweeping the graphene conductivity, the structure of the hybrid filter can be reconfigured, which correspondingly changes the SSPP upper cut-off frequency for bandwidth control. The measurement results of the prototype show that the filter bandwidth changes from 18% to 30%, and the amplitude modulation is larger than 10 dB under a bias voltage from 0 V to 1 V, which has a good agreement with the simulation. The proposed device paves a way to develop graphene-integrated tunable devices at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: 2-bit Dual-polarized Huygens Metasurface for High-order Bessel Beam Generation
abstract: This paper reports a novel approach for the efficient generation of high-order Bessel beams at 28 GHz utilizing 2-bit dual-polarized Huygens metasurface. To verify the feasibility of the scheme, we designed generators for both first-order and second-order Bessel beams using the Huygens metasurface. The full-wave simulations verify that they achieve the mode purity exceeding 80% and 77%, respectively, and non-diffraction spiral phase propagation in a distance of 150mm (about 14 λ at 28 GHz). Our work has the advantages of low fabrication cost and high transmission efficiency, which provides a new avenue for the effective generation of high-order Bessel beams.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Measuring Probe Based on Vivaldi Antenna and Ultra-Thin UWB Absorber
abstract: A novel short pulse measuring probe is proposed in this paper, which is composed of Vivaldi antenna, ultra-thin absorptive layer, and the protecting metal plate. The proposed measuring probe is placed in the near-field of UWB radiation antenna, which can realize fault detection with low disturbance. The absorptive straps in H-plane are used to enhance the bandwidth and the flatness of the equivalent height of the measuring band. The simulation results show that the equivalent height of the combined measuring probe fluctuates less than ± 4.5% in the range of 0.38 to 4.54 GHz, and the group delay fluctuates less than ±0.18 ns in the range of 460 MHz to 6.6 GHz.

articleTitle: A fast method of irregular MIMO antenna far-field pattern based on characteristic mode analysis
abstract: A fast method for calculating the pattern of irregular MIMO antennas based on characteristic mode analysis and coupling matrix is presented in this paper. The radiation characteristics of each antenna are characterized by the characteristic mode analysis, and the interaction between antenna elements is characterized by the establishment of array coupling matrix. Unlike traditional simulation software that requires time-consuming re-modeling for each structural variation, our method only needs to modify the array coupling matrix to quickly solve the array antenna pattern. Two examples of irregular dipole antenna array and patch antenna array are used to verify the method, which demonstrate our method's ability to achieve high precision in significantly less time than conventional methods.

articleTitle: An enhanced dry-wet hybrid cyclic etching method for high resistance Si (111) based AlInGaN/GaN heterojunction epitaxy: comparison on various etching process
abstract: An enhanced dry-wet hybrid cyclic etching technology based on oxygen plasma and hydrochloric acid is developed on high resistance (HR) Si (111)-AlInGaN/GaN heterojunction epitaxy. The process of one circle of dry-wet hybrid is as that applying a plasma degumming machine for 2 min with oxygen flow of 1L/min and RF power of 60W to treat the sample surface and then placing the sample in dilute hydrochloric acid soak in (HCl: H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O = 1:10) for 1 min. The etching depth can be adjusted by various etching circles. Compared with the traditional ICP etching and KOH wet etching, the enhanced etching process shows a better performance with stable etching rate of 1.142 nm/cycle, a high etching depth control accuracy within 1nm, and a low etching surface roughness within 0.3nm. The proposed enhanced low-damage quantitative hybrid circling etching method can be applied to the study of ohmic contact etching and recessed gate etching. In addition, the etching process can also be used for surface treatment after dry etching to obtain an etched surface with lower roughness. This etching technology has a wide range of application prospects.

articleTitle: AI-based Antenna Design for fiber-optic-wireless heterogeneous communication in integrated optical cable
abstract: This paper elucidates a directional circularly polarized cross dipole antenna for intelligent optical cable. The antenna is powered by a single feed point and can achieve a 90° phase shift via a quarter-wavelength path. The antenna operates in upstream and downstream bands, 1.98 GHz to 2.01 GHz and 2.17 GHz to 2.20 GHz, respectively. In order to optimize the antenna performance, it is necessary to further improve the parameters such as return loss, axis ratio and gain. However, traditional optimization methods often require an amount of time for full-wave electromagnetic simulation. In order to solve this challenge, artificial neural network proxy model is proposed to replace full-wave electromagnetic simulation for optimization to speed up the optimization process. By training artificial neural networks, the process of developing agent models can be accelerated. The test results show that the antenna can meet the requirement for fiber optic wireless heterogeneous communication in integrated optical cable, and a more efficient method to optimize antenna design is presented.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Scanning Endfire Phased Array Antenna Using Heterogeneous Beam Element Technology
abstract: Heterogeneous beam element (HBE) technology leverages the inherent design degrees of freedom (DoF) in each element pattern shape to strategically arrange HBEs, thereby generating a wide average active element pattern (AAEP) and enabling wide-angle scanning for phased array antennas (PAAs). This work proposes a wide-angle scanning endfire PAA employing HBE technology. Initially, an analysis of HBE technology is conducted using the AAEP method to elucidate its principle. Subsequently, the HBE is realized by tilting the arms of the end-fire dipole, resulting in a tilted beam. Finally, based on this HBE, a 4-element linear endfire HBE PAA is implemented. Simulation results demonstrate that this 4-element HBE PAA extends the scanning range from 60° to 70° across the 24.25-29.5 GHz band compared to its standard counterpart.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Dual-Mode LNA with Improved Dynamic Range in 90nm CMOS SOI Technology
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter wave(mm-wave) low-power dual-mode low noise amplifier (LNA) with gain-switchable technology for improved dynamic range. Multi-tanks transformer is utilized in the inter-stage and output matching network for gain-switchable operation. LNA adopts 3-stages common source (CS) amplifier, and the input matching network of LNA adopts a transformer-based matching network to realize the wideband power and noise matching. LNA is designed in 90nm CMOS SOI technology at a 0.75-V supply voltage (VDD), with a power consumption of only 7.2mW. The post-layout simulation results show that the 3dB bandwidth of LNA is 24.6~35.8GHz, the minimum noise is 2.78dB, the peak power gain is 21 dB in the high gain state, and the gain in the low gain state can be 3.5dB lower than the gain in the high gain state. Thanks to the gain-switchable technology, the input 1dB compression point (IP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>) is -15.1 and -13.1 dBm at 30GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Enabling Single Mode Radiation in Two Bands of a 5G Antenna Using Gyromagnetic Ferrite Substrate
abstract: Gyromagnetic ferrite is typical anisotropic material with tensor permeability. The elements of the matrix are function of operating frequency, that makes effective permeability of gyromagnetic ferrite dispersive. The effective permeability is higher at the lower sideband of the resonant frequency and lower at the higher sideband because of intrinsic properties of the ferrite. This specific phenomenon can make the wavelength in the ferrite dielectric fixed at two different frequencies. By employing Ni-ferrite material as the substrate, the dual-band patch antenna with single radiation mode was proposed working in sub-6-GHz bands. The antenna had uniform operating performance at two different frequencies 2.51 GHz and 4.93 GHz with high efficiency.

articleTitle: A C-Band Four-Channel Receiver with Current-Sharing and Large-Signal Multigated-Transistor Techniques in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a C-band four-channel receiver fabricated in 65-nm CMOS for high-throughput wireless communications. By utilizing a current-sharing technique, the entire chip adopts a single 2-V supply voltage, which simplifies array design. The proposed stacked phase and gain control scheme and active-combining circuit enable a compact layout. The chip achieves a 360° phase shifting range with a 5.625° resolution, and a 19.5-dB attenuation range with a 0.5-dB step. The fabricated prototype demonstrates a single-channel 33-dB gain and a 4.3-dB noise figure (NF) at 5.5 GHz. By using the large-signal multigated-transistor (MGTR) technique, it achieves an input 1-dB gain compression point (IP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>) of −21.8 dBm. The entire chip occupies 2.5 × 2.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area and consumes 334 mW.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Phase Noise on Motion Interferometry with Microwave Radar Sensor
abstract: Microwave radar interferometry shows an advantage in subtle displacement motion detection. The motion interferometry depends on the quality of the radar signals which are inevitably threatened by phase noise. However, few literatures exist regarding the quantitative analysis of the detection limit in the existence of phase noise. This paper proposes a theoretical estimation model of the detection limit based on the correlation of the phase error with the nominal distance. To validate the impact of the phase noise on the detection limit, a custom-designed 5.8 GHz radar transceiver is employed and the best phase error is estimated as 0.014°. Experiments are carried out and the results show that the displacement motion of 80 µm at the nominal distance of 10 cm could be captured with an RMSE of 0.92 µm.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Doherty Power Amplifier with Filtering Matching and Harmonic Suppression
abstract: This letter introduces a Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) with filter matching and harmonic suppression architecture. The integrated design of the filtering networks and the DPA exhibits advantages of improved integration level, lower losses, and higher out-of-band attenuation. The suppression of the second and the third harmonics also improves the efficiency of the DPA. The filtering DPA designed in this letter uses GaN HEMT and can work over the range of 3.2-3.6 GHz. The measured results indicate that the maximum output power of DPA is 43.6-45.1 dBm, with saturated drain efficiency (DE) of 60.1%-65%, and 36.1%-45.9% at the 6 dB power back-off. The measured adjacent channel leakage power ratio (ACLR) is -33.7/-53.14 dB with and without the digital pre-distortion with the 20 MHz long-term-evolution (LTE) signals.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna Based on SIGW
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) metasurface (MTS) antenna based on substrate integrated gap waveguide (SIGW) is proposed in this paper. MTS is composed of four cross patches and a series of square patches. The characteristic mode theory is used to analyze the mode of the proposed antenna, and two characteristic modes with orthogonal and same direction current distribution are selected as the operating modes. Since both modes have wide bandwidth, the proposed MTS antenna can also achieve wide bandwidth. CP characteristics can be achieved by using a spoon-shaped feeding structure and a crossed-slot to excite two modes. Compared with the microstrip structure, the use of SIGW can better suppress the cross-polarization and back lobe of the radiation pattern. The simulation results show that -10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW) of the antenna is 12.42 - 16.07 GHz (25.62%), 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) is 12.92 - 14.53 GHz (11.73%), and the peak gain is 12.9 dBic.

articleTitle: Noncontact Sleep Apnea-hypopnea Events Detection Using a K-band Biomedical Radar
abstract: The golden standard of nocturnal respiratory function assessment is polysomnography (PSG) especially for diagnosis of sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (SAHS). However, the use of PSG sensors usually obstructs the patients' breathing, causing discomfort. One of the most important signals in PSG to assess respiratory function is airflow, especially for sleep apnea detection. Radar-based contactless detection technique provides a non-contact monitor way to overcome such limitation. Aiming at automatic sleep respiratory events detection, a 24-GHz biomedical radar sensor combined with apnea detection algorithm is developed to provide accurate continuous measurement of respiratory waveform during sleep. Through the overnight experiment, the radar data and PSG data were simultaneously recorded. Professional sleep technicians' manual assessments of sleep respiratory events based on PSG data are found to be consistent with results automatically determined using radar data, which makes the at-home monitoring possible in the future.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Dielectric Circularly Polarized Lens Antenna for 5G Millimeter Wave Multibeam Application
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dielectric circularly polarized lens antenna based on 3D printed technology. The lens is composed of multiple inclined fan-shaped structures arranged in a rotation around a central axis, endowing the lens with the capability to convert linearly polarized waves into left-handed circularly polarized waves. Owing to the rotational symmetry of the lens structure about its center, it is capable of achieving highly consistent circularly polarized multi-beam radiation. The lens antenna exhibits a peak gain of 16.3 dBic and an axial ratio less than 3 dB across the frequency range of 30.4 GHz to 40.3 GHz.

articleTitle: An 18-24 GHz Active-Balun-Differential Low Noise Amplifier Based on 45nm SOI CMOS Technology
abstract: An 18-24 GHz active-balun differential-low-noise amplifier (DLNA) implemented in 45-nm silicon-on-insulator (SOI) CMOS technology for wireless communication is presented. The active-balun-DLNA adopts an active balun to convert single-ended signals into differential signals and features a differential amplifier topology with neutralized bootstrapped cascode (NBCS) feedback to achieve low noise figure and high linearity. The proposed balun-DLNA achieves a minimum NF of 2.2 dB, a maximum differential gain of 18.9 dB, an input matching better than -8 dB, a gain difference of less 0.5 dB and a phase difference of 2° over the frequency range of 18 to 24 GHz, which demonstrates well balanced characteristics. At 22GHz, the simulated input third-order intercept point and 1-dB input compression point are -5.8 dBm and -14 dBm, respectively.

articleTitle: An SISL Dual-Polarized Broadband High-Gain Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: A differential-fed dual-polarized antenna based on substrate-integrated suspended line technology is proposed for millimeter-wave base stations. The proposed antenna design is based on all low-cost FR4 substrate layers with embedded air cavities for self-encapsulation. A differential feeding structure is used to improve port isolation and cross-polarization discrimination (XPD). The combination of a cross-shaped structure and slots excites different modes to achieve a wide bandwidth. The gain is further enhanced by stacking patches. The simulated results indicate that the maximum gain from 21.6 to 31.4 GHz is 13.3 dBi. Port isolation is better than 40 dB, and XPD is better than 35 dB. The proposed antenna has the advantages of low cost, wide bandwidth, high realized gain, good cross-polarization resolution, and high port isolation.

articleTitle: A 2 MHz High Stability On-Chip Relaxation Oscillator with a 2.5-5.5-V Voltage Supply
abstract: This paper proposes a high stability on-chip RC relaxation oscillator. A voltage average feedback technique is employed to mitigate the impact of comparator delay and a reference circuit is used to achieve high stability frequency over a wide power supply voltage and temperature range. Considering manufacturing process variations, a digital trimming circuit is used to obtain better accuracy. Designed in a 180-CMOS process, the target frequency of the proposed oscillator is 2 MHz. The frequency deviation is 0.516% over a supply range of 2.5 to 5.5V and 0.321% for temperature across -40℃ to 125℃.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Phased Array Antenna with Endfire Radiation for Millimeter-Wave Mobile Terminals
abstract: In this article, a millimeter-wave (mmWave) dual linear polarized phased array antenna (PAA) with endfire radiation pattern is proposed for mobile terminal applications. In order to achieve a high integration, the dual-polarized radiators are designed in the same region. With the special arrangement of radiation patches and the dual-mode feeding, the final resultant currents can generate vertical Polarization (VP) and horizontal Polarization (HP), respectively. Then, based on the element, a 1×4-element PAA is designed with a suitable element spacing. Finally, the proposed DP PAA covers a wide overlapped bandwidth of 24.25 GHz to 29 GHz, as well as achieves a 3-dB scanning range of ±58° (HP) / ±70° (VP). The proposed design approach offers a promising solution to achieve high-performance DP PAA for millimeter-wave communication systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Substrate-Integrated Low Passive-Intermodulation Waveguide Flange Adapter
abstract: To solve the passive intermodulation (PIM) problem of waveguide flange (WF) caused by metallic contact nonlinearity, a compact dielectric-gapped waveguide flange adapter (WFA) is proposed. The WFA consists of three substrate layers, the middle layer with symmetric mushroom-type EBG structure and the dielectric layers covering on its sides. When the WFA is inserted into traditional WF, a wide band gap is formed to suppress EM wave leakage outside from the dielectric gaps. Meanwhile, the dielectric layers avoid the metallic contact between the WF, resulting in a significant PIM suppression. A Ku-band prototype of the WFA is designed, good wideband EM transmission performance is obtained, and the PIM level of traditional WF is significantly improved by the WFA, with a maximum improvement of about 40dB and an average improvement better than 25dB.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis and Experimental Validation of Enhancing Doherty Amplifier Gain via Asymmetrical Input Power Splitting
abstract: This paper proposes a method to enhance the gain of the Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) by using an asymmetrical input power splitting that delivers the majority of input power to the main branch. It starts with an in-depth analysis that identifies the positive effects of the non-linear characteristics of the transistor transconductance and input capacitance on building proper drain current profiles required for Doherty operation. Subsequently, a DPA prototype is simulated to point out the possibility of improving the DPA gain by allocating more input power to the main transistor while maintaining good DPA efficiency. The presented theory is then validated by a 25-26.5 GHz DPA designed using the proposed asymmetrical power splitting. Measurement results indicate that the fabricated one-stage mil-limeter-wave DPA can achieve an enhanced gain of 7.5-8.4 dB and a good Doherty behavior with saturation and 6 dB power-added efficiency of 33.7-37.4% and 29.1-32.2%, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of High-Efficiency Radio-Frequency Rectifiers
abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) rectifiers are key blocks in an energy harvesting system that harvests the energy from EM radiation. There are multiple design challenges in RF rectifiers. This paper briefs the background and motivation, and reviews three design examples to address the challenges, on how to extend the input power range with high efficiency, to extend the incident angle of the input energy with high efficiency, and to reduce the power loss of an integrated rectifier.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Power Management Chip with 125mV On-Chip Cold startup achieving 91% efficiency for Thermoelectric Energy Harvesting
abstract: A Power management chip with a 125mV start-up and high efficiency for a Thermoelectrical energy generator (TEG) is presented in this paper. The implemented chip in the 180 nm BCD (Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) technology process achieves a peak efficiency of 91%. In the startup circuit, the clock can be generated by a ring oscillator architecture using the stacked inverter, and the supply voltage of the ring oscillator can operate as low as 80 mV. In addition to the ring oscillator, there are voltage detectors, charge-pump stages, boost converter, and LDO. The 6-phase bulk-cmos charge pumps (CPs) using gate voltage boosting technique eliminate the reversion loss. To achieve higher end-to-end efficiency and maximum power point tracking (MPPT), a switch frequency calibration-based TEG voltage control scheme to reduce power consumption is proposed. The output voltage of 1.8 V and 1.6V can be generated by the energy harvesting system without LDO and with LDO.

articleTitle: System-level Verification of 0.007-λ-Thickness Wideband Microstrip Antenna for Cellphone Applications
abstract: This paper proposes a system-level verification method for an ultrathin mobile antenna with a thickness of only 0.4 mm (0.007 λ, λ refers to the wavelength in vacuum at the center frequency). Unlike the regular measurement for the antenna’s parameters, the proposed method can conveniently verify the communication performance without struggling to integrate the antenna with the feed port within the cellphone. The experimental results show that both the channel capacity and bit error rate (BER) of the ultrathin antenna reach the same level as the reference WiFi-6 antenna in the cellphone, proving the feasibility of deploying planar ultrathin microstrip antennas in cellphones. The proposed method can be also extended for various antennas by properly adjusting the parameters of the link, contributing a general strategy for the antenna measurement at the system level.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized S-band Low Passive Intermodulation Waveguide Flange
abstract: Waveguide flange is a typical microwave connection structure with passive intermodulation (PIM) problem, which is caused by the non-ideal metallic contact of flange surface. Contactless flange provides a new way to make low PIM flange connection, but its size is too large for low frequency applications. To solve this problem, a miniaturized low PIM flange is proposed for S-band applications in this work, where the electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure of metal dielectric composite is innovatively adopted to avoid the metallic electrical contact of wave-guide flange, while the size is dramatically reduced by more than 60%. An S-band prototype of the proposed flange is designed and manufactured, and the experimental results show good S-parameter performance with a significant low PIM level, which is close to the residual PIM level of measurement system with the difference less than 2dB.

articleTitle: Design of a W-band Substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) mixer with Ka-band intermediate frequency
abstract: A W-band mixer based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is proposed in this paper. This mixer is featured with planar structure and Ka-band intermediate frequency (IF). The mixer consists of a SIW diplexer for local oscillator (LO) signal and IF signal, and a SIW filter for radio frequency (RF) signal, a Schottky diode and two matching lines. The mixer is optimized by manipulating the frequency response of the diplexer and length of the matching lines. The measured down conversion loss is less than 9.5 dB with 31-41 GHz IF and 58 GHz LO, while the conversion loss is under 10 dB with 89.2-99.2 GHz RF and 36 GHz IF.

articleTitle: Compact Broadband Dual-Polarized Antenna Based on Hybrid Radiation Modes and Its Application to Wide-Angle Scanning Array
abstract: The work presents a new wideband ±45° dualpolarized antenna for Internet of things (IoT) applications, which consists of a radiator with hybrid operating modes, two feeding baluns and a reflector. A cross-shaped microstrip radiator printed on a planar substrate acts as a half-wavelength dipole, and is etched with a full-wavelength slot. Four T-shaped microstrip stubs are loaded symmetrically around the main radiator. The main novelty is that a broad bandwidth is achieved by simultaneously exciting the half-wavelength dipole mode and the full-wavelength slot mode. Furthermore, a broadband array is completed by interleaving 6 proposed antenna elements. 3-dB beam scanning angle of over ±45° is achieved in the broad operating bandwidth. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed antenna features a broad operating bandwidth from 1.40 to 2.77 GHz (65.7%).

articleTitle: Wideband antenna with one split for 5G metal frame mobile phones and its application for games
abstract: In this paper, a wideband antenna is proposed and analyzed. The ground clearance is only 0.5mm and the total length is 48mm. The proposed antenna can cover the band of 700-960MHz, 1710-2690MHz and 3.3-3.8GHz with only one split, the simulation efficiencies are about -10~-5.5dB at 700-960MHz, - 5.5~-2.6dB at 1710-2690MHz and at -7~-2.2dB at 3.3-3.8GHz, and the proposed antenna have a good gaming experience at 1710-2690MHz.

articleTitle: A Simple Dual-Band Coupler Design Based on A Novel Dual-Mode Transmission Line Structure
abstract: A simple dual-band coupler design method based on a novel type of dual-mode transmission line is presented. The electric field distributions of different modes of the transmission line are studied, based on which the feasibility of the dual-band joint design method is explained. In particular, the phase and impedance conditions of the coupler are analyzed, and related parameters can be controlled to meet the design requirements of the dual-band coupler. In addition, a slow-wave structure is used to control the frequency ratio more flexibly. A dual-band coupler example centered at 22 and 30 GHz is designed and demonstrated as a proof of concept. The simulated results show satisfactory matching performance and phase imbalance in both bands.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Profile Multi-Element Patch Antenna Array Based on Dual-Layer Weak Resonant Decoupling Surfaces
abstract: A novel decoupling method for multi-element MIMO antennas is proposed in this paper. Based on the array-decoupling surface (ADS), the method introduces the Egyptian Axe structure and constructs dual-layer resonant decoupling surfaces which effectively complement the amplitude and phase of the reflected waves. Simulated results demonstrate that across the N41 band (2.515–2.675 GHz), a two-element microstrip antenna achieves isolation exceeding 18 dB under matching conditions better than -10 dB, with total efficiency higher than 88%. For a quad-element array, two decoupling structures are designed, both capable of achieving coupling suppression with a profile height as low as 0.13λ₀, almost halved compared with the existing methods.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Compact 78.5-to-96.5 GHz Power Amplifier with 14.5 dBm PSAT and 20.5% PAE in 65nm Bulk CMOS
abstract: The paper presents a broadband E/W-band three-stage power amplifier (PA) with high efficiency in 65-nm CMOS technology. Customized neutralization capacitors are used to enhance the gain and stability of the PA. Transformers, coupling lines, and ground planes are co-designed to minimize the insertion loss and circuit areas of passive components, thereby enhancing the gain, output power, and PA efficiency. The measured prototype features a peak gain of 24.6 dB under a 1V power supply, with a 3dB bandwidth from 78.5 to 96.5 GHz. At 85 GHz, the PA provides a saturated output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SAT</inf>) of 14.5 dBm and a power-added efficiency (PAE) of 20.5%. The core area of the PA is only 0.05 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, achieving a compact layout.
