articleTitle: Miniaturized and High-Selective Filtering Power Divider Based on GaAs IPD Technology for 5G N77 Applications
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized N77 filtering power divider (FPD) is designed on a GaAs substrate based on the integrated passive device (IPD) fabrication process, which exhibits good out-of-band rejection characteristics. It achieves a third-order bandpass frequency response, with transmission zeros (TZs) on both sides of the passband of 0.4 GHz and 3.4 GHz, respectively. In addition, the parasitic capacitance of inductors is applied to generate TZ at higher frequencies. The bandpass response has a center frequency of 3.51 GHz and a bandwidth of about 71.5 %. The isolation between the two output ports is better than -12 dB. The minimum insertion loss is 0.68 dB, and the isolation is better than -16 dB. Moreover, the chip area is only 1.15 mm × 1.25 mm. Simulation and measured results show that the proposed FPD can achieve equal power distribution with wide bandwidth, high isolation, low insertion loss, and miniaturization. The TZs effectively improve the roll-off coefficient and out-of-band rejection in the passband, and improve the performance of out-of-band filtering and selection.

articleTitle: A 2-20 GHz Low-Noise Gallium Nitride MMIC Amplifier
abstract: In this paper, a monolithic two-stage 2- 20 GHz ultra-wideband low-noise amplifier (LNA) based on 0.1 μm GaN HEMT on Si substrate is proposed. This amplifier is designed based on the stacked structure to obtain a flat high gain and low noise performance. The first stage stacked-FET is considered to minimize the noise figure and second stage is to enhance the linearity performance. The LNA is biased at a gate voltage of −1.3 V and a drain voltage of 5 V, with a quiescent current of 75 mA. It has a gain greater than 20 dB, less than -11 dB for S11, less than -9 dB for S22, less than 2.2 dB for noise figure, larger than 18 dBm for output 1 dB compression point and 30 dBm for output third-order intercept point within the frequency range of 2-20 GHz. The chip size is 2.7 mm × 0.6 mm.

articleTitle: Optimal Shifting Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface aided Physical-Layer Key Generation in Static Environments
abstract: This paper presents an optimal shifting scheme using reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to aid physicallayer key generation (PKG) and enhance communication and key generation rate (KGR) in static environments. Our approach involves designing a protocol for RIS-aided key generation and optimizing RIS coefficients to introduce phase randomization in the wireless channel while maximizing power reception. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed protocol in improving both communication performance and KGR under static conditions.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Dual-Band Dual-Port Microstrip Patch Antenna Covering Wi-Fi 6 Bands
abstract: In 5G mobile terminals, the limited space to accommodate multiple antennas makes planar antennas which can be placed on the back cover a hotspot recently. This paper proposes a dual-port dual-band half-mode patch with low profile and compact size for WLAN system. By elaborately selecting the patch size and feeding position and resorting to lumped components for impedance matching, the first two modes of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,0</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,1</inf> are utilized for Wi-Fi 6 band coverage (2.40-2.50 GHz and 5.15-5.85 GHz). The proposed shorted patch with the dimensions of 27.2×26.5×1.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> $\left( {0.21 \times 0.21 \times 0.012{{{\lambda }}_{\text{L}}}^3} \right)$ achieves the -6 dB impedance bandwidths of 2.36-2.64 GHz and 5.09-5.88 GHz, and the isolation can be up to 36 dB. The size of the proposed antenna is smaller in contrast to the majority of the reported Wi-Fi antennas. It is an ideal candidate for modern mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Horizontally Polarized Antenna with Pattern Reconfigurability
abstract: A novel omnidirectional, horizontally polarized antenna with the pattern reconfigurability is presented for modern ceiling routers. Horizontally polarized omnidirectional radiation is achieved using a rotational dipole array. A reflector is placed below the dipole array to reduce back radiation. A reconfigurable parasitic structure is designed, allowing the antenna to switch omnidirectional beams with varied elevation angles. Additionally, a tunable matching network allows for impedance matching across different states. Measurements indicate the overlapped −10dB impedance bandwidth across different states is 100 MHz (2.53-2.63GHz). The high and low-elevation patterns yield gains of 5.7 dBi and 7.2 dBi, with variations less than 2.5 and 1.6 dBi in the θ section, respectively.

articleTitle: A miniaturised Ka-band input DR channel filter for multiplexer
abstract: This paper presents a novel channel filter for Ka-band multiplexers designed using a dielectric approach. The filter utilizes the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> mode of dielectric resonators, offering excellent single-mode operating bandwidth and Q factor(>7000). The transfer function utilizes a 10-pole pseudo-elliptic with four transmission zeros and four equalization zeros, providing a sharp out-of-band rejection while maintaining a flat in-band transmission characteristic and excellent group delay performance. A special resonator coupling structure is designed, incorporating intricate electrical and structural design to effectively control parasitic coupling within the filter, allowing for a continuous adjustable coupling amount. The vertical installation design helps to reduce the floor space required for installation, making it more suitable for onboard applications.

articleTitle: A 115-140GHz Power Amplifier With High Output Power in SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: This paper presents a power amplifier (PA) operating in the frequency range of 115-140 GHz, implemented using a 0.13 μm germanium-silicon (SiGe) BiCMOS process. The single stage amplifier employs a cascode structure and integrates gmboosting technology to enhance gain. To ensure superior broadband performance at high frequencies, input and output matching are achieved through the utilization of a Marchand balun. The PA operates from 115 GHz to 140 GHz (3dB bandwidth) with a peak gain of 23.7 dB at 130GHz. At 116 GHz, the amplifier achieves a saturated output power of 16.2 dBm, with the peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 10.2%. The total chip size is 0.92×0.73 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Novel Sideband Gain Suppression High-Efficiency Power Amplifier MMIC in Ka-Band
abstract: The design and performance of a Ka-band high-efficiency power amplifier MMIC with sideband gain suppression is presented. The three-stage amplifier chip is fabricated using 0.15 μm GaAs pHEMT technology. The output matching network contains a novel resonance circuit, which is realized by connecting the drain bias microstrip in parallel with a series capacitor and two microstrips to achieve a sideband gain suppression. The formula of the sideband resonance frequency is derived from mathematical calculations with the transformation method of equivalent capacitances and inductance. A second-harmonic control circuit at the input of the third-stage transistor is used to improve the power-added efficiency (PAE). The measured output power is 20.8-21.2 dBm and PAE of 39.1-43.5% under continuous wave conditions in the 25-27 GHz band. The chip size is 2.2×1.0mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Broadband Programmable Gain Amplifier with Accurate dB-Linear Characteristic Adopting Active Feedback Architecture
abstract: Based on an active feedback circuit and binary-weighted switching technology, a novel programmable gain amplifier (PGA) circuit is presented in this paper to achieve extensive gain dynamic range, high precision decibel (dB)-linearity, better in-band flatness, and broadband performance. The circuit structure includes a precision fine-tuned gain stage and two modified coarse-tuned gain stages. DC offset cancellation (DCOC) circuits are integrated into the design to suppress DC-level shifts effectively. Operating at a supply voltage of 1.8 V, the circuit demonstrates a power consumption of 3.87 mW. Fabricated using a 130-nm silicon-on-insulator (SOI) process, the circuit has a core area of 0.048 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It has a gain range from -10.75 to 39.16 dB, with a precise gain step of 2 dB. Additionally, it features a minimum -3 dB bandwidth of 340 MHz.

articleTitle: A Grating Lobe Suppression Method for Sparse Antenna Arrays in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: This article proposes a three-dimensional grating lobe suppression method used in the sparse antenna arrays for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms to address the problem of grating lobes. When the UAV swarm antenna array is deployed, the large distance between antenna elements due to the size limitation of UAVs leads to the appearance of grating lobes. This article proposes a three-dimensional antenna array for UAV swarms, which introduces new degrees of freedom in three-dimensional space to increase the density of the antenna array in the target direction, effectively avoiding the generation of grating lobes. By deploying a three-layer antenna array with a spacing of 1.5λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in space and adjusting the phase between the layers, the generation of grating lobes is successfully suppressed, and the sidelobe level at the corresponding position is below -13 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Bandpass Filters by Employing Independently Controllable Dual-Mode Patch Resonators
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-band bandpass filters (BPFs) with the use of short-ended dual-mode patch resonators. The dual-mode resonators offer the advantage of individually adjustable resonant frequencies and minimized size. These advantages enable the design of dual-band BPFs with fully controllable bandwidth and compact footprint. To demonstrate these novel resonators, we conduct a detailed study to investigate their resonant frequencies and the adjustment mechanism of resonant frequencies. Additionally, we performed a theoretical synthesis procedure for the proposed BPFs and obtain key design parameters to realize the filters. Finally, we validate the feasibility of the design and the advantages of filters based on the substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) platform through simulations and measurements on the designed BPFs.

articleTitle: Waveform Investigation of Base Harmonic Injection for High Efficiency HBT Device
abstract: An active load pull waveform measurement system has been utilized to investigate the benefits of base harmonic matching on a Gallium Arsenide(GaAs) Hetero-junction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) device. Theoretical and experimental investigations are carried out to find out the role of source harmonic matching in power amplifier's high efficiency operating modes. The second harmonic injection experiment on a real device at 2.6GHz leads to a 4.2% improvement in PAE, a 0.7 dB gain enhancement, and improved linearity.

articleTitle: An Efficient Transistor Modelling Method using Convolutional Neural Network with Transfer Learning
abstract: In this paper, an efficient CNN model with transfer learning ability is developed for predicting the nonlinear behavior of transistors under large signal stimuli. The CNN consists of multiple hierarchical layers where different levels capture different nonlinear relationships. Meanwhile, we propose fine-tuning neural layers to minimize the number of measurement data under varying operational conditions of transistors. A 0.25 um GaN HEMT transistor was selected as the device under test for this experiment. Using the proposed transfer learning based method, only 30% of the conventional measurement data is needed to achieve a normalized mean squared error (NMSE) below -40 dB. This proposed approach provides a practical solution for efficient transistor behavioral models.

articleTitle: A 3–6 GHz High-precision 6-bits Phase Shifter in 0.5-μm GaAs pHEMT Technology
abstract: A 3–6 GHz high-precision 6-bits phase shifter (PS) based on a 0.5-μm GaAs pHEMT technology is presented. The PS incorporates a switched L/C structure, a bridge T-type structure, and an enhanced high-pass/low-pass structure, achieving optimal performance by arranging units with better and worse return loss(RL) alternately. Besides, the bridge T-type structure uses the transistor's turn-off capacitor instead of a standard one, reducing the number of components and achieving a compact 1.3mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> chip size. The PS achieves high phase resolution with a step of 5.625°, an RMS PS error of less than 3.77°, an RMS insertion loss(IL) error of less than 0.46 dB, and an IL of less than 6.5 dB .

articleTitle: A High-Isolated Inverted-F Antenna Pair for In-Band Full-Duplex Applications
abstract: In this paper, a high-isolated inverted-F antenna (IFA) pair is proposed for in-band full-duplex (IBFD) applications. By introducing a capacitive ground cut that can effectively manipulate the ground currents, a standing null area at two frequencies appears simultaneously when one IFA is excited. Therefore, high isolation can be achieved with two transmission zeros by placing another IFA in the standing null area. The results show that the isolation is obtained with 10.2 % fractional bandwidth for 40 dB isolation and 6.1 % for 50 dB isolation while the impedance matching is better than -10 dB. Moreover, the simulated total efficiency is higher than 90.3% with the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) lower than 0.00023. In addition, the size of the capacitive ground cut is only about 0.05 × 0.06λ.

articleTitle: A Fully Digital RF Signal Generation Scheme for Low-Cost GNSS Signal Generator
abstract: This paper presents a fully digital radio frequency (RF) signal generation scheme for global navigation satellite system (GNSS) spread-spectrum transmitters which is based only on digital logic and passive structures. Compared to conventional radio transmitters, the proposed signal generation scheme eliminates the local oscillator (LO) and the mixer and adopts highorder Nyquist zone subsampling and high-pass Δ-Σ modulation techniques to greatly simplify the frontend design to generate the spread spectrum signal. The high-order Nyquist zone technique converts the DAC samples to RF without active devices, and the high-pass Δ-Σ modulator generates a 1-bit bitstream within limited logic resources. Due to the extremely lean architecture, the entire system contains only 2 active and 3 passive devices, which is fairly low-cost and ready for mass deployment.

articleTitle: A 0.5-6 GHz Ultra-Wideband Bidirectional Amplification and Digital Controlled Attenuation Integrated Multifunctional Chip based on 0.5μm GaAs P-HEMT Process
abstract: Based on the GaAs 0.5μm pHMET process, a 0.5-6 GHz ultra-wideband amplification and attenuation multifunctional chip was developed in this paper. For the amplification unit, a Darlington-Cascode circuit structure was employed to design the transmission amplifier, while a first-stage common-source LNA structure was adopted in the reception channel. A three-stage inverted-П type structure driven by TLL driver was employed for the digital attenuation unit. The size of the fabricated chip is 3.5×2.7×0.1mm. In the frequency range of 0.5 to 6 GHz, the chip presents a gain of 7.5dB, a P-1dB of more than 8dBm, and a noise coefficient of 4.5dB for the transmission side; meanwhile, it presents a gain of 20dB, a P-1dB of more than 16.5dBm, and a noise coefficient of 3dB for the reception side. Furthermore, the chip presents a good attenuation accuracy as less than 0.5dB at 5dB, 10dB, and 20dB attenuation degree, respectively.

articleTitle: A 16V 3.3-3.6GHz GaN Doherty Power Amplifier Module for Next-Generation Satellite Communication Applications
abstract: The design of a 16V 3.3-3.6GHz 4W gallium nitride (GaN) Doherty power amplifier (DPA) is presented in this paper. To achieve an optimal performance, knee voltage reduction and current density enhancement techniques are employed to improve the efficiency and bandwidth characteristics of the GaN process at 16V. Furthermore, the two-stage cascading performance is optimized through active bandwidth enhancement technique. A gain of 28dB, a saturation power of 4W, and an efficiency greater than 46% at an average power of 28.5dBm are achieved in the design.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reshaping of Aperture-Sharing Metasurface-Based Wide-Beam Rectenna
abstract: An aperture-sharing metasurface-based wide-beam rectenna with radiation pattern reshaping for decomposed high TMxy mode is proposed. The critical contribution of this aperture-sharing metasurface-based rectenna is to reuse unit cells on the MTS layer to excite three modes by three ports simultaneously, thereby achieving a wide beam width. But the radiation pattern of the modes excited by side feed ports, decomposed in high TMxy mode, is with the sidelobe, affecting this rectenna’s energy harvesting ability. Hence, radiation pattern reshaping of decomposed high TMxy mode is studied in this paper. According to the working principle, two key factors, the size ratio between outer unit cells and inner unit cells and the size ratio between length and width of unit cells, are discovered that could affect the radiation pattern transformation of this high mode. The overall size of this proposed rectenna is λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.03 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Three excited modes operate at 2.45 GHz. By combining the direct current output from these three modes, this rectenna can achieve a beamwidth of 114° and a peak gain of 10.7 dBi.

articleTitle: A 220-GHz 20-Gbps Long-Distance Wireless Link Using a High-Gain Two-Dimensional Beam-Scanning Antenna
abstract: This paper presents a 220 GHz long-distance wireless link system, established using a set of fundamentally operated transmit (Tx) / receive (Rx) radio frequency (RF) frontend modules and the purpose-designed high-gain two-dimensional beam-scanning reflector antennas. The designed system has a maximum communication distance of over 2-km with a capability of fast link alignment. The antenna has a measured peak gain of 45.26 dBi at 218GHz and can cover a beam-scanning range of at least ±30° in both E- and H-planes. Using the quadrature phase-shift keying (QPSK) modulation, an experiment is carried out, and a data rate of 20 Gbps with an error vector magnitude of EVM < 31% is achieved at 212 GHz with 100-m distance.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Filtering Patch Antenna And Array For 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: In this letter, a novel filtering patch antenna and its array functioning in the millimeter wave frequency band is presented. The proposed antenna element features a rectangular patch fed with transmission line. By cutting four slots all around the radiating edges of the patch and loading the filtering structure, the filtering response is realized. What’s more, antenna element can be effectively applied to millimeter-wave array designs. The results of the simulation reveal out that the impedance bandwidth (S11<-10dB) are 21.6% and 19% for element and array, respectively, and the peak gain is 6.53 dB and 12.37dB. Furthermore, this design does not incorporate any extra filtering circuits and has three independently controllable radiation nulls distributed outside the passband.

articleTitle: A Wafer-Integrated Ultra-wideband Energy Selective Surface Design Method
abstract: In order to avoid the high intensity radiation field to enter the electronic information system working at an ultra-wideband, a wafer-integrated ultra-wideband energy selective surface is designed. The diode loaded on the wafer-integrated ESS is specially designed, which has a low junction capacitance of 30 fF and low conduction resistance of 30 ohm. The metal lines and the diodes on both the top layer and the bottom layer, which are arranged in a hexagonal honeycomb shape, grow on the sapphire substrate together. The top and the bottom layer is mirror symmetric about the middle layer whose material is F4B225. The ESS behaves like a lowpass filter with a 2 dB bandwidth covering 0 GHz to 18.62 GHz at the diode-off state, while provides an attenuation above 18 dB in the bandwidth of 0 GHz to 18.62 GHz at the diode-on state. The designed ESS has an excellent angle stability when the incident angle change within the range of 0 to 25 degrees.

articleTitle: A Compact Ka-band Asymmetric SPDT Switch in 0.15-μm GaN-on-SiC Technology for 5G Applications
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact Ka-band asymmetric single-pole double-throw (SPDT) transmit/receive (TRx) switch for 5G applications in a 0.15-μm GaN-on-SiC process. The inductive susceptance of the OFF-STATE branch is harnessed to create resonators, which are subsequently incorporated with coupled-resonators to achieve wideband bandpass transmission characteristics for TRx. In the RX branch, the parasitic parameters of the additional series switch device are leveraged to alternate the coupling parameters of the resonators between TX and RX modes, aiming to enhance the RX insertion loss (IL) and TX isolation (ISO) performance. The chip size is 0.9 × 1.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Measurement results show that, from 24 to 33 GHz, the proposed switch features an IL of less than 1.0 dB in TX mode, and less than 2.71 dB in RX mode. The measured TX-to-RX ISO is better than 17 dB in TX mode.

articleTitle: Design of a Directional Coupler with Independently Adjustable Power Divisions and Phase Differences
abstract: This paper presents a directional coupler with independently adjustable power divisions and phase differences. The proposed directional coupler is composed of a compact 90° coupler with tunable power divisions and two phase shifters with 360° phase ranges. From theoretical derivation, it can be inferred that by cascading the phase shifters separately at the input and output ports of the tunable 90° directional coupler, a directional coupler with independently adjustable power divisions and phase differences can be achieved. To prove the correctness of the theory, a directional coupler working at 3.5 GHz has been designed and fabricated. To achieve miniaturization, the tunable 90° directional coupler adopts coupled line structure, and the 360° phase shifters use the stub branched-line structure. As a result, the area of the whole coupler is 0.4 λ × 0.6 λ. The proposed directional coupler can reach a power division range from 1:8 to 8:1, and a phase difference range from 0 to 360°.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Design and Optimization of Complementary Split Ring Resonator Filters
abstract: Designing Complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) filters is a complex task due to the strong interaction between CSRR and resonators. Traditional methods struggle to maintain high selectivity and low insertion loss while accommodating wideband requirements. This study proposes a novel approach for CSRR filter design using a deep reinforcement learning-based method. This approach uses the ideal S-parameter curve as the optimization target and employs a deep Q-Network (DQN) based reinforcement learning framework. Furthermore, we utilize CST Studio, an electromagnetic simulation software, to optimize the CSRR filter design parameters. The final filter exhibits a passband frequency of 37.6GHz-50.6GHz, with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> in the passband less than -20dB and minimum insertion loss IL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf> less than -1.5dB. Experimental results demonstrate the method’s efficiency and scalability, providing a promising solution for efficient and accurate CSRR filter design.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Leaky Wave Antenna Based on SIW TE20 Mode
abstract: This paper presents a periodic leaky wave antenna (LWA) based on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) transmission line TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> mode with continuous beam scanning capability. Using the field distribution characteristics of the SIW TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> mode, directional radiation is achieved using a single longitudinal slot, and open stopband suppression is achieved by controlling the length-to-width ratio. To enhance the gain of the LWA, dual-longitudinal slots with in-phase radiation sources are employed. Similarly, open stopband suppression is achieved by controlling the length-to-width ratio. Finally, LWA 1 and LWA 2 are formed by cascading 10-unit cells. Simulation results demonstrate that both LWA 1 and LWA 2 achieve broadside radiation. LWA 2 exhibits higher gain compared to LWA 1. The proposed LWAs are suitable as a candidate for millimeter wave beam scanning system antennas.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna with Broadband for 5G Communication
abstract: A dual-band shared-aperture antenna, offering broadband coverage and efficient aperture reuse, is presented. In this design, an eight-element millimeter-wave (mmW) linear array is integrated into a microwave antenna, sharing the same radiation aperture. The low-frequency part of the antenna operates at the Sub-6 GHz band, featuring a novel integrated balanced double-layer printed dipole antenna with a center frequency of 3.5 GHz. The high-frequency part operates in the mmW band at 28 GHz, comprising an array of end-fire dipole antennas fed by a substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) network. The integration of these two antennas achieves a significantly high aperture reuse rate, with minimal impact on the radiation performance in each frequency band. Simulation results demonstrate that the system has stable radiation performances. The proposed dual-band antenna has a -10 dB operating bandwidth of 27.8% and 24.9% for the microwave band and mmW band, respectively. The peak gains are 7.49 dBi and 14.96 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Uncorrelated Phase Noise Cancellation for Low-IF Radar With Separate Reference Sources of Dual PLLs
abstract: This paper presents a low-IF dual-PLL radar architecture with two separate reference sources of two PLLs. Compared with the existing low-IF architectures, an additional mixer is used to generate an IF reference signal whose phase noise correlates to the received down-converted IF signal. These two IF signals can be combined destructively by tuning the phase and attenuation of the IF reference signal. Consequently, IF cancellation can be implemented. The phase noise can be significantly eliminated in the IF cancellation and improved SNR of the radar receiver can be obtained. Signal-noise model and experiment measurement are provided to illustrate the proposed concept.

articleTitle: An Eight-Beam Planar Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Broadband Dipoles
abstract: This letter proposes an eight-beam planar pattern reconfigurable antenna based on broadband dipoles. The antenna adopts a single-layer structure with a low profile. And it consists of four broadband dipoles and a reconfigurable feeding network which is composed of four microstrip lines with balun. By switching the ON/OFF states of four PIN diodes soldered onto the feeding network, the maximum radiation direction of the devised antenna is rotated at intervals of 45° in the azimuth plane. The simulation results indicate that the devised antenna can achieve an overlapping operating bandwidth of 32.7% (2.3–3.2 GHz) in eight states. The antenna has a stable gain performance, with a maximum gain of 5.5 dBi. These excellent performance characteristics make the antenna a promising candidate for WLAN applications in future wireless communications.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Bandpass Filter Using Hybrid Microstrip/SIDGS with Dual-Notched Band, Wide Stopband, and Low Radiation
abstract: In this paper, a dual-notched ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) using hybrid microstrip and substrate-integrated defected ground structure (SIDGS) with wide stopband and low radiation is proposed. Firstly, such a miniaturized broadside-coupled using microstrip T-stubs and SIDGS are introduced to achieve the UWB operation with low insertion loss and wide stopband. Secondly, two non-identical meander open-stubs are utilized to allocate the dual-notched bands. Thirdly, to further extend the upper stopband and suppress the radiation, the cascaded lowpass units (LPUs) and spur-lines are used. To verify the mechanism mentioned above, a prototype UWB bandpass filter with dual-notched bands (i.e., 5.35 and 5.92 GHz) is proposed and fabricated. Good agreement between the measured and simulated results are achieved, which exhibits merits of 0.53 dB insertion loss, 26 dB rejection level up to 50 GHz, and 2.7 dB maximum radiation loss.

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligence Near-Field Probe Calibration Method Based on Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: The near field scanning method specified in the international standard IEC-61967 is an important international diagnostic method for detecting electromagnetic compatibility problems. The near-field probe, as an important part of near-field scanning, mainly detects the magnetic field or electric field. The measurement accuracy of the near field probe directly affects the measurement accuracy of the electromagnetic field on the surface of the device, affecting the accuracy of electromagnetic compatibility diagnostics. To ensure measurement accuracy, it is essential to carry out near-field probe calibration. In this work, we proposed an artificial intelligence probe calibration method based on the generative adversarial networks, which helps improve the difference of calibration parts’ quality difference measurement field and eliminate the unnecessary influence field on the probe performance. Based on the proposed method, we effectively calibrate two kinds of electric field probes, which overcomes the problem of the difference of calibration parts’ quality difference measurement field, and eliminate the influence of unnecessary field to the probe performance.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Phase-Reconfigurable Equivalent Magnetic Dipole Element Applied to Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit phase-reconfigurable aperture coupled equivalent magnetic dipole element operating at the Cband is proposed. The element contains a symmetrical feeding network and an equivalent magnetic dipole placed on the ground. By utilizing two PIN diodes, various feeding paths can be selectively activated to achieve a 1-bit reconfigurable phase shift (0°/180°). Simulated results show that the half-power beam-width (HPBW) of the E-plane and H-plane at 5.8 GHz are 155° and 100° under radiation boundary conditions, respectively. The element has the advantages of compact structure, wide beam and reconfiguration, which has certain application prospects in wide-angle scanning phased array.

articleTitle: Miniaturized WIFI Bandpass Filter based on Spiral Stepped Impedance Resonator with Multiple Transmission Zeros
abstract: In this paper, a novel spiral stepped impedance resonator (SSIR) is proposed, which has a double-layer structure, It features the advantage of miniaturization, and distributes the electric and magnetic fields of the resonator in different layers of the dielectric substrate. Based on the proposed resonator, a bandpass filter (BPF) with excellent performance is realized for Wi-Fi application. The hybrid coupling between the two resonators can be easily realized and flexibly controlled. In addition, six transmission zeros are introduced into the filter due to the special layout of the spiral high impedance line, thus the designed filter achieves high out-of-band rejection level. A fourth-order bandpass filter is then designed based on the same resonator, and the cascade characteristics of the resonator are verified in EM simulation. To demonstrate the mechanism, a second-order bandpass filter is implemented and tested with a core size of only 9.9 mm×15.3 mm (i.e., 0.12λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>×0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>), a measured center frequency of 2.5 GHz, a relative bandwidth of 18%, an in-band insertion loss of only 0.43 dB and a stopband range of 4.9f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (with a stopband suppression of more than 30 dB).

articleTitle: Linearity-Enhanced GaN Power Amplifier with Dual-Transistor Compensation Strategy
abstract: In this article, a parallel dual-transistor architecture with different bias voltage is proposed to compensate the soft gain compression (AM-AM distortion) and phase shift (AMPM distortion) behaviors in GaN power amplifiers (PAs). The compressive and expanding nonlinear curves of the transistor's large signal transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) and input capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</inf>) are combined to achieve flat total g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</inf> over a wide output power range. As a proof-of-concept prototype, a 3.5 GHz PA using commercial GaN HEMTs is fabricated, powered by a 48V power supply, achieving 41.25–41.89 dBm output power 3-dB compression point (OP3-dB), 57.8–63.1% power added efficiency (PAE) and 17.3-20.4 dB power gain over n78 band. Within the operating frequency range, the output power back-off within the range of 20 dBm, AM-AM distortion is less than 1 dB, and AMPM distortion is less than 2 deg.

articleTitle: Design of Metamaterial Using Split-Ring Resonators for Efficiency Enhancement of Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: A metamaterial (MTM) with negative effective permeability has been proposed used as an intermediate power focusing element in a wireless power transmission (WPT) network. Split ring resonators with a 0.4 mm thickness have been formed on FR4 substrate for the MTM. The proposed MTM was modelled and simulated using CST Studio Suite with the effective permeability educed from its S-parameters. The real part of effective relative permeability is µ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>=-3.47 at 432 MHz. By applying the proposed MTM to a WPT link, an improvement in power transfer efficiency (PTE) and magnetic field distribution can be achieved. When the overall distance between the transmitter and receiver is 40 mm, the PTE improves from 0.25% to 72.25% at the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Critical Area Identification of Sea Target Using Passive Millimeter-Wave Imaging
abstract: Passive millimeter-wave (PMMW) imaging has effective maritime monitoring capabilities under adverse weather conditions. The existing research mainly focuses on the detection of the whole target. However, when the detector is close to the target, we need to identify the critical areas of the target. There is no work to address this problem. In this paper, we propose a physical-based identification method that identifies critical areas of ships. The method first adjusts the brightness temperature threshold to differentiate between the sea surface and the ship's body and enhances the continuity of target areas through morphological operations after analyzing the brightness temperature distribution at close range. Subsequently, critical areas are calibrated by identifying the active jamming area and the area of the ship's fuel tanks are located. Edge detection techniques are further employed to optimize the recognition of these critical areas, ensuring accurate focus on critical areas of ships. Through simulation and experimental verifications, our study ensures the accuracy of critical area identification in complex marine environments and provides adequate methodological support for developing ship automatic identification and tracking systems. The application of this method strengthens monitoring capabilities under adverse visual conditions and demonstrates the potential of PMMW imaging technology in maritime security domains.
